The derivative of $\psi_n^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\psi_{\ell-1}^{-1}$ maps $E^u_\ell$ to $E^u_n$, and contracts vectors in $E^u_\ell$ by a factor of $1/(\lambda^u_n\cdots\lambda^u_{\ell-1})$. Therefore $W$ is an  $E^u_n$-segment with length $\ell^u(a_\ell)/(\lambda^u_n\cdots\lambda^u_{\ell-1})$. Since $W\subset C$, $\ell^u(C)\geq \ell^u(a_\ell)/(\lambda^u_n\cdots\lambda^u_{\ell-1})$. On the other hand, $(\psi_{\ell-1}\circ\cdots\circ\psi_n)(C)\subset a_\ell$, so  $\ell^u(C)\lambda^u_n\cdots\lambda^u_{\ell-1}\leq \ell^u(a_\ell)$. Necessarily, 
$
\ell^u(C)=\ell^u(a_\ell)/(\lambda^u_n\cdots\lambda^u_{\ell-1})
$

                                                 
   
                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                       

Now consider a general cylinder $C=\<a_{n-k},\ldots,\dot{a}_n,\ldots,a_{n+m}\>$. By \eqref{e.cylinder-shift}, 
$$
C=(\psi_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\psi_{n-k})(C'),\textrm{ where }C':=\<\dot{a}_{n-k},\ldots,a_{n+m}\>. 
$$ 
The differential of  $\psi_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\psi_{n-k}$ maps  $E^t_{n-k}$ to $E^t_n$ $(t=u,s)$. It contracts $E^u_{n-k}$ by  $\lambda^s_{n-k}\cdots\lambda^s_{n-1}$, and  expands $E^s_{n-k}$ by $\lambda^u_{n-k}\cdots\lambda^u_{n-1}$. Thus $C$ is a $(E^u_n,E^s_n)$-parallelogram, and by the discussion above, $\ell^s(C)=\lambda^s_{n-k}\cdots\lambda^s_{n-1}\ell^s(C')=\ell^s(a_{n-k})\lambda^s_{n-k}\cdots\lambda^s_{n-1}$, and 
$\ell^u(C)=\lambda^u_{n-k}\cdots\lambda^u_{n-1}\ell^u(C')=\ell^u(a_{n+m})/(\lambda^u_{n}\cdots\lambda^u_{n+m-1})$. 

Thus $\displaystyle \mu_0(C)=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Area}(C)=\frac{1}{2}\ell^s(a_{n-k})\ell^u(a_{n+m})|\sin\measuredangle(E^s_{n},E^u_{n})|
\frac{\lambda^s_{n-k}\cdots\lambda^s_{n-1}}{\lambda^u_{n}\cdots\lambda^u_{n+m-1}}$.

Lemma \ref{Lemma-Partition}(10) gives uniform bounds on $\ell^s(a_{n-k}),\ell^u(a_{n+m})$. Proposition \ref{Prop-Contracting-Automorphisms}(2) gives  uniform bounds on $|\sin\measuredangle(E^s_{n},E^u_{n})|$,  and  Proposition \ref{Prop-Contracting-Automorphisms}(3) gives uniform bounds on $\lambda^s_i, \lambda^u_j$. It follows that $\mu_0(C)\asymp 1$ with bounds depending only on $k+m$.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{Prop-Markov-Kernel} 
If $\omega$ is chosen randomly uniformly in 
${\mathsf{St}}_0$, then:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item  $X_i^{(n)}\in\mathfrak P_i$  for all $i\geq 0$.
\item  $\displaystyle {\mathbb{P}}(X_0^{(n)}=a_0,\ldots,X_\ell^{(n)}=a_\ell)=\mu_0(a_0)\prod_{i=0}^{\ell-1} \frac{\ell^u(a_{i+1})t_{a_i,a_{i+1}}^{(i)}}{\lambda_{i}^u\ell^u(a_{i})}.$
\item $(X^{(n)}_i)_{i\geq 0}$ is equal in distribution to an inhomogeneous Markov chain $(X_i)_{i\geq 0}$ with
\begin{enumerate}
\item $i$-th state space $\mathfrak P_i$;
\item initial probability vector $\pi_a:={\mathbb{P}}[X_0=a]=\mu_0(a)$ $(a\in \mathfrak P_0)$;
\item $i$-th transition kernel $\displaystyle\pi_{i,i+1}(a_i,a_{i+1}):={\mathbb{P}}[X_{i+1}=a_{i+1}|X_i=a_i]=\frac{\ell^u(a_{i+1})}{\lambda_i^u\ell^u(a_i)}t_{a_i,a_{i+1}}^{(i)}$.
\end{enumerate}
\item $\pi_a$  are positive and uniformly bounded away from zero by constants which only on $M(\beta)$  in \eqref{e.M-beta}, and $\pi_{i,i+1}(a_i,a_{i+1})$ are either zero or uniformly bounded away from zero by constants which depend only on $M(\beta)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Part (1) holds by definition.

Suppose $\ell\geq n$. 
If we sample $\omega$ randomly uniformly in ${\mathsf{St}}_0$, then 
\begin{align*}
&{\mathbb{P}}(X_0^{(n)}=a_0,\ldots,X_\ell^{(n)}=a_\ell)=\mu_0[\<a_0,\ldots,\dot{a}_n,\ldots,a_\ell\>]\\
&=\frac{1}{2} \ell^s(a_0)\ell^u(a_\ell)|\sin\measuredangle(E^s_n,E^u_n)|\frac{\lambda^s_{0}\cdots\lambda^s_{n-1}}{\lambda^u_n\cdots \lambda^u_{\ell-1}}\prod_{i=0}^{\ell-1}t_{a_i,a_{i+1}}^{(i)}, \textrm{ see  Lemmas \ref{Lemma-Cylinders} and \ref{Lemma-Cylinder-Area}}.
\end{align*}
The automorphism  $\psi_{0}^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\psi_{n-1}^{-1}$ maps the parallelogram with unit sides parallel to $E^s_n,E^u_n$, to a parallelogram with (perpendicular) sides parallel to  $E^s_0,E^u_0$, and with lengths $1/(\lambda^s_0\cdots\lambda^s_{n-1})$, $1/(\lambda^u_0\cdots\lambda^u_{n-1})$. Since the Jacobian is one, the area remains unchanged, whence 
$
|\sin\measuredangle(E^s_n,E^u_n)|=1/(\lambda^s_0\cdots\lambda^s_{n-1}\cdot\lambda^u_0\cdots\lambda^u_{n-1})
$.  Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
&{\mathbb{P}}(X_0^{(n)}=a_0,\ldots,X_\ell^{(n)}=a_\ell)=\frac{1}{2} \frac{\ell^s(a_0)\ell^u(a_\ell)}{\lambda^u_0\cdots \lambda^u_{\ell-1}}\prod_{i=0}^{\ell-1}t_{a_i,a_{i+1}}^{(i)}.
\end{align*}
Since $E^s_0\perp E^u_0$,  $\mu_0(a_0)=\frac{1}{2}\textrm{Area}(a_0)=\frac{1}{2}\ell^s(a_0)\ell^u(a_0)$, and 
\begin{align*}
&{\mathbb{P}}(X_0^{(n)}=a_0,\ldots,X_\ell^{(n)}=a_\ell)=
\frac{ \mu_0(a_0)\ell^u(a_\ell)}{\lambda^u_0\cdots \lambda^u_{\ell-1}\ell^u(a_0)}\prod_{i=0}^{\ell-1}t_{a_i,a_{i+1}}^{(i)}=\mu(a_0)\prod_{i=0}^{\ell-1} \frac{\ell^u(a_{i+1})}{\lambda^u_i\ell^u(a_i)}t_{a_i,a_{i+1}}^{(i)}.
\end{align*}


This proves part (2) when $\ell\geq n$. To extend this to the case $\ell<n$, we first observe that by Part 6 of Lemma \ref{Lemma-Partition}, 
$\displaystyle \lambda^u_i \ell^u(a_i)=\sum_{a_{i+1}\in\mathfrak P_{i+1}}t_{a_i,a_{i+1}}^{(i)}\ell^u(a_{i+1})$, whence 
$$
\sum_{a_{i+1}\in\mathfrak P_{i+1}}\frac{\ell^u(a_{i+1})}{\lambda^u_i\ell^u(a_i)}t_{a_i,a_{i+1}}^{(i)}=1.
$$ 
Summing the identity 
$\displaystyle {\mathbb{P}}(X_0^{(n)}\!\!=\!\!a_0,\!\ldots\!,X_n^{(n)}\!\!=\!\!a_n)\!\!=\!\! \mu(a_0)\!\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} \frac{\ell^u(a_{i+1})}{\lambda^u_i\ell^u(a_i)}t_{a_i,a_{i+1}}^{(i)}
$ over  $a_n\!\!\in\!\!\mathfrak P_n$, we  obtain  
$
\displaystyle {\mathbb{P}}(X_0^{(n)}\!\!=\!\!a_0,\ldots,X_{n-1}^{(n)}\!\!=\!\!a_{n-1})\!\!=\!\!\mu(a_0)\prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \frac{\ell^u(a_{i+1})}{\lambda^u_i\ell^u(a_i)}t_{a_i,a_{i+1}}^{(i)}.
$
Summing  on $a_{n-1}\in\mathfrak P_{n-1}$ gives  
$\displaystyle
{\mathbb{P}}(X_0^{(n)}=a_0,\ldots,X_{n-2}^{(n)}=a_{n-2})=\mu(a_0)\prod_{i=0}^{n-3} \frac{\ell^u(a_{i+1})}{\lambda^u_i\ell^u(a_i)}t_{a_i,a_{i+1}}^{(i)}.
$ Continuing in this way, we obtain the second part for $\ell<n$.


Part (3) is just a restatement of Part (2) in the terminology of Markov chains. Part (4)
 follows from the bounded geometry estimates in Lemma \ref{Lemma-Partition}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- cor-10: body_md -->
The joint distribution of $(X^{(n)}_i)_{i\geq 0}$ does not depend on $n$.
<!-- end cor-10 -->
<!-- defi-6: body_md -->
\label{d.uniform-ellipticity}\index{Uniform ellipticity}
$(Y_n)_{n\geq 0}$ is   {\em uniformly elliptic}, if there is a positive constant $\varepsilon_0$, called an {\em ellipticity constant}, and a representation $\pi_{n,n+1}(y,y')=p_n(y,y')\mu_{n+1}(y')$, where 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item $\mu_n$ are probability measures on $\mathfrak S_n$;
\item $0\leq p_n(\cdot,\cdot)\leq 1/\varepsilon_0$;
\item $\displaystyle \sum_{y\in\mathfrak S_{n+1}} p_n(x,y)p_{n+1}(y,z)>\varepsilon_0$ for all $x\in\mathfrak S_n, z\in\mathfrak S_{n+2}$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defi-6 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\normalfont
The condition in Definition \ref{d.uniform-ellipticity} is sometimes called the {\em two-step ellipticity 
condition}, because (3) says that one can jump from any state at time $n$ to any state at time $n+2$ with positive probability, in two steps. For a discussion of  other $\gamma$-step ellipticity conditions, see  \S2.4 in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book}.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{Prop-Doeblin}
The Markov chain $(X_n)_{n\geq 0}$ is uniformly elliptic, with ellipticity constant $\varepsilon_0$ which only depends on $M(\beta)$ in \eqref{e.M-beta}.
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Let $\mathfrak S_n:=\mathfrak P_n$, and let $\pi_{n,n+1}(\cdot,\cdot)$ denote the transition kernel of $(X_n)_{n\geq 0}$. 
First we claim that the following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item $\mathfrak S_n$ have bounded cardinality;
\item $\exists\varepsilon_0'>0$  such that for all $n\geq 1$, $x\in \mathfrak S_n$ and $y\in\mathfrak S_{n+1}$, either $\pi_{n,n+1}(x,y)=0$ or 
$\pi_{n,n+1}(x,y)\geq \varepsilon_0'$;
\item For every $n\geq 0$, $x\in\mathfrak S_n$ and $z\in \mathfrak S_{n+2}$, there exists some $y\in\mathfrak S_{n+1}$ for which $\pi_{n,n+1}(x,y)\pi_{n+1,n+2}(y,z)>0$. 
\end{enumerate}

Part (1) is Propositions \ref{Prop-Markov}(4). Part (2) follows Proposition \ref{Prop-Markov-Kernel}(3), by noting that $\ell^u(\cdot)$ are uniformly bounded away from zero and infinity by Lemma \ref{Lemma-Partition}(10), and $\lambda_i^u$ are bounded away from zero and infinity by Proposition \ref{Prop-Contracting-Automorphisms}(4).

To see part (3), it is sufficient to find for every  $a\in \mathfrak P_n$ and $c\in\mathfrak P_{n+2}$ some $b\in\mathfrak P_{n+1}$ such that
$t^{(n)}_{a,b}, t^{(n+1)}_{b,c}\neq 0$. 

Write $a=Q_{\alpha,\beta}^n$ and $c=Q_{\gamma,\delta}^{n+2}$.
By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Partition},    $\mathrm{int}(c)\subset \psi_{n+1}(\mathrm{int}(Q_\gamma(n+1)))$.
Let $W$ be some $u$-fibre in $\mathrm{int}(a)$. By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Bounded-Geometry-Gamma(M)}, 
$\ell(W)\!\!\geq\!\!\Gamma(M)^{-1}.$  By Proposition \ref{Prop-Contracting-Automorphisms}(2)(b) and Equation \eqref{e.choice-of-lambda},
 $\ell(\psi_n(W))\geq T_0(M)$.  By the choice of $T_0(M)$ in \S\ref{ss.density-const}, $\psi_n(W)$ must intersect $\mathrm{int}(Q_\gamma(n+1))$. 
 
 Necessarily, $\psi_n(\mathrm{int}(a))$ intersects the interior of some $b\in\mathfrak P_{n+1}$ inside $Q_\gamma(n+1)$. Thus $t^{(n)}_{a,b}=1$. 
Since $b\subset Q_{\gamma}(n+1)$ and $c=Q_{\gamma,\delta}^{n+2}$, $\psi_{n+1}(b)$ intersects $\mathrm{int}(c)$ (Lemma~\ref{Lemma-Partition}(7)), so $t_{b,c}^{(n+1)}=1$, and we are done.


\smallskip
Conditions (1)--(3) imply uniform ellipticity with $\mu_n:=$uniform measure on $\mathfrak S_n$, 
$p_n(x,y):=\pi_{n,n+1}(x,y)\cdot|\mathfrak S_n|$,
and $\varepsilon_0:=(\varepsilon_0'/M')^2$,  $M':=\max\{|\mathfrak S_n|:n\geq 0\}$. 
These constants  depend only on the bounded geometry estimates in 
Lemma \ref{Lemma-Bounded-Geometry-Gamma(M)} and on the uniform bounds on $\|d\psi_i\|, \|d\psi_i^{-1}\|$. Therefore, they depend only on $M(\beta)$.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- cor-11: body_md -->
\label{Cor-rho-mixing}
There exist constants $C_{mix}>1$ and $\rho\in (0,1)$, which only depend on the ellipticity constant $\varepsilon_0$, such that for any $k,n$ and   square integrable functions $h_1, h_2$ such that $h_1$ is $\mathcal F_0^k$-measurable and $h_2$ is $\mathcal F_{k+n}^\infty$-measurable,
$$
\left|\mathbb E\bigl(h_1 h_2\bigr)-\mathbb E\bigl(h_1\bigr)\mathbb E\bigl(h_2\bigr)\right|\leq C_{mix}
\rho^n \sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(h_1)\mathrm{Var}(h_2)}.
$$
<!-- end cor-11 -->
<!-- cor-12: body_md -->
\label{Cor-phi-mixing}
There exist constants $C_{mix}>1$ and $\rho\in (0,1)$, which only depend on the ellipticity constant $\varepsilon_0$, such that for any $n>m>0$ and a bounded  function $h_n:\mathfrak P_n\to\mathbb R$, 
$
\left|\mathbb E\bigl(h_n(X_n)|X_m\bigr)-\mathbb E\bigl(h_n(X_n)\bigr)\right|\leq C_{mix}
\rho^{n-m}\|h_n\|_\infty.
$
<!-- end cor-12 -->
<!-- lem-19: body_md -->
\label{lemma-Hex-Meas}
 There exists $c_0>0$ so that  $m_{\mathrm{Hex}^n}(H)>c_0$ for every $n$ and  $H\in\mathrm{Hex}(n)$.
<!-- end lem-19 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{Prop-Markov-Kernel}, the probabilities of any pair ${\mathbb{P}}[X_k=a,X_{k+1}=b]$ and any triplet ${\mathbb{P}}[X_k=a,X_{k+1}=b,X_{k+2}=c]$ are either zero, or are bounded away from zero. By  Proposition \ref{Prop-Doeblin}, the probability of any event  ${\mathbb{P}}[X_{k-1}=a, X_{k+1}=b]$ is bounded away from zero. The lemma follows by direct calculation.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- defi-7: body_md -->
\cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book}
The {\em structure constants} of $(\mathsf X,\mathsf f)$  are the numbers
\begin{align}
& u_n:= \bigl(\mathbb E_{m_{\mathrm{Hex}}^n}(\Gamma^2)\bigr)^{1/2}\label{e.u},\\
&d_n(\xi):=\bigl(\mathbb E_{m_{\mathrm{Hex}}^n}(|e^{i\xi \Gamma}-1|^2)\bigr)^{1/2}\ \ \ \ (\xi\in\mathbb R)\label{e.d}.
\end{align}
<!-- end defi-7 -->
<!-- thm-29: body_md -->
\label{Theorem-D_N-Growth} Fix $M>1$. There are  constants $c_\xi>0$ such that \index{Structure constants!growth bounds}  every $\alpha\in{\mathsf{BT}}(M)$ (see \eqref{e.BT}), the Markov chain and jump functions from \S\ref{ss.Jump-Functions} and \ref{ss.IMC} satisfy the following:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item For every $N$ large enough,
$
\displaystyle c_0 N\leq \sum_{n=3}^N u_n^2\leq c_0^{-1}N.
$
\item For every $\xi\not\in 2\pi\mathbb Z$, for every $N$ large enough,
$
\displaystyle \sum_{n=3}^N d_n^2(\xi)\geq c_\xi N.
$
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-29 -->
<!-- lem-20: body_md -->
For every ${\varepsilon}>0$, there are
$N_{{\varepsilon}, M},  \delta_{\varepsilon,M}>0$ such that for every $\alpha\in{\mathsf{BT}}(M)$, \begin{equation}\label{e.q}
\exists1\leq q\leq N_{{\varepsilon},M}\textrm{ s.t. } \delta_{\varepsilon,M}<\|q\alpha\|<\frac{{\varepsilon}}{4}\textrm{ and } \sum_{j=0}^{q-1} \tau(z +j\alpha)=\pm 1 \textrm{ for all }z\in\mathbb T.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lem-20 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Denote the principal denominators of $\alpha$ by $q_k$. 
There are constants $1<M_1<M_2$ which only depend on $M$ so that 
    $
    M_1^k\leq q_k\leq M_2^k\textrm{ for all }k\geq 1
    $: Write $\alpha=[a_0;a_1,a_2,\ldots]$ and recall from \cite{Khintchine-Continued-Fractions} that $q_{n+1}=a_{n+1}q_n+q_{n-1}$, $q_0=0, q_1=a_1$. Then we can take $M_2:=2M$, and $M_1=\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$ (the lower bound for Fibonacci's sequence).



Fix $j_{\varepsilon}\in\mathbb N$ so large that $M_1^{j_{\varepsilon}}>\frac{1}{\sqrt{{\varepsilon}/4}}$ and let
$
N_{{\varepsilon},M}:=M_2^{j_{\varepsilon}+5}
$,  then 
$q_{j_{\varepsilon}}\!\!>\!\!2{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}$, and $q_{j_{\varepsilon}+4}\!\!<\!\!N_{{\varepsilon},M}$.
It is well-known that for at least one 
$j_{\varepsilon}\!\leq\! j\!\leq\!  j_{{\varepsilon}}+3$,  $q_j$ is an {\em odd} principal denominator satisfying 
$\displaystyle
\|q_j \alpha\|<\frac{1}{2q_j^2}
$ 
(see e.g. \cite[Lemma 1]{Huveneers}).
Positive integers $q$ such that $\|q\alpha\|<\frac{1}{2q^2}$ are called {\em Legendre denominators}. \index{Legendre denominators}\index{Odd Legendre denominators}
{\em Odd}  Legendre denominators $q$ satisfy
$
\displaystyle\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}\tau(x+j\alpha)=\pm 1\textrm{ on }\mathbb T,
$
see \cite[\S3]{Nakada-Keio} or \cite[Sublemma 1.2]{ANSS}. 
By construction, $q_j< N_{\varepsilon, M}$, $\|q_j\alpha\|<\frac{1}{2q_j^2}<\frac{{\varepsilon}}{4}$, 

By  \cite[Theorems 9,13]{Khintchine-Continued-Fractions},
 $\displaystyle \|q_j\alpha\|>1/(q_j+q_{j+1})>\frac{1}{2}M_2^{-N_{{\varepsilon},M}}=:\delta_{{\varepsilon},M}
$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lem-21: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-T} For every ${\varepsilon}>0$, there exist 
$T_{{\varepsilon}, M}$ such that for every $\alpha\in\mathrm{BT}(M)$ and  $\upsilon\!\!\in\!\!{\mathsf{St}}_0$, the following holds: Every line segment in ${\mathsf{St}}$ of length $T_{{\varepsilon},M}$ and direction  ${2\alpha-1 \choose 1}$ contains two points $\widetilde{\omega},\widetilde{\varpi}$ such that
${\rm dist}_{{\mathsf{St}}}(\widetilde{\varpi},D(\widetilde{\omega}))<{\varepsilon}$ and  ${\rm dist}_{{\mathsf{St}}_0}(\pi(\widetilde{\omega}),\upsilon)<{\varepsilon}$.
<!-- end lem-21 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Let $\Sigma$ and $\omega:\mathbb T\times\mathbb Z\to\Sigma$ be as in Theorem \ref{t.HHW}, and let $\beta:=2\alpha-1$.  
Choose $N_{\varepsilon,M}$, $\delta_{\varepsilon,M}$ and $1\leq q\leq N_{\varepsilon,M}$ as in the previous lemma.

Set $K_M\!\!:=\!\!\sqrt{1+(2M+3)^2}$. 
The linear flow $\phi$ traverses a  distance  $r\!\!:=\!\!\sqrt{1+\beta^2}\leq K_M$ between consecutive visits to the Poincar\'e section $\Sigma$. 
It is sufficient to consider the case when  $\upsilon$ is in the projection of $\Sigma$ to ${\mathsf{St}}_0$, otherwise we slide it in direction ${\beta\choose 1}$  no more than $K_M$ units of distance to $\Sigma$, and prove the lemma for the resulting point.
 We will show that for such $\upsilon$, the lemma holds with  $T_{\varepsilon,M}:=3N_{\varepsilon,M}K_M/\delta_M.$ 

Let $L$ be an arbitrary line segment in ${\mathsf{St}}$ with initial point $p$,  direction ${\beta\choose 1}$, and length bigger than $T_{\varepsilon,M}$. 

$\bullet$ Let $\widetilde{\omega}_0:={\omega}(x_0,n_0)$ denote the first intersection of $L$ with $\Sigma$. This point lies within distance $r$ from $p$, along $L$. 

$\bullet$ The $(k+1)$-th intersection of $L$ with $\Sigma$ is $\widetilde{\omega}_k:={\omega}(\{x_0+k\alpha\}, n_0+\tau_k(x_0))$, where 
    $
    \displaystyle \tau_k(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\tau(x+k\alpha)
    $. It is within distance $(k+1)r$ from $p$, in the direction of $L$. 

$\bullet$ Choose $q$ as in \eqref{e.q}. 
Since $\delta_{\varepsilon,M}<\|q\alpha\|<\frac{\varepsilon}{4}$,  
$\{\{x_0+k\alpha\}: 0\leq k\leq N_{\varepsilon,M}/\delta_{\varepsilon,M}\}$ is $\varepsilon/4$-dense in $\mathbb T$, and  there exists an integer $0\leq k^\ast\leq N_{{\varepsilon},M}/\delta_{\varepsilon,M}$ such that 
$$
{\rm dist}_{{\mathsf{St}}}(\widetilde{\omega}_{k^\ast},\widetilde{\upsilon})<\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\textrm{ for some $\widetilde{\upsilon}$ such that $\pi(\widetilde{\upsilon})=\upsilon$.}
$$
\item Let $k^\#\!\!:=\!\!k^\ast+q$ and $\sigma\!\!:=\!\!\tau_q(x_0+k^\ast\alpha)$. By the choice of $q$, 
$\sigma\!\!\in\!\!\{\!-\!1,\!+\!1\}$, and by Theorem~\ref{t.HHW},
${\widetilde{\omega}}_{k^\#}=\omega(T_\alpha^q(\{x_0+k^\ast\alpha\},n_{0}+\tau_{k^\ast}(x_0)))
=\omega(\{x_0+k^\ast\alpha+q\alpha\},n_{0}+\tau_{k^\ast}(x_0)+\sigma).
$

Comparing this to $D^{\sigma}({\widetilde{\omega}}_{k^\ast})=\omega(\{x_0+k^\ast\alpha\},n_{0}+\tau_{k^\ast}(x_0)+\sigma)$, we find that 
\begin{align*}
&{\rm dist}_{{\mathsf{St}}}(\widetilde{\omega}_{k^\#},D^{\sigma}({\widetilde{\omega}}_{k^\ast}))\leq  2\|q\alpha\|<\frac{\varepsilon}{2}.
\end{align*}
 (the factor $2$ is because of the formula for $\omega(\cdot,\cdot)$). By the choice of $q$, $|\sigma|=1$.



We obtained two points, $\widetilde{\omega}_{k^\ast}$ and $\widetilde{\omega}_{k^\#}$, which project to the ${\varepsilon}$-neighborhood of $\upsilon$, such that ${\rm dist}_{{\mathsf{St}}}(\widetilde{\omega}_{k^\#},D^{\sigma}(\widetilde{\omega}_{k^\ast}))<\frac{\varepsilon}{2}$, where $|\sigma|=1$.
These points are both on $L$, because their distance from  $p$ along $L$ is at most 
$
(k^\#+1)r\leq (2N_{\varepsilon,M}/\delta_{{\varepsilon},M}+1)K_M<T_{\varepsilon,M}
$.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lem-22: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-D_N-Growth}
For every $\xi\not\in 2\pi\mathbb Z$, there exists a positive constant $c_\xi$  so that for all $N$ large enough, 
for all $\alpha\in{\mathsf{BT}}(M)$,
$
\displaystyle \sum_{n=3}^N d_n^2(\xi)\geq c_{ \xi} N.
$
<!-- end lem-22 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Let $\mathfrak H(2m,n)$ denote the collection of arrays 
$
\left(
x_n \begin{array}{l}
x_{n+1}\\
y_{n+1}
\end{array}
\cdots
\begin{array}{l}
x_{n+m-1}\\
y_{n+m-1}
\end{array} y_{n+m}
\right)
$ such that  $x_i,y_i\in\mathfrak P_i$ and
$$
{\mathbb{P}}((X_n,\ldots,X_{n+m})=(x_n;\,x_{n+1},\ldots,x_{n+m-1};\, y_{n+m})|X_n=x_n)\neq 0;
$$
$$
{\mathbb{P}}((X_n,\ldots,X_{n+m})=(x_n;\, y_{n+1},\ldots,y_{n+m-1};\,y_{n+m})|X_n=x_n)\neq 0.
$$
The elements of $\mathfrak H(2m,n)$ are called  {\em admissible $2m$-gons} (at position $n+2$).\footnote{This scheme of enumerating the positions is in accordance with the conventions of \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book}.} 
The {\em balance} of an admissible $2m$-gon is 
$$
\Gamma\left({
x_n \begin{array}{l}
x_{n+1}\\
y_{n+1}
\end{array}
\cdots
\begin{array}{l}
x_{n+m-1}\\
y_{n+m-1}
\end{array} y_{n+m}}
\right):=\sum_{k=1}^{m-1} f_{n+k}(x_{n+k})-\sum_{k=1}^{m-1} f_{n+k}(y_{n+k}).
$$

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Claim 1.\/} For some $m\geq 3$, for every $n\geq 3$, $\Gamma(H)=1$ for some $H\in\mathfrak H(2m,n)$.

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Proof of the Claim.\/} 
Let  $\lambda_1:=1/\max \{\|d\widetilde{\psi}_k^{-1}\|:k\geq 0\}$ (this is a finite set) and $\lambda_2:=\lambda^{-1}$ with $\lambda$ as in Proposition \ref{Prop-Contracting-Automorphisms}, then 
 $$
 \lambda_2^{-1}\leq \|d\widetilde{\psi}_k^{-1}|_{E^s_{k+1}}\|\leq \lambda_1^{-1}\textrm{ for all $k$}.
 $$

 
 
 By Lemma~\ref{Lemma-Partition}(11), there is a positive constant $0<w<1$ such that every element of every  $\mathfrak P_k$ contains a ball of radius $w$.
Let ${\varepsilon}:=w/3$, and  let $M$ be a bound for the digits of the regular CFE of $\alpha$ and $1/(2\alpha-1)$. Choose $T_{{\varepsilon},M}$ as in Lemma \ref{Lemma-T}, making sure it is large enough to also satisfy the conclusion of Lemma \ref{LmDenseWs}.

Let   $m:=\lceil \log_{\lambda_2^{-1}}(T_{{\varepsilon},M}/w)\rceil$, and fix
 $n\geq 3$.
 Choose some arbitrary  $Q_{n+m}\in\mathfrak P_{n+m}$. By the definition of $w$, $Q_{n+m}$ contains in its interior a linear segment ${L}_{n+m}$ of length $w$ and direction $E^s_{n+m}$. Lift it to some segment $\widetilde{L}_{n+m}$ in the staircase. 
 Since $L_{n+m}$ does not intersect the boundary of any element of $\mathfrak P_{n+m}$, $\widetilde{L}_{n+m}$ does not intersect the boundary of $D^k(\widetilde{F}_{n+m})$ for any $k\in\mathbb Z$, and the $\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{n+m}$-coordinate remains constant on $\widetilde{L}_{n+m}$.

 Let
$
\widetilde{L}_n:=\widetilde{\psi}_n^{-1}\widetilde{\psi}_{n+1}^{-1}\cdots \widetilde{\psi}_{n+m-1}^{-1}(\widetilde{L}_{n+m}).
$
This is a linear segment in direction $E^s_n$, and 
$\displaystyle
|\widetilde{L}_n|\geq \lambda_2^{-m}w>T_{{\varepsilon},M}.
$

Fix some $\upsilon$ at the center of a ball with radius $w$, completely inside the interior of some element of $\mathfrak P_n$. 
By the choice of $T_{\varepsilon, M}$,  $\widetilde{L}_n$ contains two points $\widetilde{\omega},\widetilde{\varpi}$ such that 
$${\rm dist}_{{\mathsf{St}}}(\widetilde{\varpi},D(\widetilde{\omega}))<w/3\textrm{ and }{\rm dist}_{{\mathsf{St}}_0}(\pi(\widetilde{\omega}),\upsilon)<w/3.$$ 
The line segment $\gamma$ from  $\pi(\widetilde{\varpi})$ to $\pi(D({\widetilde{\omega}}))$ is inside $B(\upsilon,w)$, therefore it does not intersect the boundaries of any of the elements of $\mathfrak P_n$. Therefore, the line segment $\widetilde{\gamma}$ from $\widetilde{\varpi}$ to $D({\widetilde{\omega}})$ does not cross the boundary of $D^k(\widetilde{F}_n)$ for any $k\in\mathbb Z$. It follows that 

\begin{equation}\label{e.omega-varpi-1}
 \widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n(\widetilde{\varpi})=\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n(D({\widetilde{\omega}}))=\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}})+1.
\end{equation}
Similarly, $(\widetilde{\psi}_{n+m-1}\cdots\widetilde{\psi}_n)(\widetilde{\omega}), (\widetilde{\psi}_{n+m-1}\cdots\widetilde{\psi}_n)(\widetilde{\varpi})\in \widetilde{L}_{n+m}$, so 
\begin{equation}\label{e.omega-varpi-2}
\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{n+m}[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n+m-1}\cdots\widetilde{\psi}_n)(\widetilde{\omega})]=\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{n+m}[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n+m-1}\cdots\widetilde{\psi}_n)(\widetilde{\varpi})]
\end{equation}


Let $\omega,\varpi$ denote the projections of $\widetilde{\omega},\widetilde{\varpi}$ 
to the punctured torus ${\mathsf{St}}_0$.
We may assume without loss of generality that the points $\omega_n:=\omega$, $\varpi_n:=\varpi$ and the points
\begin{equation}\label{e.orbit-of-xy}
\omega_{n+j}:=(\psi_{n+j-1}\cdots{\psi}_n)(\omega), \quad
\varpi_{n+j}:=(\psi_{n+j-1}\cdots{\psi}_n)(\varpi) \quad
(j=1,\ldots,m)
\end{equation}
all lie in the interior of the Markov elements of $\mathfrak P_{n+j}$. Otherwise we shift 
$\widetilde{L}_{n+m}$ in the $E^u_{n+m}$-direction  slightly, and we shift $\omega,\varpi$ 
 in the $E^s_n$ direction slightly.
 
We can now safely define for $0\leq j\leq m$,
\begin{align*}
&\xi_{n+j}:=\mathfrak P_{n+j}-\textrm{element which contains $\omega_{n+j}$ in its interior};\\
&\eta_{n+j}:=\mathfrak P_{n+j}-\textrm{element which contains $\varpi_{n+j}$ in its interior}.
\end{align*}
Notice that
$
\xi_n=\eta_n\textrm{ and }\xi_{n+m}=\eta_{n+m}.
$
The first identity is because
$$
\omega, \varpi \in B(\omega,2w/3)\subset\textrm{ the interior of the same element of }
\mathfrak P_n.
$$
The second identity is because $\widetilde{L}_{n+m}$ was chosen to lie completely inside the interior of a Markov element of $\mathfrak P_{n+m}$. 


By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Cylinders} and the choice of $\omega_{n+j}, \varpi_{n+j}$, the cylinders $\<\dot{\xi}_n,\ldots,\xi_{n+m-1},\eta_{n+m}\>$ and 
$\<\dot{\xi}_n,\eta_{n+1}\ldots,\eta_{n+m}\>$ have non-empty interior. Therefore, 
$$
{\mathbb{P}}[(X_n,\ldots,X_{n+m})=(\xi_n;\,\xi_{n+1},\ldots,\xi_{n+m-1};\, \eta_{n+m})|X_n=\xi_n]\neq 0;
$$
$$
{\mathbb{P}}[(X_n,\ldots,X_{n+m})=(\xi_n;\, \eta_{n+1},\ldots,\eta_{n+m-1};\,\eta_{n+m})|X_n=\xi_n]\neq 0.
$$
Thus  $\left(
\xi_n \begin{array}{l}
\xi_{n+1}\\
\eta_{n+1}
\end{array}
\cdots
\begin{array}{l}
\xi_{n+m-1}\\
\eta_{n+m-1}
\end{array} \eta_{n+m}
\right)$ is an admissible $2m$-gon in position $n+2$. We have: 
\begin{align*}
&\Gamma\left(
\xi_n \begin{array}{l}
\xi_{n+1}\\
\eta_{n+1}
\end{array}
\cdots
\begin{array}{l}
\xi_{n+m-1}\\
\eta_{n+m-1}
\end{array} \eta_{n+m}
\right)
=\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}f_{n+j}(\xi_{n+j})-
\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}f_{n+j}(\eta_{n+j})\\
&=\sum_{j=1}^{m}f_{n+j}(\xi_{n+j})-
\sum_{j=1}^{m}f_{n+j}(\eta_{n+j}),\textrm{ because $\xi_{n+m}=\eta_{n+m}$}\\ 
&=\sum_{j=1}^{m}{f}_{n+j}(X^{(n+m)}_{n+j}(\omega_{n+m}))-
\sum_{j=1}^{m}{f}_{n+j}(X^{(n+m)}_{n+j}(\varpi_{n+m})), \textrm{ see }\eqref{e.X-new}\\
&=
\sum_{j=1}^{m}\widetilde{f}_{n+j}^{(n+m)}(\omega)-
\sum_{j=1}^{m}\widetilde{f}_{n+j}^{(n+m)}(\varpi), \textrm{ see Lemma \ref{Lemma-f(X)}}\\
&=\left[\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{n+m}({\widetilde{\omega}}_{n+m})-
\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}}_n)\right]-
\left[\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{n+m}(\widetilde{\varpi}_{n+m})-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n(\widetilde{\varpi}_n)\right], \textrm{ by \eqref{Eq-Modified-Frobenius}}\\
&=[\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n(\widetilde{\varpi})-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n(\widetilde{\omega})]+
[\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{n+m}((\widetilde{\psi}_{n+m-1}\cdots\widetilde{\psi}_n)(\widetilde{\omega}))-
\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{n+m}((\widetilde{\psi}_{n+m-1}\cdots\widetilde{\psi}_n)(\widetilde{\varpi}))]\\
&=1+0=1,\textrm{ by \eqref{e.omega-varpi-1} and \eqref{e.omega-varpi-2}}.
\end{align*}

\medskip
\noindent
{\sc Claim 2.\/} \label{page-hexagon-claim}{\em For every $\ell\geq 2$ and $n\geq 0$ there exists $n\leq n'\leq n+m-3$ and an admissible hexagon at position $n'+2$ such that 
$
\displaystyle \Gamma\left(
\xi_{n'} \begin{array}{l}
\xi_{n'+1}\\
\zeta_{n'+1}
\end{array}
\begin{array}{l}
\zeta_{n'+2}\\
\eta_{ n'+2}
\end{array} \eta_{n'+3}
\right)\neq 0\mbox{$\,\mathrm{mod}\,$}\ell
$.
}\\

\begin{figure}
  \centering
  \fbox{\includegraphics[width=7cm,angle=90]{Figure-Hex-Decomp-New}}
  \caption{A decomposition of a $2m$-gon to hexagons}\label{Figure-Hex-Decomposition}
\end{figure}



\noindent
{\em Proof of the Claim.\/} Let $\xi_i,\eta_j$ be in the proof of Claim 1. By uniform ellipticity  (Proposition \ref{Prop-Doeblin}), for every  $j=0,\ldots,m-1$ there is some $\zeta_{n+j+1}\in\mathfrak P_{n+j+1}$ such that
$$
{\mathbb{P}}[(X_{n+j},X_{n+j+1},X_{n+j+2})=(\xi_{n+j},\zeta_{n+j+1},\eta_{n+j+2})|X_{n+j}=\xi_{n+j}, X_{n+j+2}=\eta_{n+j+2}]\neq 0.
$$
Since $\xi_n=\eta_n$ and $\xi_{n+m}=\eta_{n+m}$, we may take
$
\zeta_{n+1}=\eta_{n+1}\textrm{ and }\zeta_{n+m-1}=\xi_{n+m-1}.
$

Let $H_i:=
\left(
\xi_{n+i} \begin{array}{l}
\xi_{n+i+1}\\
\zeta_{n+i+1}
\end{array}
\begin{array}{l}
\zeta_{n+i+2}\\
\eta_{n+i+2}
\end{array} \eta_{n+i+3}
\right).
$
These are admissible hexagons, and looking at Figure \ref{Figure-Hex-Decomposition}, we see that
$\displaystyle
\Gamma\left(
\xi_n \begin{array}{l}
\xi_{n+1}\\
\eta_{n+1}
\end{array}
\cdots
\begin{array}{l}
\xi_{n+m-1}\\
\eta_{n+m-1}
\end{array} \eta_{n+m}
\right)=\sum_{i=0}^{m-3}\Gamma(H_i),
$
because the terms $f_{n+j}(\zeta_j)$ on  the dashed lines appear twice with opposite signs, and cancel out.
Since the left-hand side equals one,  $\Gamma(H_i)\neq 0\mbox{$\,\mathrm{mod}\,$}\ell$ for some $i$, proving the claim.

\medskip
Suppose $\xi\in 2\pi\mathbb Q\setminus 2\pi\mathbb Z$. Then  $\xi\in\frac{2\pi}{\ell}\mathbb Z$ for some $\ell\in\mathbb N$, $\ell\geq 2$. If $\Gamma(H)\neq 0\mbox{$\,\mathrm{mod}\,$}\ell$, then $e^{i\xi\Gamma(H)}\in \{e^{2\pi i k/\ell}:k=1,\ldots,\ell-1\}$, and therefore  $|e^{i\xi\Gamma(H)}-1|>{{\overline c}_\xi}>0$ with ${\overline c}_\xi$ independent of $H$. 
Thus the claim says that for every $n\geq 2$, there are some $n\leq n'\leq n+m-3$  and  $H\in\mathrm{Hex}(n'+2)$ such that $|e^{i\xi \Gamma(H)}-1|\geq {\overline c}_\xi$. By Lemma \ref{lemma-Hex-Meas}, $ d_{n'}^2(\xi)\geq c_0 c_\xi^2$. Thus
$\displaystyle\sum_{n=2}^N d_n^2(\xi)\geq \left(\frac{N}{m}-1\right)c_0c_\xi^2$, and the lemma follows for all $\xi\in 2\pi\mathbb Q\setminus 2\pi\mathbb Z$.

Suppose $\xi\in 2\pi(\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Q)$. There is a constant such that $|\Gamma(H)|\leq M$ for all $H$, therefore if $\Gamma(H)\neq 0$, then  $e^{i\xi\Gamma(H)}\in \{e^{ik\xi}: k\in\mathbb Z\cap [-M,M], k\neq 0\}$. By the irrationality of  $\xi/2\pi$, this set does not contain $1$, and since it is finite, $|e^{i\xi\Gamma(H)}-1|>{\overline c}_\xi>0$ with ${\overline c}_\xi$ independent of $H$. Continuing as before, we obtain the lemma for $\xi\in 2\pi(\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Q)$.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- cor-13: body_md -->
\label{e.U_N-Growth}
Let $u_n:=\mathbb E_{m_{\mathrm{Hex}}^n}(\Gamma^2)^{1/2}$. 
There exists constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that for all $N$ large enough, 
$
\displaystyle c_1N\leq \sum_{n=3}^N u_n^2\leq c_2 N.
$
<!-- end cor-13 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Recall that $f_k$ are uniformly bounded. Therefore, the balance functions $\Gamma$ are uniformly bounded. So $u_n^2$ are bounded above, and the upper bound follows.

By the  general inequality $|e^{i\theta}-1|^2=4\sin^2\frac{\theta}{2}\leq \theta^2$,  
$ |d_n(\xi)| \leq u_n |\xi|$. Taking $\xi=\frac{2\pi}{\ell}$ with any $\ell\geq 2$, and looking at   Lemma \ref{Lemma-D_N-Growth}, we deduce the linear lower bound.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{Prop-Irred}
$(\mathsf X,\mathsf f)$ is irreducible, and its algebraic and essential ranges are both equal to $\mathbb Z$.
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
The {\em co-range} of $(\mathsf X,\mathsf f)$ is the set\index{Co-range}\index{Essential range!and the co-range}
$
H:=\{\xi\in\mathbb R:\sum d_n(\xi)^2<\infty\}.
$ The following facts are proved in \cite[Chapter 4]{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book}:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item $H$ is a closed additive group of $\mathbb R$, thus $H=\{0\}, t\mathbb Z$, or $\mathbb R$;
\item If $H=\{0\}$ then the essential range is $\mathbb R$; If $H=t\mathbb Z$ with $t\neq 0$ then the essential range is $\frac{2\pi}{t}\mathbb Z$; And if $H=\mathbb R$, then the essential range is $\{0\}$. 
\end{enumerate}
In our case, $H\!\!\supset\!\! 2\pi\mathbb Z$ (because $\Gamma$ takes values in $\mathbb Z$, so $d_n(2\pi)=0$).  But $H\cap (\mathbb R\setminus 2\pi\mathbb Z)\!\!=\!\!\varnothing$ by  Theorem \ref{Theorem-D_N-Growth}. Necessarily $H=2\pi\mathbb Z$, and the essential range is $\mathbb Z$. 
Since $f_k$ take values in the integers,  the algebraic range is contained in $\mathbb Z$. However it also contains the essential range, so it  must also equal $\mathbb Z$.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- prop-7: body_md -->
\label{Prop-Drift}
There exists a constant $E$ which only depends on $M(\beta)$ such that $|\mathbb E(S_N)|\leq E$ for all $N$.\index{Drift of $S_N$}
<!-- end prop-7 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Let $\mu_0$ denote the normalized area measure on ${\mathsf{St}}_0$. 
By  Lemma \ref{Lemma-f(X)}
                                           
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb E(S_N)=\int_{{\mathsf{St}}_0}\sum_{k=1}^N f_k(X^{(N)}_k(\omega))\, d\mu_0=\int_{{\mathsf{St}}_0}\sum_{k=1}^N \widetilde{f}_k^{(N)}(\omega)\, d\mu_0.
\end{align*}
For each $\omega\in{\mathsf{St}}_0^\ast$, let ${\widetilde{\omega}}_N\in {\mathsf{St}}^\ast$ be the unique lift of $\omega$ such that ${{\mathfrak{z}}}({\widetilde{\omega}}_N)=0$, and let 
${\widetilde{\omega}}_{k}:=(\widetilde{\psi}_k^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{N-1}^{-1})({\widetilde{\omega}}_N)$. 
Then
$
\widetilde{f}^{(N)}_{k+1}(\omega)=\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{k+1}({\widetilde{\omega}}_{k+1})-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_k({\widetilde{\omega}}_k)
$ by definition, whence 
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb E(S_N)=\int_{{\mathsf{St}}_0} [\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{N}({\widetilde{\omega}}_{N})-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)] d\mu_0(\omega)=
\int_{{\mathsf{St}}_0} [{\mathfrak{z}}({\widetilde{\omega}}_{N})-{\mathfrak{z}}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)] d\mu_0(\omega)+E_N,
\end{align*}
where the $\displaystyle |E_N|\leq E:=2\sup_{N}\sup_{{\widetilde{\omega}}\in{\mathsf{St}}^\ast}|\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_N({\widetilde{\omega}})-{\mathfrak{z}}({\widetilde{\omega}})|$. $E$ is finite by Lemma \ref{Lemma-Modified-Approx-Canonical}, and by the bounded geometry of $\Pi(n)$, 
$E$ has 
                         
an upper  bound which depends only on $M(\beta)$. 

Since $\omega$ is uniformly distributed on ${\mathsf{St}}_0$, and $\pi:{\mathsf{R}}_0\to{\mathsf{St}}_0$ is measure preserving, ${\widetilde{\omega}}_N$ is uniformly distributed on ${\mathsf{R}}_0$. So
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb E(S_N)=\int_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} [{\mathfrak{z}}({\widetilde{\omega}}_N)-{\mathfrak{z}}((\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{N-1}^{-1})({\widetilde{\omega}}_N)] d\mu_0({\widetilde{\omega}}_N){\pm E} \\
        
&=\int_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} [{\mathfrak{z}}(\widetilde{\psi}_{N-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)({\widetilde{\omega}}_0))-{\mathfrak{z}}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)] d\mu_0({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)
{\pm E} 
       
\textrm{ because $\widetilde{\psi}_i$ are area preserving}\\
&=\delta(\widetilde{\psi}_{N-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0){ \pm E} 
        
\textrm{ where $\delta(\cdot)$ is the average drift defined in \eqref{Eq-Drift-Defn}.}
\end{align*}
Now recall that  $\delta(\widetilde{\psi}_{N-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)=\sum \delta(\widetilde{\psi}_i)$ (see \cite{Avila-Dolgopyat-Duryev-Sarig}), and  $\delta(\widetilde{\psi}_i)=0$.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- prop-8: body_md -->
\label{Prop-Var-Growth}
There exist positive constants $C_1,C_2$ which only depend on $M(\beta)$, such that for all $N$ large enough, \index{Variance of $S_N$}
$
C_1 N\leq \mathrm{Var}(S_N)\leq C_2 N.
$
<!-- end prop-8 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
By Theorem \ref{LmVarCycles}
there are positive constants $C_1$ and $C_2$ which only depend on the ellipticity constant and on $\sup_{n\geq 1} \|f_n\|$ such that 
$$
C_1^{-1}\sum_{n=3}^N u_n^2-C_2\leq \mathrm{Var}(S_N)\leq C_1 \sum_{n=3}^N u_n^2+C_2.
$$
The proposition follows from Theorem \ref{Theorem-D_N-Growth}.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- prop-9: body_md -->
\label{Prop-Markov-Representation-of-Phi}
There exists a uniformly bounded sequence of functions $\overline{\varepsilon}_n:{\mathsf{St}}^\ast\to\mathbb Z$ so that the stochastic processes  \index{Random walks driven by renormalizations!and $S_N$} $\{\Phi_n-\overline{\varepsilon}_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ and  $\{S_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ are equal in distribution.
<!-- end prop-9 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Suppose ${\widetilde{\omega}}\in{\mathsf{R}}_0$,
then ${\mathfrak{z}}({\widetilde{\omega}})=0$, and 
\begin{align*}
\Phi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})&={\mathfrak{z}}[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)({\widetilde{\omega}})]-{\mathfrak{z}}({\widetilde{\omega}})
=\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)({\widetilde{\omega}})]-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0({\widetilde{\omega}})
+\overline{{\varepsilon}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}}),\textrm{ with }\\
\overline{{\varepsilon}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}})&:=({\mathfrak{z}}-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n)((\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)({\widetilde{\omega}}))-({\mathfrak{z}}-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0)({\widetilde{\omega}}).
\end{align*}

The functions $\overline{{\varepsilon}}_n$ are uniformly bounded,  by Lemma \ref{Lemma-Modified-Approx-Canonical}. We claim that $(\Phi_n-\overline{{\varepsilon}})_{n\geq 1}$ is equal in distribution to $S_n$. It is convenient to set  ${\widetilde{\omega}}_0:={\widetilde{\omega}}$, and  
$
{\widetilde{\omega}}_k:=(\widetilde{\psi}_{k-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)$. Then ${\widetilde{\omega}}=(\widetilde{\psi}_{0}^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})({\widetilde{\omega}}_n)$, and   
\begin{align*}
&\Phi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})=\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}}_n)-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0({\widetilde{\omega}})
+\overline{{\varepsilon}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}})\\
&=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}[\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{k+1}({\widetilde{\omega}}_{k+1})-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_k({\widetilde{\omega}}_k)]+\overline{{\varepsilon}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}})
=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}f_{k+1}^{(n)}(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}}_n))+\overline{{\varepsilon}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}}),\textrm{ see }\eqref{Eq-Modified-Frobenius}\\
&=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}f_{k+1}\bigl(X_{k+1}^{(n)}(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}}_n))\bigr)+\overline{{\varepsilon}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}})=\sum_{k=1}^n f_k\big(X_k^{(0)}(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}}))\bigr)+\overline{{\varepsilon}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}}),
                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                        
\end{align*}
by Lemma \ref{Lemma-f(X)} and  \eqref{e.X_i-tranformation-law}. 
The map  $\pi:{\mathsf{R}}_0\to{\mathsf{St}}_0^\ast$ is area preserving and invertible. So  if ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is sampled randomly uniformly in ${\mathsf{R}}_0$, then $\pi({\widetilde{\omega}})$ is distributed randomly uniformly in ${\mathsf{St}}_0$, and
$
\Phi_n-\overline{{\varepsilon}}_n
$ is equal in distribution to $\displaystyle \sum_{k=1}^{n} f_k(X_k^{(0)}(\omega'))$, where $\omega'$ is distributed randomly uniformly in ${\mathsf{St}}_0$. By Proposition \ref{Prop-Markov-Kernel}, $\Phi_n-\overline{{\varepsilon}}_n=S_n$ in distribution.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lem-23: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-Psi-and-Phi}
                                                                                                                                     
The slopes
 of $d\widetilde{e}^{-1}{1\choose 0}, d\widetilde{e}^{-1}{0\choose 1}$ for $\widetilde{e}\in\mathcal E$ are uniformly bounded away from the slopes of $E^u_n, E^s_n$ for all $n$.
<!-- end lem-23 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{Prop-Contracting-Automorphisms}, the slopes of $E^s_n,E^u_n$ have uniformly bounded  regular CFE.
On the other hand, since $m_i$ are bounded, the slopes of  $d\widetilde{e}^{-1}{1\choose 0}$ and $d\widetilde{e}^{-1}{0\choose 1}$ are rational numbers $p/q$ with uniformly bounded denominator, say  $1\leq q\leq Q$. 

The lemma now follows from
 the following well-known fact: For every $M$ there is a $c(M)>0$ such that for every irrational number $\sigma$ with regular continued fraction expansion all of whose digits are less than $M$,  for all relatively prime integers $p,q$, $|\sigma-\frac{p}{q}|\geq c(M)q^{-2}$. See e.g. the proof of Theorem 23 in \cite{Khintchine-Continued-Fractions}.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lem-24: body_md -->
\label{l.Phi-Decomp}
For every $N=nN_0+\ell$ and integers  $n\geq 1$ and $0\leq \ell\leq N_0-1$, \index{Random walks driven by renormalizations!and $S_N$}
\begin{align}
&\Upsilon_{N}=\overline{S}_{n}-\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0+\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_{n,\ell} \label{e.Phi-Decomp}
\end{align}
where $\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0:={\mathfrak{z}}-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0$, $\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_{n,\ell}:=({\mathfrak{z}}\circ \widetilde{\varphi}_{n,\ell}-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n)\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0$,  $\displaystyle \overline{S}_n(\widetilde{\omega}):=\sum_{k=1}^n f_k(\overline{X}_k(\widetilde{\omega}))$,  
\begin{align}
\overline{X}_k(\widetilde{\omega})& := X^{(0)}_k(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}}))=\textrm{unique element of $\mathfrak P_k$ containing $(\psi_{k-1}\circ\cdots\psi_0)(\pi(\widetilde{\omega}))$}.\label{e.X-bar}
\end{align} 
If ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is sampled randomly uniformly from ${\mathsf{R}}_0$, then $(\overline{X}_k({\widetilde{\omega}}))_{k\geq 0}$ is equal in distribution to $(X_k)_{k\geq 0}$, and $(\overline{S}_n({\widetilde{\omega}}))_{n\geq 1}$ is equal in distribution to $(S_n)_{n\geq 1}$. The quantities 
$\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0$ and $\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_{n,\ell}$ are uniformly bounded.
<!-- end lem-24 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
See \eqref{e.Psi-and-Phi}, and the proof of Proposition \ref{Prop-Markov-Representation-of-Phi}.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lem-25: body_md -->
\label{l.sigma-algebra}
$\overline{\mathcal F}_0^\infty=\mathcal W^s_0({\mathsf{R}}_0)$ mod $\mu_0$,  i.e. for every $A\in \overline{\mathcal F}_0^\infty$ there is a $B\in \mathcal W_0^s({\mathsf{R}}_0)$ such that $\mu_0(A\triangle B)=0$, and vice versa. Moreover, if $\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}:=\mu_0|_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}$,   then 
   for all $g\in L^1(\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0})$,  
\begin{equation}\label{e.conditional-expect-id-s}
\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}(g|\overline{\mathcal F}_0^\infty)(x)=\frac{1}{|W^s_0(x)|}\int_{W^s_0(x)}g\, ds\ \ \ (\textrm{integral with respect to arc length}).
\end{equation}
<!-- end lem-25 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
If $\mathcal{F}', \mathcal{F}''$ are two $\sigma$-algebras s.t. for each $g\in L^1(\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0})$,
$\mathbb E(g|\mathcal{F}')=\mathbb E(g|\mathcal{F}'')$ almost everywhere then for each $A'\in \mathcal{F}'$ there exists $A''\in \mathcal{F}''$
such that $\mu_0(A'\triangle A'')=0$, e.g. 
$A''=\{\omega: F=1\}$, where $F$ is an $\mathcal{F}''$-measurable a.e. version of $ \mathbb E(1_{A'}|\mathcal{F}'')(\omega)$. 


Thus, to prove the lemma, it is sufficient to verify \eqref{e.conditional-expect-id-s}. 

By Fubini's theorem, both sides of \eqref{e.conditional-expect-id-s} define bounded linear operators on $L^1$; therefore it is sufficient to prove   \eqref{e.conditional-expect-id-s} on a dense set in $L^1$. We will prove it for $g$ such that $g\circ\pi|_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}^{-1}$ is uniformly continuous on ${\mathsf{St}}_0$. 




Given ${\widetilde{\omega}}\in{\mathsf{St}}$, let $C_n({\widetilde{\omega}}):=\<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_n\>$, where $a_i:=\overline{X}_i({\widetilde{\omega}})$, then  $\overline{\mathcal F}_0^n$ is the discrete $\sigma$-algebra with atoms $\pi^{-1}|_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(C_n({\widetilde{\omega}}))$, and 
$$
\mathbb E(g|\overline{\mathcal F}_0^n)({\widetilde{\omega}})=\frac{1}{\mu_0(C_n({\widetilde{\omega}}))}\int_{C_n({\widetilde{\omega}})}g\circ\pi|_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}^{-1} d\mu_0.
$$
$C_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$ are $(E^s_0,E^u_0)$-parallelograms with stable side of length $\ell^s(a_0)$, and unstable sides of length tending to zero as $n\to\infty$. These parallelograms decrease to an $E^u_0$-segment of length $\ell^s(a_0)$, containing $\pi({\widetilde{\omega}})$. By length considerations, this segment equals $\pi[W^s_0({\widetilde{\omega}})]$ up to endpoints. By the uniform continuity of $g\circ\pi|_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}^{-1}$, 
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb E(g|\overline{\mathcal F}_0^n)({\widetilde{\omega}})=\frac{1}{|\pi(W^s_0({\widetilde{\omega}}))|}\int_{\pi(W^s_0({\widetilde{\omega}}))}g\circ\pi|_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}^{-1}\, ds=\frac{1}{|W^s_0({\widetilde{\omega}})|}\int_{W^s_0({\widetilde{\omega}})}g\, ds.
$$
By the martingale convergence theorem, the left-hand-side is $\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}(g|\overline{\mathcal F}_0^\infty)$.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lem-26: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-Xi-and-S_n}
There exists a uniformly bounded sequence of functions  $\varepsilon_n:{\mathsf{St}}^\ast\to\mathbb Z$ such that \index{Random walks driven by renormalizations!and $S_N$}
$
\displaystyle\Xi_n-\varepsilon_n=-\sum_{k=1}^{n}f_{k}\circ X^{(n)}_{k}\circ \pi
$, with $X^{(n)}_k$ as in \eqref{e.X-new}.
<!-- end lem-26 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Let $\varepsilon_n:{\mathsf{St}}^\ast\to\mathbb Z$ be the function
\begin{equation}\label{e.epsilon-process}
\varepsilon_n:={\mathfrak{z}}\circ (\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1}) -\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{0}\circ (\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})+\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n-{\mathfrak{z}}.
\end{equation}
By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Modified-Approx-Canonical}, $\varepsilon_n(\cdot)$ is a uniformly bounded sequence of functions.  

Define ${\widetilde{\omega}}_n:={\widetilde{\omega}}$, and ${\widetilde{\omega}}_k:=(\widetilde{\psi}_k^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})({\widetilde{\omega}}_n)$. Then, 
\begin{align*}
&\Xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})-{\varepsilon}_n({\widetilde{\omega}})=\Xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}}_n)-{\varepsilon}({\widetilde{\omega}}_n)={\mathfrak{z}}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)-{\mathfrak{z}}({\widetilde{\omega}}_n)-{\mathfrak{z}}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)+\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}}_n)+{\mathfrak{z}}({\widetilde{\omega}}_n)\\
&=\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}}_n)=-\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \bigl[\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{k+1}({\widetilde{\omega}}_{k+1})-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{k}({\widetilde{\omega}}_{k})\bigr]
=-\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}f^{(n)}_{k+1}(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}})), \textrm{ see \eqref{Eq-Modified-Frobenius}}.
\end{align*}
Now apply Lemma \ref{Lemma-f(X)}.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- defi-8: body_md -->
\label{d.pure-E-segments}
A {\em pure} $E^s_n$-segment with {\em depth}\index{Depth} $k$ and {\em height}\index{Height} $\ell$ is an $E^s_n$-segment inside $D^\ell(\widetilde{F}_n)\subset{\mathsf{St}}$, which projects up to endpoints to a maximal $E^s_n$-segment inside a cylinder $\<a_{n-k},\ldots,\dot{a}_n\>\subset{\mathsf{St}}_0$.
<!-- end defi-8 -->
<!-- defi-9: body_md -->
\label{d.elementary}
Let $W$ be a pure $E^s_n$-segment. \index{Elementary events} \index{E$^u$-segment and E$^s$-segment @ $E^u$-segment and $E^s$-segment!pure segments!elementary events}
The elements of the $\sigma$-algebra on $W$ generated by  $X^{(n)}_i\circ\pi:W\to\mathbb Z$, $i=0,\ldots,n$ are called {\em elementary events} in $W$.
<!-- end defi-9 -->
<!-- lem-27: body_md -->
\label{l.prob-of-elementry-event}
Under the above assumptions, \index{Elementary events} \index{E$^u$-segment and E$^s$-segment @ $E^u$-segment and $E^s$-segment!pure segments!elementary events}
\begin{align}\label{e.prob-of-elementary-event}
{\mathbb{P}}_W(C)&={\mathbb{P}}[X_0=a_0,\ldots,X_{n}=a_{n}|X_{n-k}=a_{n-k},\ldots,X_n=a_n]\\
&=
{\mathbb{P}}[X_0=a_0,\ldots,X_{n-k-1}=a_{n-k-1}|X_{n-k}=a_{n-k}].\notag
\end{align}
<!-- end lem-27 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Set $Q:=\<a_{n-k},\ldots,\dot{a}_n\>$, and let $\widetilde{Q}$ denote the lift of $Q$ to $D^\ell(\widetilde{F}_n)$. 
 By Lemma~\ref{Lemma-Cylinder-Area}, these  are $(E^u_n,E^s_n)$-parallelograms.
                                                                                  
 
By assumption, $W$ is a maximal $E^s_n$-segment in $\widetilde{Q}$. Let
$
{\vartheta}:\widetilde{Q}\to W
$ denote the {projection along the $E^u_n$-direction}, namely the function which maps ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ to the unique point in  $W^u({\widetilde{\omega}},\widetilde{Q})\cap W$, where  $W^u({\widetilde{\omega}},\widetilde{Q}):=$ the maximal $E^u_n$-segment  through ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ in $\widetilde{Q}$. 

         
          
                                            
 
 
 
                                                    
   
                                                                                     
 
           
          
                             
                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
   
                                                                                                                      
   
                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                   

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Claim 1.\/} Let ${\mathbb{P}}_W, {\mathbb{P}}_{\widetilde{Q}}$ denote the uniform distributions on $W$ and $\widetilde{Q}$, then ${\mathbb{P}}_{W}={\mathbb{P}}_{\widetilde{Q}}\circ\vartheta^{-1}$. 

\smallskip
\noindent
{\em Proof of the Claim.\/} Let $\ell$ and $m$ denote the Euclidean length and area.  
Suppose $J$ is sub-segment of $W$, then $\vartheta^{-1}(J)$ is a parallelogram with $E^s_n$-side  $J$, and $E^u_n$-side with length $\ell^u(a_n)$. Thus  $m(\vartheta^{-1}(J))=\ell(J)\ell^u(a_n)|\sin\measuredangle(E^u_n,E^s_n)|$. Since $J$ was arbitrary,  $(m\circ\vartheta^{-1})|_{W}=\operatorname{const}.\ell|_{W}$. Normalizing to total mass one, we obtain ${\mathbb{P}}_{\widetilde{Q}}\circ\vartheta^{-1}={\mathbb{P}}_{W}$.





\medskip
\noindent
{\em Claim 2.\/} Let  $\widetilde{P}$ denote the lift of $P:=\<a_0,\ldots,\dot{a}_n\>$ to $D^\ell(\widetilde{F}_n)$, then  $\vartheta^{-1}(C)=\widetilde{P}$.

\smallskip
\noindent
{\em Proof of the Claim.\/}    By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Cylinder-Area}, $\widetilde{P}$ is an $(E^u_n,E^s_n)$-parallelogram, and the $E^u_n$-sides of $\widetilde{P},\widetilde{Q}$ have the same length $\ell^u(a_n)$. Since $\widetilde{P}\subset\widetilde{Q}$, the maximal $E^u_n$-segments in $\widetilde{P}$ must  also be maximal $E^u_n$-segments in $\widetilde{Q}$. 
Thus $\vartheta^{-1}(C)$ equals the  union of all maximal $E^u_n$-segments  in $\widetilde{P}$ which intersect $C$.  
$C$ is a maximal $E^s_n$-segment of $\widetilde{P}$, because $\pi(C)$ is a maximal $E^s_n$-segment of $P$,  by assumption. So  
$
\vartheta^{-1}(C)=\widetilde{P}. 
$

\medskip
By Claims 1 and 2,  $\displaystyle{\mathbb{P}}_W(C)={\mathbb{P}}_{\widetilde{Q}}(\vartheta^{-1}(C))={\mathbb{P}}_{\widetilde{Q}}(\widetilde{P})=\frac{\textrm{Area}(\widetilde{P})}{\textrm{Area}(\widetilde{Q})}=
\frac{\textrm{Area}(P)}{\textrm{Area}(Q)}$. By Proposition \ref{Prop-Markov-Kernel},   ${\mathbb{P}}_W(C)={{\mathbb{P}}[X_0=a_0,\ldots,X_n=a_n]}/{{\mathbb{P}}[X_0=a_{n-k},\ldots,X_n=a_n]}$. Since $(X_i)_{i\geq 0}$ is a Markov chain, 
${\mathbb{P}}_W(C)={\mathbb{P}}
[X_0=a_0,\ldots,X_{n-k-1}=a_{n-k-1}|X_{n-k}=a_{n-k}]$.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- cor-14: body_md -->
Suppose $W\in\mathfs W_{n,k}$. If $W$ projects to a maximal $E^s_n$-segment in $\<a_{n-k},\ldots,\dot{a}_n\>$,  then for every $n>k$, \index{E$^u$-segment and E$^s$-segment @ $E^u$-segment and $E^s$-segment!pure segments!conditioning on}
\begin{equation}\label{e.Xi-W-local-prob-formula}
{\mathbb{P}}(\Xi_n^W-{\varepsilon}_n=t)={\mathbb{P}}\left(S_{n-k-1}=-t-\sum_{j=n-k}^n f_j(a_j)\,\bigg|\,X_{n-k}=a_{n-k}\right).
\end{equation}
<!-- end cor-14 -->
<!-- lem-28: body_md -->
\label{l.approx-by-pure-segments}
For every $L>1$ and $\delta>0$ there are positive integers $k,K>1$ as follows. Suppose  $W_n$ is a sequence of $E^s_n$-segments in ${\mathsf{St}}$ with lengths in $[L^{-1},L]$.\index{E$^u$-segment and E$^s$-segment @ $E^u$-segment and $E^s$-segment!approximation by pure segments} Then for all $n>K$, there are pure $E^s_n$ segments of depth $k$ $W_{n,1},\ldots,W_{n,m_n+2}$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item $W_{n,i}$ have pairwise disjoint relative interiors;
\item $\displaystyle\bigcup_{i=1}^{m_n}W_{n,i}\subset W_n\subset \bigcup_{i=1}^{m_n+2}W_{n,i}$\textrm{ and each $\overline{W}_{n,i}$ intersects $\overline{W}_n$};
\item $\displaystyle \frac{1}{|W_n|}\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}|W_{n,i}|{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}(\cdot)\leq 
{\mathbb{P}}_{W_n}(\cdot)\leq \frac{1}{|W_n|}\sum_{i=1}^{m_n+2}|W_{n,i}|{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}(\cdot)
$;
\item $\displaystyle 1-\delta\leq \frac{1}{|W_n|}\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}|W_{n,i}|\leq 1\leq \frac{1}{|W_n|}\sum_{i=1}^{m_n+2}|W_{n,i}|\leq 1+\delta
$;
\item $m_n\leq K$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-28 -->
<!-- lem-29: body_md -->
\label{l.trivial-prob-fact}
Suppose $Y_n,Y_n'$ are random variables on the same probability spaces $\mathfrak S_n$ such that  $\|Y_n-Y_n'\|_\infty\to 0$ or $\|Y_n/Y_n'-1\|_\infty\to 0$. If $Y_n$ converges in distribution to a limit without atoms, then $Y_n'$ converges in distribution to the same limit. \index{Convergence in distribution}
<!-- end lem-29 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
For every $\varepsilon>0$ and $t\neq 0$,  ${\mathbb{P}}[Y_n'<t]$ is eventually between ${\mathbb{P}}[Y_n<t\pm{\varepsilon}]$.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- lem-30: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-Pure-Seg-CLT}Let $W_n$ be a sequence of pure $E^s_n$-segments  such that $|W_n|$ is bounded below.
                                                           
Then for all $a<b$,
$$
{\mathbb{P}}\left[{\Xi_n^{W_n}}/{\sqrt{V_n}}\in (a,b)\right]\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_a^b e^{-t^2/2} dt.
$$
<!-- end lem-30 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
By \eqref{e.c-over}, the depths of $W_n$ must be bounded above,  so  we can split $\{W_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ to subsequences with eventually  constant depth. Without loss of generality, all $W_n$ have the same  depth $k$. In particular, each $W_n$ projects to a maximal $E^s_n$-segment in some cylinder $\<a_{n-k}^{(n)},\ldots,\dot{a}_n^{(n)}\>$. 
Let  $\displaystyle s_{n,k}=\sum_{j=n-k}^n f_j(a_j^{(n)})=O(1)$. By \eqref{e.Xi-W-local-prob-formula}, 
\begin{equation}\label{e.do}
{\mathbb{P}}_{W_n}\left[\frac{\Xi_n-{\varepsilon}_n}{\sqrt{V_{n}}}\in (a,b)\right]=
{\mathbb{P}}\left(\frac{S_{n-k-1}+ s_{n,k}}{\sqrt{V_{n}}}\in (-b,-a)\, \bigg|\, X_{n-k}=a_{n-k}^{(n)}
\right).
\end{equation}
 Here ${\varepsilon}_n$ is the uniformly bounded sequence of functions from Lemma \ref{Lemma-Xi-and-S_n} 

The conditioning is on the last coordinate, not the first coordinate. To deal with this, we reverse time and work with the array 
$$
\begin{array}{lllll}
X_0 &&&&
\textrm{conditioned on }X_0=a_0^{(k)}\\
X_1 & X_0 &&& \textrm{conditioned on }X_1=a_1^{(k+1)}\\
 \ \vdots & \ \vdots & \ddots & &\\
 X_{n-k}& X_{n-k-1} & \cdots & X_0 & \textrm{conditioned on }X_{n-k}=a_{n-k}^{(n)}.
\end{array}
$$
Each row is a finite Markov chain, and one 
can prove exactly as in Proposition \ref{Prop-Doeblin} that all rows are uniformly elliptic with the same ellipticity constant. 

Using the exponential mixing of uniformly elliptic Markov arrays (Proposition \ref{p.mixing-for-arrays}), it is possible to show that
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb E'(S_{n-k-1}):= \mathbb E(S_{n-k-1}|X_{n-k}=a_{n-k}^{(n)})=\mathbb E(S_{n-k-1})+O(1);\\
&V_{n-k-1}':={\rm Var}(S_{n-k-1}|X_{n-k}=a_{n-k}^{(n)})\sim V_{n-k-1};\\
&V_{n-k-1}\sim V_n.
\end{align*}
By Propositions \ref{Prop-Drift} and \ref{Prop-Var-Growth},  $V_{n-k-1}'\to\infty$ and $\mathbb E(S_{n-k-1}|X_{n-k}=a_{n-k}^{(n)})=O(1)$.
 
We now apply  Dobrushin's central limit theorem, in its version  for  uniformly elliptic  Markov arrays (Theorem \ref{ThMCCLT}). By Lemma~\ref{l.trivial-prob-fact}, we can replace $A_n$ by minus $\mathbb E'(S_{n-k-1})$ and $V_n$ by $V_{n-k-1}'$, and this leads to
 $$
{\mathbb{P}}\left(\frac{S_{n-k}+s_{n,k}}{\sqrt{V_{n}}}\in (-b,-a)\, \bigg|\, X_{n-k}=a_{n-k}^{(n)}
\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_a^b e^{-t^2/2}dt.
$$
By  \eqref{e.do},  $\frac{\Xi_n^{W_n}-{\varepsilon}_n}{\sqrt{V_n}}$ converges in distribution to the standard normal. Since $s_{n,k}$ and ${\varepsilon}_n$ are uniformly bounded and $V_n\!\to\!\infty$, the lemma follows from  Lemma \ref{l.trivial-prob-fact}.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
Fix 
$\widetilde{\omega}\in {\mathsf{St}}$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
Suppose $T\gg 1$, and let 
$
A_T:=\{\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}):0<t<T\}.
$

By Proposition \ref{Prop-Contracting-Automorphisms}, 
$
(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(A_T)
$ is an $E^s_n$-segment of length $\lambda_{n-1}^s\cdots\lambda_0^s T$, where $\lambda^s_i:=\|d\widetilde{\psi}_i|_{E^s_i}\|\leq \lambda^{-1}<1$.  Since there are only finitely many different $\widetilde{\psi}_i$, $\lambda^s_i>L^{-1}$ with $L>1$ independent of $i$. So for every $T>1$, there are $n$ such that 
\begin{equation}
\label{DefBrN}
A_T^\ast:=(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(A_T)\textrm{ has length in }[1,L].
\end{equation}
 Let $n(T)$ be the minimal number satisfying this condition.
Necessarily,  $n/\log T$ is bounded away from zero and infinity for all $T$ large enough. Let 
$$
\sigma_T:=\sqrt{V_n},\textrm{ where }V_n:=\mathrm{Var}(S_n), \quad
a_T(\widetilde{\omega}):=z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}}), \textrm{ see \eqref{e.z-n} and \eqref{e.mat-prod-form}}.  
$$
$A_T^\ast$ begins inside horizontal rectangle ${\mathsf{R}}_{a_T({\widetilde{\omega}})}$, and  $A_T^\#:=D^{-a_T}(A_T^\ast)$ begins inside ${\mathsf{R}}_0$. Since $A_T^\#$ has bounded length, its ${\mathfrak{z}}$-coordinate is uniformly bounded on $A_T^\#$. 

By  Proposition \ref{Prop-Var-Growth}, $V_n\asymp n$, therefore $\sigma_T\asymp\sqrt{\log T}$. By Lemmas \ref{Lemma-Modified-Approx-Canonical} and  \ref{Lemma-f(X)},  
$\displaystyle  |a_T(\widetilde{\omega})|\leq n\sup_k\|f_k\|_\infty+O(1)\leq C\log T$, with  $C$ independent of $\widetilde{\omega}$.
   
                                        
                                   
                                                                                                                               
               
                                                                                         



$D^{-a_T}\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0:A_T\to A_T^\#$ is an affine map, which carries the normalized length measure ${\mathbb{P}}_{A_T}$ on  $A_T$,  to the normalized length measure ${\mathbb{P}}_{A_T^\#}$  on $A_T^\#$. So 
\begin{align*}
&{\mathbb{P}}_{A_T}\left[\frac{{\mathfrak{z}}-a_T}{\sigma_T}\in (a,b)\right]=
{\mathbb{P}}_{A_T^\#}\left[\frac{{\mathfrak{z}}\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{0}^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1}\circ D^{a_T}-a_T}{\sigma_T}\in (a,b)\right]\\
&\overset{!}{=}{\mathbb{P}}_{A_T^\#}\left[\frac{{\mathfrak{z}}\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{0}^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1}}{\sigma_T}\in (a,b)\right] ={\mathbb{P}}_{A_T^\#}\left[\frac{\Xi_n+{\mathfrak{z}}}{\sqrt{V_n}}\in (a,b)\right].
\end{align*}
(The marked identity holds because  $\widetilde{\psi}_i\circ D=D\circ\widetilde{\psi}_i$ and ${\mathfrak{z}}\circ D={\mathfrak{z}}+1$).

Fix $\delta>0$ arbitrarily small, and choose pure $E^s_n$-segments $W_{n,1},\ldots,W_{n,m_n+2}$ with depth $k$ as in Lemma \ref{l.approx-by-pure-segments}. Since $W_{n,i}$ have fixed depth, $|W_{n,i}|$ is  bounded away from zero and infinity. Since  $\overline{W}_{n,i}\cap\overline{A}_T^\#\neq \varnothing$ and ${\mathfrak{z}}$ is uniformly bounded on $A_T^\#$, ${\mathfrak{z}}$ is uniformly bounded on $W_{n,i}$. Thus by Lemmas \ref{l.trivial-prob-fact} and \ref{Lemma-Pure-Seg-CLT}, 
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}\left[\frac{\Xi_n+{\mathfrak{z}}}{\sqrt{V_n}}\in (a,b)\right]=\lim_{n\to\infty}{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}\left[\frac{\Xi_n}{\sqrt{V_n}}\in (a,b)\right]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_a^b e^{-t^2/2}dt.
$$
Invoking parts (3) and (4) of Lemma \ref{l.approx-by-pure-segments}, we obtain that for all $T$ large enough, 
$$
\frac{1-2\delta}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_a^b e^{-t^2/2}dt\leq 
{\mathbb{P}}_{A_T^\#}\left[\frac{\Xi_n+{\mathfrak{z}}}{\sqrt{V_n}}\in (a,b)\right]\leq  \frac{1+2\delta}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_a^b e^{-t^2/2}dt.
$$
Thus  ${\mathbb{P}}_{A_T}\left[\frac{{\mathfrak{z}}-a_T}{\sigma_T}\in (a,b)\right]={\mathbb{P}}_{A_T^\#}\left[\frac{\Xi_n+{\mathfrak{z}}}{\sqrt{V_n}}\in (a,b)\right]\xrightarrow[T\to\infty]{}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_a^b e^{-t^2/2}dt$.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
We  use the notation of the previous proof. 
Let ${\widetilde{\omega}}_0$ denote the singularity at the middle of the top side of ${\mathsf{R}}_0$,  let $T_n:=n$, and set 
$
 A_n:= \frac{1}{2} a_{T_n}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)\ , \ B_n:= \frac{1}{2}\sigma_{T_n}.
$

Recall that $D_N(\alpha)$ takes values in $\frac{1}{2}\mathbb Z$.  By \eqref{e.Lin-Flow-1}, 
\begin{align*}
&\frac{1}{n} \#\{1\leq N\leq n: \frac{D_N(\alpha)-A_n}{B_n}\in (a,b)\}=\sum_{\xi\in \frac{1}{2}\mathbb Z,\frac{\xi-A_N}{B_N}\in (a,b) }\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!(1/n) \#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha)=\xi\}\\
&=\sum_{\xi\in\frac{1}{2}\mathbb Z,\frac{\xi-A_N}{B_N}\in (a,b) }\frac{1}{T_n}\int_{-1}^{T_n-1}{ 1_{\{2\xi\}}}({\mathfrak{z}}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)))dt
=\frac{1}{T_n}\int_{-1}^{T_n-1}1_{(a,b)}\left(\frac{{\mathfrak{z}}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}_0))/2-A_n}{B_n}\right)dt\\
&={\mathbb{P}}_{A_{T_n}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)}\left[\frac{{\mathfrak{z}}-2A_n}{2B_n}\in (a,b)\right]+O(T_n^{-1})
={\mathbb{P}}_{A_{T_n}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)}\left[\frac{{\mathfrak{z}}-a_{T_n}}{\sigma_{T_n}}\in (a,b)\right]+o(1).
\end{align*}
Thus,  by Theorem \ref{ThStairTLT}, $\frac{1}{n} \#\{1\leq N\leq n: \frac{D_N(\alpha)-A_n}{B_n}\in (a,b)\}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_a^b e^{-t^2/2}dt$.  
 Since $|a_T|\leq C\log T$ and $B_T\asymp\sqrt{\log T}$, $A_n=O(\log n)$ and $B_n\asymp\sqrt{\log n}$, giving us Theorem \ref{t.A_n-B_n-estimates}. 
 
 Next,  $A_n=\frac{1}{2}a_{T_n}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)=\frac{1}{2} z_{k_n N_0}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)$, where $k_n=n(T_n)$ is the minimal integer such that $\lambda^s_0\cdots\lambda^s_{k_n-1} T_n\in [1,L]$, see \eqref{DefBrN}.  Thus,  $k_n\asymp \log n$, $k_n$ is non-decreasing, and  $k_{n+1}-k_n$ is bounded. 
Let $\nu_n:=k_nN_0$, then   Theorem \ref{ThDriftOfOrigin} (proved in Appendix \ref{Appendix-Twist}) says that  
$
\displaystyle A_n=\frac{1}{2} z_{\nu_n}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)=\frac{1}{2}{\mathfrak{z}}_{k_n}
=\frac{1}{4}\sum_{j=1}^{\nu_n}[\operatorname{sgn}(m_{2j})-\operatorname{sgn}(m_{2j-1})].
$
Theorem \ref{t.A_n} follows.\hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-3 -->
<!-- lem-31: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-Pure-Seg-LLT}
                                                        
 Let $W_n$ be a sequence of pure $E^s_n$-segments  with heights $h_n$, and length bounded below.   Fix $C:=\<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}\>\neq \varnothing$.  If $k_n\in\mathbb Z, t\in\mathbb R$, and  $\frac{k_n-h_n}{\sqrt{V_n}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}t$, then 
$$
{\mathbb{P}}_{W_n}\left\{{\widetilde{\omega}}:\begin{array}{c}
({\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}}))\in C\\
\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0[(\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})({\widetilde{\omega}})]=k_n
 \end{array}
\right\}=[1+o(1)]\frac{e^{-t^2/2}\mu_0(C)}{\sqrt{2\pi V_n}},\textrm{ as }n\to\infty.
$$
<!-- end lem-31 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
As in the proof of Lemma \ref{Lemma-Pure-Seg-CLT}, it is sufficient to consider the case when the depth of  $W_n$ is constant, equal to  $d$. 
Then each $W_n$ projects to a maximal $E^s_n$-segment in some cylinder $\<b_{n-d}^{(n)},\ldots,\dot{b}_n\>$. 

Let 
$E_n:=\{{\widetilde{\omega}}\in W_n: ({\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}}))\in C, \widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0[(\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})({\widetilde{\omega}})]=k_n
\}.$
By assumption, $\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n=h_n$ on $W_n$. By the definition of the jump functions and  \eqref{e.X-new}, on $W_n$, 
$$
\sum_{j=1}^{n}f_j[X^{(n)}_j(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}}))]=\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n({\widetilde{\omega}})-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0[(\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})({\widetilde{\omega}})]=h_n-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0[(\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})({\widetilde{\omega}}).
$$
It follows that 
$\displaystyle
E_n=\left\{{\widetilde{\omega}}\in W_n:\begin{array}{l}
X^{(n)}_i(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}}))=a_i\textrm{ for }i=0,\ldots,k-1\\
\displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^{n}f_j[X^{(n)}_j(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}}))]=h_n-k_n
\end{array} \right\}.
$
We conclude that  $E_n$ is an elementary event in the sense of Definition \ref{d.elementary}. Thus, by Lemma \ref{l.prob-of-elementry-event} and the Markov property,
\begin{align}
&{\mathbb{P}}_{W_n}(E_n)={\mathbb{P}}\left[S_n=h_n-k_n,\, X_1=a_1,\ldots,X_{k-1}=a_{k-1}\, \big|\, X_{n-d}=b_{n-d}^{(n)},\ldots,X_n=b_n^{(n)}\right]\notag\\
&={\mathbb{P}}[X_1=a_1,\ldots,X_{k-1}=a_{k-1}]\times\notag\\
&\hspace{0.7cm}{\mathbb{P}}\left[\sum_{i=k}^{n-d-1} f_i(X_i)=h_n-k_n-\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}f_i(a_i)-\sum_{i=n-d}^n f_i(b_i^{(n)})\, \bigg|\, X_{k-1}=a_{k-1}, X_{n-d}=b_{n-d}^{(n)}\right]\notag\\
&=\mu_0(C){\mathbb{P}}[S_{n'}'-\mathbb E(S_{n'}')=\delta_{n'}|X_0'=a_{k-1}, X_{n'}'=b_{n-d}^{(n)}],\label{e.Prob[S-n-prime]}
\end{align}
 where   $n'=n-d-k$,  $X_i'=X_{i+k-1}$,  $f_j'=f_{j+k-1}$, 
 $\displaystyle S_{n'}'=\sum_{j=1}^{n'}f_j'(X_j')$, and 
$$\delta_{n'}:=h_n-k_n-\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}f_i(a_i)-\sum_{i=n-d}^n f_i(b_i^{(n)})-\left(\mathbb E(S_{n-d-1})-\mathbb E(S_{k-1})\right)=h_n-k_n+O(1).$$

A calculation using  Corollary  \ref{Cor-rho-mixing} shows that  $V_{n'}':={\rm Var}(S_{n'}')\sim V_n$. 
Thus  
$\frac{\delta_{n'}}{\sqrt{V_{n'}'}}\to -t$. 

Now we apply that the  mixing local limit theorem (Theorem \ref{ThLLTArrays}) to the Markov chain 
$(X_i)_{i\geq k-1}$ 
{started from $X_{k-1}=a_{k-1}$ and conditioned on $X_{n-d}=b_{n-d}.$
The conditioned chain has transition probabilities
\begin{equation}
\label{CondChain}
 \pi_{i, i+1}^{b_{n-d}}(a_i, a_{i+1})=\pi_{i, i+1}(a_i, a_{i+1}) 
\frac{{\mathbb{P}}(X_{n-d}=b_{n-d}|X_{i+1}=a_{i+1})}{{\mathbb{P}}(X_{n-d}=b_{n-d}|X_{i}=a_{i})}
\end{equation}
The conditions of Theorem \ref{ThLLTArrays} are all satisfied.
First, $f_i$ are uniformly bounded by Lemma \ref{Lemma-f(X)}.
Next, uniform ellipticity, irreducibility and the hereditary property for the unconditioned chain 
hold  by Propositions \ref{Prop-Doeblin}, \ref{Prop-Irred} and Lemma \ref{l.hereditary}.
The conditioned chain enjoys the same property because the second factor in \eqref{CondChain}
is uniformly bounded from above and away from zero due to Proposition  \ref{Prop-Markov-Kernel}(4) and 
the uniform ellipticity of the unconditioned chain
(or by $\phi$-mixing given by Corollary \ref{Cor-phi-mixing}). 
Theorem \ref{ThLLTArrays} gives the asymptotic behavior of \eqref{e.Prob[S-n-prime]}, and  the lemma follows.
}
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- lem-32: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-Constant-Ratio}
There exist $\delta_k\to 0$ as $k\to\infty$
such that for each $\widetilde{C}_\ell\in\mathfs C_k$ and for every maximal $E^s_0$-segment $W\subset \mathrm{int}(\widetilde{C}_\ell)$,  
\begin{equation}\label{e.constant-ratio}
\left|\frac{|W\cap{{\mathsf{R}}}_0|}{|W|}-\frac{\mu_0(\widetilde{C}_\ell\cap{{\mathsf{R}}}_0)}{\mu_0(\widetilde{C}_\ell)}
\right|<\delta_k.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lem-32 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
Suppose $\widetilde{C}_\ell\in \mathfs C_k$, where $C=\<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}\>$. 
By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Cylinder-Area}, $C$ and  $\widetilde{C}_\ell$ are rectangles  with sides parallel to $E^s_0$ and $E^u_0$; The $E^s_0$-side has length   $\ell^s(a_0)\geq c^{-1}>0$; and the $E^u_0$-side has length $\ell^u(a_{k-1})/\prod_{i=0}^{k-2}\lambda_i^u\leq c \lambda^{-k}$.  Here $c>1$ is some  constant independent of   $k$,$\ell$,  $a_1,\ldots,a_{k-1}$, and coming from Lemma \ref{Lemma-Partition}(10).

Since $E^s_0\parallel {\beta\choose 1}$, the angle between $E^s_0$ and the vertical side of ${\mathsf{R}}_0$ is $\theta:=\tan^{-1}(\beta)$.
By Euclidean geometry, for any maximal $E^s_0$-segments $W,W'$ in $\widetilde{C}_\ell$ parallel to $E^s_0$, 
$$
\big| |W\cap{\mathsf{R}}_0|-|W'\cap{\mathsf{R}}_0|\big|\leq 2c\lambda^{-k}\tan\theta\textrm{ and }|W|=|W'|=\ell^s(\widetilde{C}_\ell)\geq c^{-1}.
$$
So $\displaystyle \left|
\frac{|W\cap{\mathsf{R}}_0|}{|W|}-\frac{|W'\cap{\mathsf{R}}_0|}{\ell^s(\widetilde{C}_\ell)}
\right|<2c^2\beta\lambda^{-k}.
$ Keeping $W$ fixed and integrating over $W'$ intersecting  the $E^u_0$-side, we obtain
$
\left|\frac{|W|\cap{\mathsf{R}}_0|}{|W|}\ell^u(\widetilde{C}_\ell)-\frac{\textrm{Area}(\widetilde{C}_\ell\cap{\mathsf{R}}_0)}{\ell^s(\widetilde{C}_\ell)}
\right|<2c^2\beta\lambda^{-k}\ell^u(\widetilde{C}_\ell).
$
Dividing by $\ell^u(\widetilde{C}_\ell)$, we obtain the lemma (since $E^u_0\perp E^s_0$).
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- head-4: body_md -->
Given integers $k_T$,  let  
$
\mathfrak m_T(\widetilde{\omega},k_T):=\frac{1}{T}\mathrm{mes}\left\{t\in (0,T): \phi^t(\widetilde{\omega})\in{{\mathsf{R}}}_{k_T}\right\}
$, where $\textrm{mes}$ is Lebesgue's measure.  {We need to show that}
  if $\frac{k_T-a_T({\widetilde{\omega}})}{\sigma_T}\to s$, then 
  $
  \sqrt{2\pi\sigma_T^2}\times\mathfrak{m}_T(\widetilde{\omega},k_T)\to e^{-\frac{1}{2}s^2}.
  $
   
We use the notation of the proof of the temporal CLT in \S\ref{ScProofBeck}.
Write $A_T=A_T'\uplus E$, where $A_T'$ projects to a  union of maximal $E^s_0$-segments in $\mathfrak P_0$-elements, and $E$ (an edge effect) is contained in a union of at most two such pieces. Then 
$$
\mathfrak m_T(\widetilde{\omega}_0,k_T)=\frac{|A_T'\cap {{\mathsf{R}}}_{k_T}|}{|A_T|}+O(T^{-1}).
$$

Fix  $T$ and $k$ arbitrarily large, and consider the collection  $\{D^{k_T}(\widetilde{C}_\ell):\widetilde{C}_\ell\in\mathfs C_k, \ell\in\mathbb Z\}$. This is a pairwise disjoint cover of ${{\mathsf{R}}}_{k_T}$, therefore, 
\begin{align*}
\mathfrak m_T(\widetilde{\omega}_0,k_T)&=
\sum_{\widetilde{C}_\ell\in\mathfs C_k}\frac{|A_T'\cap D^{k_T}(\widetilde{C}_\ell)\cap {{\mathsf{R}}}_{k_T}| }{|A_T|}+O(T^{-1}).
\end{align*}
Write $\displaystyle A_T'\cap D^{k_T}(\widetilde{C}_\ell)=\biguplus_i D^{k_T}(W_i)$, where $W_i$ are maximal $E^s_0$-segments in  $\widetilde{C}_\ell$, then 
\begin{align*}
&|A_T'\cap D^{k_t}(\widetilde{C}_\ell)\cap {{\mathsf{R}}}_{k_T}|=\sum_i |D^{k_T}(W_i\cap{{\mathsf{R}}}_0)|\\
&=\sum_i \frac{|D^{k_T}(W_i\cap{{\mathsf{R}}}_0)|}{|D^{k_T}(W_i)|}\times |D^{k_T}(W_i)|=\sum_i \frac{|W_i\cap{{\mathsf{R}}}_0|}{|W_i|}\times |D^{k_T}(W_i)|\\
&=\left(\frac{\mu_0(\widetilde{C}_\ell\cap{{\mathsf{R}}}_0)}{\mu_0(\widetilde{C}_\ell)}\pm\delta_k\right)
|A_T'\cap D^{k_T}(\widetilde{C}_\ell)|, \textrm{ see Lemma \ref{Lemma-Constant-Ratio}.}
\end{align*}

Dividing by $|A_T|$, and summing over $\widetilde{C}_\ell\in\mathfs C_k$,  we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{e.8.6}
\mathfrak m_T(\widetilde{\omega}_0,k_T)=\frac{|A_T'|}{|A_T|}\sum_{\widetilde{C}_\ell\in\mathfs C_k}
\left(\frac{\mu_0(\widetilde{C}_\ell\cap{{\mathsf{R}}}_0)}{\mu_0(\widetilde{C}_\ell)}\pm\delta_k\right)
\left(\frac{|A_T'\cap D^{k_T}(\widetilde{C}_\ell)|}{|A_T'|}\right)+O(T^{-1}).
\end{equation}
The term $O(T^{-1})$ equals $|E\cap{{\mathsf{R}}}_{k_T}|/|A_T|$, and is uniform in $k$ and $k_T$.



Fix $C=\<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}\>$ such that $\widetilde{C}_\ell\in\mathfs C_k$.
In \S \ref{ScProofBeck}, we constructed 
  an integer\\ $n=n(|A_T'|)\asymp \log |A_T'|\asymp\log T$ such that 
$
A_T^\ast:=(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(A_T')\textrm{ has length in }[1,L],
$
where $L$ is a global constant. Then
\begin{align*}
\frac{|A_T'\cap D^{k_T}(\widetilde{C}_\ell)|}{|A_T'|}&={\mathbb{P}}_{A_T'}\{\widetilde{\omega}:\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0(\widetilde{\omega})=k_T+\ell,\ 
\pi(\widetilde{\omega})\in \<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}\>\}\\
&=
{\mathbb{P}}_{A_T^\ast}\left[
\begin{array}{c}
\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0\circ \widetilde{\psi}_{0}^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1}=k_T+\ell;\\
 X^{(n)}_i\circ\pi=a_i\ (i=0,\ldots,k-1)
 \end{array} \right].
\end{align*}

We calculate this probability by first approximating $A_T^\ast$ by pure $E^s_n$-segments $W_i$ of arbitrarily large (but constant) depth $d$ as in Lemma \ref{l.approx-by-pure-segments}, and then applying Lemma \ref{Lemma-Pure-Seg-LLT}.  
Since all points in $A_T^\ast$ have ${\mathfrak{z}}$-coordinate $a_T({\widetilde{\omega}})+O(L)$, each $W_i$ has height $a_T({\widetilde{\omega}})+O(L)$, and  we obtain the following consequence: If $\frac{k_T-a_T}{\sigma_T}\xrightarrow[T\to\infty]{}s$, then 
$$
\frac{|A_T'\cap D^{k_T}(\widetilde{C}_\ell)|}{|A_T'|}=[1+o(1)]\frac{e^{-\frac{1}{2}s^2}\mu_0(\widetilde{C}_\ell)}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_T^2}}.
$$
Substituting this in \eqref{e.8.6}, and recalling that $|{\mathfs C}_k|<\infty$, we see that 
\begin{align*}
&\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_T^2}\times\mathfrak{m}_T(\widetilde{\omega}_0,k_T)
=(e^{-\frac{1}{2}s^2}+o(1))\sum_{ \widetilde{C}_\ell\in\mathfs C_k}[\mu_0(\widetilde{C}_\ell\cap{{\mathsf{R}}}_0)\pm\delta_k \mu_0(\widetilde{C}_\ell)]+O\left(\frac{\sigma_T}{T}\right)\\
&=(e^{-\frac{1}{2}s^2}+o(1))\biggl[\mu_0({{\mathsf{R}}}_0)\pm\delta_k 
\mu_0\biggl( \bigcup_{\widetilde{C}_\ell\in\mathfs{C}_k} \widetilde{C}_\ell\biggr)\biggr]
+O\left(\frac{\sigma_T}{T}\right).
\end{align*}
Recall that $\mu_0({{\mathsf{R}}}_0)=1$,   $\mu_0(\bigcup\mathfs C_k)$ is uniformly bounded,   $\sigma_T=O(\sqrt{\log T})$, and  $\delta_k$ can be made arbitrarily small by choosing $k$ sufficiently large.  Thus, if $(k_T-a_T)/\sigma_T\to s$, then $\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_T^2}\times\mathfrak{m}_T(\widetilde{\omega}_0,k_T)\to e^{-\frac{1}{2}s^2}$, as required. 
\hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-4 -->
<!-- head-5: body_md -->
Let ${\widetilde{\omega}}_0$ denote the midpoint of  the top side of ${\mathsf{R}}_0$. Let $T_n:=n$,  and define as before  $A_n:=\frac{1}{2}a_{T_n}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)$ and $B_n:=\frac{1}{2}\sigma_{T_n}$. We saw above that  $A_n=O(\log n)$ and $B_n\asymp\sqrt{\log n}$.

Suppose $\xi_n\in\frac{1}{2}\mathbb Z$, and $\frac{\xi_n-A_n}{B_n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}t$. Then $\frac{2\xi_n-a_{T_n}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)}{\sigma_{T_n}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}t$, and
by \eqref{e.Lin-Flow-1}, 
\begin{align*}
\mathfrak{d}_n(\xi_n)&:= \#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha)=\xi_n\}=\mathrm{mes}\{-1<t<T_n-1: {\mathfrak{z}}(\phi^{t}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0))=2\xi_n \}\\
&=T_n\mathfrak{m}_{T_n}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0,2\xi_n)+O(1)=[1+o(1)]\frac{T_n e^{-t^2/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_{T_n}^2}}+O(1).
\end{align*}
Since  $B_n=\frac{1}{2}\sigma_{T_n}\asymp \sqrt{\log n}$, ${\mathfrak d}_n(\xi_n)=[1+o(1)]\frac{ne^{-t^2/2}}{\sqrt{8\pi B_n^2}}$, as stated in Theorem \ref{t.LLT-for-D_N}.
\hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-5 -->
<!-- lem-33: body_md -->
\label{LmAddPres}
For some $a_n\in\mathbb R$, 
there are unique 
 real-analytic  $p_n:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and unique parameterized families of functions  $h_n(\cdot, \xi):\mathfrak P_n\to\mathbb R^+$ $(\xi\in\mathbb R)$ such that 
  for all $n\in\
 \mathbb N\cup\{0\}$ and  $\xi\in\mathbb R$, 
 \begin{equation}
 \sum_x h_n(x, \xi) {\mathbb{P}}(X_n=x)=e^{a_n\xi},\   h_n(\cdot,0)\equiv 1, 
 \end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\label{e.eigenfunction}
\sum_{y\in\mathfrak P_{n+1}} e^{\xi f_{n+1}(y)}\pi_{n,n+1}(x,y) h_{n+1} (y, \xi)=e^{p_n(\xi)} h_n(x, \xi)\ \ (x\in\mathfrak P_n),  
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{e.p-prime-constraint}
\ p_i(0)=0,\ \textrm{ and } p_1'(0)+\cdots+p_n'(0)=\mathbb E(S_n).
\end{equation}
In addition, $h_i(\cdot,\xi)$ is real-analytic in $\xi$, and there are constants  $\mathsf{C}=\mathsf{C}(R)$ $(R\!>\!0)$ 
which depend only on $M(\beta)$ such that 
\begin{equation}
\displaystyle \frac{1}{\mathsf{C}}\leq h_n(\cdot,\xi)\leq \mathsf{C}, \textrm{ and }\quad |p_n(\xi)|\leq \mathsf{C} \textrm{ for  all
$n\in \mathbb{N}$ and $\xi\in [-R, R]$}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lem-33 -->
<!-- defi-10: body_md -->
The {\em change of measure} of $\{X_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ {\em with parameter $\xi$} is the Markov chain $\{\widetilde{X}^\xi_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ \index{Change of measure}  with   state spaces $\mathfrak P_k$,  initial distribution ${\mathbb{P}}[X_0=\cdot]$, and transition kernel 
\begin{equation}\label{ProbXi}
{\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}_{n+1}^\xi=y|\widetilde{X}_n^\xi=x]=\pi_{n,n+1}^\xi(x,y):=\frac{e^{\xi f_{n+1}(y)} h_{n+1}(y, \xi)}{e^{p_n(\xi)} h_n(x,\xi)}\pi_n(x,y).
\end{equation}
<!-- end defi-10 -->
<!-- lem-34: body_md -->
\label{l.V-n-xi}
For every $R>0$ \index{Change of measure!variance estimates}there exists $\mathsf C=\mathsf C(R)$ such that for all for all  $N$ large enough, for all $\xi\in [-R,R]$, $\mathsf C^{-1}\leq \widetilde{V}^\xi_N/V_N\leq \mathsf C$. For every ${\varepsilon}>0$ there exists $\xi^\ast({\varepsilon})>0$ such that for all $N$ large enough, for all $|\xi|\leq \xi^\ast$, $e^{-{\varepsilon}}\leq \widetilde{V}^\xi_N/V_N\leq e^{{\varepsilon}}$.
<!-- end lem-34 -->
<!-- lem-35: body_md -->
\label{l.uniform-Doeblin}
Suppose $M(\beta)\leq M$. \index{Uniform ellipticity}\index{Change of measure!uniform ellipticity}
For every $R$, there exists ${\varepsilon}_0(M,R)$ such that for every $\xi\in [-R,R]$, $\pi_n^\xi(\cdot,\cdot)$ is uniformly elliptic with  ellipticity constant ${\varepsilon}_0(R)$.
<!-- end lem-35 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{Prop-Doeblin}, $\pi_{n,n+1}$ is uniformly elliptic with ellipticity constant ${\varepsilon}_0(M)$. By Lemma \ref{Lemma-f(X)},  $f_n$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $M$, and  by Lemma \ref{LmAddPres}, there is a constant $\mathsf C(M,R)$ for which  $|p_n(\xi)|\leq \mathsf C(M,R)$ and $|\log h(\cdot,\xi)|\leq  \log\mathsf C(M,R)$ when $|\xi|\leq R$  (for the formula of this constant, see the proof of Lemma 7.14 in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book}). Now the lemma follows directly from the definition of $\pi_{n,n+1}^\xi$.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- lem-36: body_md -->
\label{LmPressure}
For each $R\!\!>\!\!0$, there is a constant $\mathsf{C}=\mathsf{C}(R)$, so that  for all $\xi\in [-R,R]$,
 \begin{equation}
\label{Pres0thDer}
\mathsf{P}_n(0)=0\textrm{ and }\left|\mathsf{P}_n(\xi)-\log\mathbb E(e^{\xi S_n})\right|\leq \mathsf{C}, 
\end{equation} 
 
\begin{equation}
\label{Pres1stDer}
\mathsf{P}_n'(0)=\mathbb E(S_n)\textrm{ and }\left|\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)-\widetilde{{\mathbb{E}}}^\xi (S_n)\right|\leq \mathsf{C}, 
\end{equation} 
\begin{equation}
\label{Pres1stDerLM}
 \left|\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)-\frac{d}{d\xi} \left[\log {\mathbb{E}}\left(e^{\xi S_n}\right)\right]  \right|\leq \mathsf{C}, 
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\label{Pres2dDer}
\frac{V_n-1}{\mathsf{C}}  \leq \mathsf{P}_n''(\xi)\leq \mathsf{C}[V_n+1] .
\end{equation}
<!-- end lem-36 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
Equations \eqref{Pres0thDer}--\eqref{Pres1stDerLM} are the content of parts 1,4 and 5 in Lemma 7.18 in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book}.   \eqref{Pres2dDer} follows from Lemma 7.17 in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book}, after noting that the function denoted there  by $\overline{P}_n$ differs from  $\mathsf{P}_n$ by a linear function.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- cor-15: body_md -->
Suppose there exists  $R>0$ such that  $z_n\in (\mathsf{P}_n'(-R),\mathsf{P}_n'(R))$, then for all $n$ large enough that $V_n>1$, there exists a unique $\xi_n\in\mathbb R$ such that $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)=z_n$. These $\xi_n$ satisfy
$
|z_n-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_n}(S_n)|\leq \mathsf C(R)\textrm{ and } |\xi_n|\leq R.
$
<!-- end cor-15 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{LmAddPres}, $\mathsf{P}_n(\xi)$ is real-analytic on $\mathbb R$. 
By Corollary \ref{Prop-Var-Growth},  $V_n>1$ for all  $n$ large. For such $n$, Equation \eqref{Pres2dDer} says that $\mathsf{P}_n(\xi)$ is strictly convex on $\mathbb R$. It follows that $\mathsf{P}_n'$ is continuous and strictly increasing.  Since
