$\mathsf{P}_n'(-R)<z_n<\mathsf{P}_n({R})$, there exists a unique $\xi_n$ such that $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)=z_n$, and $|\xi_n|<R$. By \eqref{Pres1stDer}, $|z_n-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_n}(S_n)|\leq \mathsf C(R)$.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- prop-10: body_md -->
\label{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}
Fix $z_k\in\mathbb R$, and integers $n_k\to\infty$, $0\leq \ell_k\leq N_0-1$,  $N_k=n_k N_0+\ell_k$.\index{Geometric pressure!and pressure} \index{Pressure!and geometric pressure}
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item For all $k$ large enough, there can be at most one $\xi_k$ such that $\mathcal P_{N_k}'(\xi_k)=z_k$, and at most one $\eta_k$ such that $\mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(\eta_k)=z_k$.
\item There is a bounded sequence of $\xi_k$ such that for all $k$ large enough $\mathcal P_{N_k}'(\xi_k)\!=\!z_k$ iff  there is  bounded sequence of $\eta_k$ such that for all $k$ large enough, $\mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(\eta_k)=z_k$. Moreover,  $|\xi_k-\eta_k|\to 0$. 
\item If $\mathcal P_{N_k}'(\xi_k)=\mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(\eta_k)$, then $\xi_k\to\infty$ iff $\eta_k\to\infty$, and $\xi_k\to-\infty$ iff $\eta_k\to-\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-10 -->
<!-- lem-37: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-is-it-really-this-hard-to-prove?}
There are constants  ${c(R)}, K(R)>0$ and   $C(k,R)$, $N(k,R)$ ($k\geq 1$) as follows. 
For all $k>K(R)$, $n>N(k,R)$ and $N$ such that  $\lfloor N/N_0\rfloor=n$,
$$
\mathcal P_{N}'(\xi)=
e^{\pm c(R)\lambda^{-k}}\bigl(\mathsf{P}_{n}'(\xi)\pm C(k,R)\bigr), \ \textrm{ whenever }|\xi|\leq R.
$$
<!-- end lem-37 -->
<!-- sublem-1: body_md -->
\label{sl.small-xi}
Let $r(k):=1/(2B_0\lambda^k)$,  $C:=\mathsf C(1)+B_0 e^{2B_0}$, { where $\mathsf{C}(R)$ comes from 
Lemma \ref{LmPressure},} and let $K_0:=|\log_\lambda(2B_0)|+1$. Then for all $k>K_0$, for all $|\xi|\leq r(k)$,
$$
\mathcal P_{N}'(\xi)={}e^{\pm\lambda^{-k}}\left(\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)\pm C\right).$$
<!-- end sublem-1 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
$\displaystyle \mathcal P_N'(\xi)=\frac{\int\, e^{\xi\Upsilon_{N}}\Upsilon_N d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}{\int\,e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}=\frac{\int\, e^{\xi\Upsilon_{N}}(\overline{S}_n\pm B_0)d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}{\int\,e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}=
\frac{\int\, e^{\xi\Upsilon_{N}}\overline{S}_n\, d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} }{\int\, e^{\xi\Upsilon_{N}}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\pm B_0$
\begin{align}
&=e^{\pm 2B_0|\xi|}\frac{\int\, e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}{\int\,e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\pm B_0
=e^{\pm 2B_0|\xi|}\frac{d}{d\xi}
\left(\log\mathbb E(e^{\xi \overline{S}_n})\right)\pm B_0\notag\\
&=e^{\pm 2B_0|\xi|}(\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)\pm\mathsf C(r))\pm B_0, \textrm{ by \eqref{Pres1stDerLM} and since $\overline{S}_n=S_n$ in distribution.}\label{e.pre-factor}
\end{align}
If   $r(k):=(2B_0\lambda^k)^{-1}$, then $2B_0|\xi|\leq \lambda^{-k}$. If $k>K_0$, then $r(k)<1$, so $\mathsf C(r)$ can be replaced by $\mathsf C(1)$.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- sublem-2: body_md -->
\label{sl.A}
There exist a constant $c_0(R)>0$ and $\overline{\mathcal F}_0^k$-measurable real-valued  functions  $A_{k,\xi}$ on ${\mathsf{R}}_0$ such that for all $\xi\in [-R,R]$ and $k\in\mathbb N$,
$$
\mathbb E(e^{-\xi\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0}|\overline{\mathcal F}_0^\infty)(x)=e^{\pm c_0(R)\lambda^{-k}}A_{k,\xi}(x).
$$
<!-- end sublem-2 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
By identity \eqref{e.conditional-expect-id}, 
it is sufficient to find $c_0(R)>0$ such that for every $\xi\in[-R,R]$ and  $k\in\mathbb N$,  if $x,y\in{{\mathsf{R}}}_0$ and  $\pi(x),\pi(y)$ are  in the same $\mathfrak P_0^k$-atom, then 
$$
e^{- c_0(R)\lambda^{-k} }\leq {\frac{1}{|W_0^s(x)|}\int_{W^s_0(x)} e^{-\xi\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0}ds}\bigg/
{\frac{1}{|W_0^s(y)|}\int_{W^s_0(y)} e^{-\xi\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0}ds}\leq e^{c_0(R)\lambda^{-k} }.
$$
 
By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Modified-Approx-Canonical}, ${{\mathsf{R}}}_0$  intersects at most finitely many copies of $\widetilde{F}_0:=[\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0=0]$; therefore $\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0$ attains finitely many different values $z_1,\ldots,z_\nu$ on ${\mathsf{R}}_0$.  
Partition ${\mathsf{R}}_0$ into the pieces $H_1,\ldots,H_\nu$ where $\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0|_{H_i}=z_i$. Then
$$
\frac{1}{|W^s_0(x)|}\int_{W^s_0(x)} e^{-\xi\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0}ds=\sum_{j=1}^{\nu} e^{-\xi z_j}\frac{|W^s_0(x)\cap H_j|}{|W^s_0(x)|}.
$$
$H_j$ are polygons, bounded by linear segments which are either horizontal, or vertical, or parallel to $E^u_0$ or $E^s_0$.
If $\pi(x),\pi(y)$ are in the same atom  $B\in\mathfrak{P}_0^k$, then $W^s_0(x),W^s_0(y)$ are two $E^s_0$-segments with the same length, and their distance is bounded above by $O(\lambda^{-k})$ (because the width of $B$ in the $E^u_0$ direction is $O(\lambda^{-k})$). It follows that 
$$
\bigl||W^s_0(x)\cap H_j|-|W^s_0(y)\cap H_j|\bigr|=O(\lambda^{-k}) \textrm{ uniformly in $j$, $k$, $x$, and $y$.}
$$

Since $\pi(x),\pi(y)$ are in the same $\mathfrak P_0^k$-atom, they are in the same $\mathfrak P_0$-atom, and therefore $|W^s_0(x)|=|W^s_0(y)|$. Moreover, this quantity is bounded away from zero and infinity, because it equals $\ell^s(a)$ for some $a\in \mathfrak P_0$. 
It follows that 
$$
\biggl|\frac{|W^s_0(x)\cap H_j|}{|W^s_0(x)|}-\frac{|W^s_0(y)\cap H_j|}{|W^s_0(y)|}\biggr|=O(\lambda^{-k}) \textrm{ uniformly in $j$, $x$, and $y$,}
$$
whence $|\frac{1}{|W^s_0(x)|}\int_{W^s_0(x)} e^{-\xi\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0}ds-\frac{1}{|W^s_0(y)|}\int_{W^s_0(y)} e^{-\xi\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0}ds|=O(\lambda^{-k})$, uniformly in $x,y$. 
By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Modified-Approx-Canonical},  $\frac{1}{|W^s_0(y)|}\int_{W^s_0(y)} e^{-\xi\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0}ds$ is  bounded away from zero. The  result follows.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- sublem-3: body_md -->
\label{sl.non-eccentric}
There are constants $M_0$ and $m(k)\geq 0$ ($k\geq 0$) such that every cylinder $\<a_{n-k},\ldots,\dot{a}_n\>$ with $n>k$ can be written as a finite disjoint union of cylinders 
$C'=\<a_{n-k},\ldots,\dot{a}_n,c_{n+1},\ldots,c_{n+m}\>$ so that $m\leq m(k)$
and 
\begin{equation}\label{e.nearly-square}
M_0^{-1}\leq \ell^s(C')/\ell^u(C')\leq M_0.
\end{equation}
<!-- end sublem-3 -->
<!-- sublem-4: body_md -->
\label{s.D-n-k}
There exists $c_1>0$ and a $\widetilde{\mathfrak D}_{N,k}$-measurable set $D_{N,k}$ such that $\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_{n,\ell}$ is constant 
on the interiors of sets in $\widetilde{\mathfrak D}_{N,k}^\ast:=\{D\in \widetilde{\mathfrak D}_{N,k}:D\subset D_{N,k}\}$, and  for every $\widetilde{A}\in\widetilde{\mathfrak P}_0^n:=\{\pi|_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}^{-1}(C): C\in\mathfrak P_0^n\}$, 
\begin{equation}\label{e.much-better-D_n-small}
\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\widetilde{A}\cap D_{N,k}^c)\leq c_1\lambda^{-k} \mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\widetilde{A}).
\end{equation}
<!-- end sublem-4 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Every $D'\in\widetilde{\mathfrak D}_{N,k}$ has the form 
\begin{equation}\label{e.D-form}
D'=\pi|_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}^{-1}((\psi_{0}^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\psi_{n-1}^{-1})(C)), \textrm{ where } 
C=\<a_{n-k},\ldots,\dot{a}_n,\ldots,a_{n+m}\>.
\end{equation}
The 
 discontinuities of  $\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n$ are located in $\displaystyle \bigcup_{i\in\mathbb Z} D^i(\partial\widetilde{F}_n)$, where 
$\widetilde{F}_n=[\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n=0]$. 
Clearly,  
$(\psi_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ \psi_0)(\mathrm{int}(C))\subset \mathrm{int}(a_n)\subset \mathrm{int}(\pi(\widetilde{F}_n))$, and 
$$(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ \cdots \circ \widetilde{\psi}_0)(\mathrm{int}(D'))\cap \bigcup_{i\in\mathbb Z} D^i(\partial\widetilde{F}_n)=\varnothing.$$ 
It follows that  $\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0$ is constant on the interior of $D'$. 

Thus, all the discontinuities   of $\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_{n,\ell}$ on $\mathfrak D_{N,k}$-atoms are due to jumps in the values  of ${\mathfrak{z}}\circ\widetilde{\Psi}_N$. These occur in 
$(\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})(\widetilde{\varphi}_{n,\ell}^{-1}\mathfs S)$, where 
$
{\mathfs S}$ is  the union of boundaries of the  horizontal rectangles.

Recall that $\widetilde{\varphi}_{n,\ell}\in\mathcal E$, where $\mathcal E$ is a {\em finite} set, independent of $N,\ell$. Let 
$
\displaystyle \widetilde{\mathfs S}:=\bigcup_{\widetilde{\varphi}\in\mathcal E}\widetilde{\varphi}^{-1} \mathfs S,
$
and 
let $\widetilde{\mathfrak D}_{N,k}^\ast$ denote the collection of sets in $\widetilde{\mathfrak D}_{N,k}$ whose $\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0$-images do {\em not} intersect $\widetilde{\mathfs S}$. Let $D_{N,k}:=$union of  $\widetilde{\mathfrak D}_{N,k}^\ast$. By the previous paragraph,  $\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_{n,\ell}$ is constant on the interior of every element of $\widetilde{\mathfrak D}_{N,k}^\ast$. It remains to prove \eqref{e.much-better-D_n-small}. 




Fix some $\widetilde{A}\in\widetilde{\mathfrak P}_0^n$, and some $\widetilde{D}\in\widetilde{\mathfrak D}_{N,k}$ which intersects it. Let $A:=\pi(\widetilde{A})$ and $D:=\pi(\widetilde{D})$ and write $A=\<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_n\>$ and 
$D=(\psi_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\psi_{n-1}^{-1})(C)$, 
with $C\!\!=\!\!\<c_{n-k},\ldots,\dot{c}_n,\ldots,c_{n+m}\>$ non-eccentric, and 
$m\!\!\leq\!\!m(k)$.  Necessarily $a_{n-k}\!\!=\!\!c_{n-k},\ldots,a_n\!\!=\!\! c_n$, and 
$
A\cap D=\<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_{n},c_{n+1},\ldots,c_{n+m}\>.
$
Let $C':=\<\dot{a}_n,c_{n+1},\ldots,c_{n+m}\>$. Then 
$$
\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\widetilde{A}\cap\widetilde{D})=\mu_0(A\cap D)\overset{!}{=}\frac{\mu_0(A)\mu_0(C')}{\mu_0(a_n)}\leq G^{-1}\mu_0(A)\mu_0(C')=G^{-1}\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\widetilde{A})\mu_0(C'),
$$
where $G:=\inf\{\mu_0(a): a\in \mathfrak P_n, n\in\mathbb N\}$ (a positive constant,  by Proposition \ref{Prop-Markov-Kernel}). The marked equality follows easily from the identity 
$$\mu_0(A\cap D)={\mathbb{P}}[X_0=a_0,\ldots,X_n=a_n,X_{n+1}=c_{n+1},\ldots,X_{n+m}=c_{n+m}],
$$
(see Proposition \ref{Prop-Markov-Kernel}), and the rules for calculating probabilities for Markov chains.


$C'$ is a parallelogram with sides parallel to $E^s_n$, $E^u_n$. By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Cylinder-Area}, $\ell^u(C')=\ell^u(C)$, and $\ell^s(C')=\ell^s(a_n)$.  
Recalling that $\mu_0=\frac{1}{2}\times$ Euclidean area measure, we find that  
$\mu_0(C')=\frac{1}{2}\ell^s(a_n)\ell^u(C)|\sin\measuredangle(E^u_n,E^s_n)|\leq \ell^s(a_n)\ell^u(C)$. 

By non-eccentricity and Lemma  \ref{Lemma-Cylinder-Area}, 
\begin{align*}
\mu_0(C')                                                                                               
  
\leq M_0 \ell^s(a_n) \ell^s(C)                                                          
\leq M_0\ell^s(a_n)\ell^s(c_{n-k})\lambda^s_{n-k}\cdots\lambda^s_1.                                              
   
                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                           
\end{align*}
Since $\lambda^s_i\leq \lambda^{-1}<1$ and  $\sup\{\ell^s(a): a\in \mathfrak P_n, n\geq 1\}<\infty$, there is global constant $c_1'$ such that $\mu_0(C')\leq c_1'\lambda^{-k}$. Taking $c_1'':=G^{-1}c_1'$, we find that 
$
\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\widetilde{A}\cap\widetilde{D})\leq c_1''\lambda^{-k}\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\widetilde{A}) 
$.
Summing over all $\widetilde{D}\in\mathfrak D_{N,k}$ inside $D_{N,k}^c$ such that $\mu_0(\widetilde{A}\cap\widetilde{D})\neq 0$, we obtain 
\begin{equation}\label{e.sum-of-sqrts}
\frac{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\widetilde{A}\cap D_{N,k}^c)}{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\widetilde{A})}\leq c_1''\lambda^{-k} \#\{\widetilde{D}\in \mathfrak D_{N,k}\setminus \mathfrak D_{N,k}^\ast: \mu_0(\widetilde{D}\cap\widetilde{A})\neq 0\}.
\end{equation}

It remains to bound the number of $\widetilde{D}\in \mathfrak D_{N,k}\setminus \mathfrak D_{N,k}^\ast$ such that $\mu_0(\widetilde{D}\cap\widetilde{A})\neq 0$.
Each $\widetilde{D}$ like that equals $\pi|_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}^{-1}((\psi_{0}^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\psi_{n-1}^{-1})(C))$, where $C=\<a_{n-k},\ldots,\dot{a}_n,c_{n+1},\ldots,c_{n+m}\>$, $C$ is non-eccentric, and $C$ intersects $\pi(\widetilde{\mathfs{S}})$. Moreover different sets $\widetilde{D}$ are represented by disjoint sets  $C$. We will bound the number of  $C$.


By  Lemma \ref{Lemma-Psi-and-Phi},  $\pi(\widetilde{\mathfs S})$ is made of a bounded number of line segments, with slopes uniformly bounded {\em away} from the slopes of $E^s_n,E^u_n$. By contrast, $A':=\<a_{n-k},\ldots,\dot{a}_n\>$ is a parallelogram with sides {\em parallel} to $E^s_n,E^u_n$. 
Because of this uniform transversality, 
$\pi(\widetilde{\mathfs S})\cap A'$ is the union of  linear segments $\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_\nu$, with  lengths $O(\ell^s(A'))$. Since $\pi(\widetilde{\mathfs S})$ has finite length and $A'$ is has bounded geometry,  the number $\nu$  is bounded by some global constant $\nu_0$.

Choose one of the $E^u_n$ sides of $A'$, and let  $\mathrm{proj}^u_n$ denote the projection from $A'$ to this side, along the $E^s_n$ direction.  Then $\mathrm{proj}^u_n(A'\cap\pi(\widetilde{\mathfs S}))$ consists of $\nu$ $E^u_n$-segments $\Sigma^u_1,\ldots,\Sigma^u_\nu$ of length $O(\ell^s(A'))$.  

The sets $C$ we are counting are non-overlapping $(E^u_n,E^s_n)$-sub-parallelograms  of $A'$, which intersect 
$\pi(\widetilde{\mathfs S})$. Their projections to the $E^u_n$-side of $A_n'$ are non-overlapping $E^u_n$-segments of length $\ell^u(C)$, which intersect $\bigcup\Sigma^u_i$, 

By  Lemma \ref{Lemma-Cylinder-Area},  $\ell^s(C)\!\!=\!\!\ell^s(A')$, and by non-eccentricity, 
$\ell^u(C)\!\!\geq\!\! M_0^{-1}\ell^s(C)\!\!=\!\! M_0^{-1}\ell^s(A')$. 
Length considerations reveal that each $\Sigma_i^u$ can intersect at most
$
\frac{|\Sigma^u_i|}{M_0^{-1}\ell^s(A')}+2
$
$E^u_n$-sides of  sets $C$. So the total number of $C$ is at most
$$
\frac{|\Sigma^u_1|+\cdots+|\Sigma^u_\nu|}{M_0^{-1}\ell^s(A')}+2\nu\leq \frac{O(\ell^s(A'))}{M_0^{-1}\ell^s(A')}+2\nu_0\leq \nu_1,
$$
where $\nu_1$ is a global constant. Thus
$
\#\{\widetilde{D}\in \mathfrak D_{N,k}\setminus \mathfrak D_{N,k}^\ast: \mu_0(\widetilde{D}\cap\widetilde{A})\neq 0\}\leq \nu_1
$.

Now  \eqref{e.sum-of-sqrts} implies \eqref{e.much-better-D_n-small}.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- sublem-5: body_md -->
\label{sl.integral-ineq}
There exists $K_1(R),c_2(R), C_2(R)\!\!>\!\!1$ so that for all $k\geq K_1(R)$, $N\!\!>\!\!N_0 k$,   and $\xi\in [-R,R]\setminus\{0\}$,
 \begin{align}
&\int_{D_{N,k}^c}e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\, d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\leq c_2\lambda^{-k} \int e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\, d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0};\label{e.D_n-additional-small-denom}\\
&\int_{D_{N,k}^c \cap[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\, d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\leq c_2\lambda^{-k} \int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\, d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0};\label{e.D_n-small-denom}\\
&\bigg|\int\limits_{D_{N,k}^c\cap [\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\Upsilon_N d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\bigg|<c_2\lambda^{-k}\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\int\limits_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]\cap D_{N,k}}   \!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\! e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}|\Upsilon_N| d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}+C_2\int e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}. \label{e.D_n-small}
\end{align} 
In addition, for every $0<r<R$ there exists $N(r,R)$ such that for all  $n>N(r,R)$,
\begin{equation}\label{e.lalala}
\forall\xi\in[-R,R]\setminus[-r,r],\ \ \ \int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n<0]}e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}|\Upsilon_N|d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}<\int e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end sublem-5 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
$\overline{S}_n$ is constant on atoms of $\widetilde{\mathfrak P}_0^n$. Therefore, multiplying both sides of \eqref{e.much-better-D_n-small} by the constant value of  $e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}$  on each $\widetilde{A}\in \widetilde{\mathfrak P}_0^n$, and then summing over  $\widetilde{A}$, 
we obtain
$
\int_{D^c_{N,k}} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\leq c_1\lambda^{-k}\int e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}.
$

Similarly,  multiplying both sides of \eqref{e.much-better-D_n-small} by the constant value of  $e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}$ or $e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}|\overline{S}_n|$ on $\widetilde{A}$, and then summing over all the $\widetilde{A}\in\widetilde{\mathfrak P}_0^n$ such that  $\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0$ on $\widetilde{A}$, 
we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{e.better-D_n-small}
\begin{aligned}
&\int_{D_{N,k}^c\cap[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\, d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\leq c_1\lambda^{-k} 
\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}e^{\xi\overline{S}_n} \, d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0};\\
&\left|\int_{D_{N,k}^c\cap[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n\, d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\right|\leq c_1
\lambda^{-k} \left|\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}e^{\xi\overline{S}_n} \overline{S}_n\, d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\right|.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Since 
 $\displaystyle B_0=\sup_n\, \operatorname{ess\,sup}|\Upsilon_N-\overline{S}_n|<\infty$, 
 \eqref{e.D_n-additional-small-denom} and  \eqref{e.D_n-small-denom}  follow (with larger $c$).
 
To obtain  \eqref{e.D_n-small}, suppose for simplicity that $0<\xi<R$, then 
\begin{align}
&\int_{D_{N,k}^c\cap[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}
|\Upsilon_N|
\, d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\leq 
e^{B_0 R}\int_{D_{N,k}^c\cap[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}(\overline{S}_n+B_0) d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\notag\\ 
&\hspace{0.5cm}\leq e^{B_0 R}\int_{D_{N,k}^c\cap[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}+B_0 e^{B_0 R}\int_{D_{N,k}^c\cap [\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\notag \\
&\hspace{0.5cm}\leq c_1e^{B_0 R}\lambda^{-k}\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}+B_0 e^{B_0 R}c_1\lambda^{-k}\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\textrm{ by \eqref{e.better-D_n-small}}\notag\\
&\hspace{0.5cm}\leq c_1e^{2B_0 R}\lambda^{-k}\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\Upsilon_N d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}+2B_0 e^{2B_0 R}c_1\lambda^{-k}\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\notag\\
&\hspace{0.5cm}\leq c_1e^{2B_0 R}\lambda^{-k}\left[\int_{D_{N,k}^c\cap[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\Upsilon_N d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}+\int_{D_{N,k}\cap[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\Upsilon_N d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\right]\notag \\
&
\hspace{0.5cm}\hspace{8cm}+2B_0 e^{2B_0 R}c_1\lambda^{-k}\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\notag\\
&\hspace{0.5cm}\leq c_1e^{2B_0 R}\lambda^{-k}\left[\int_{D_{N,k}^c\cap[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\Upsilon_N} |\Upsilon_N| d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}+\int_{D_{N,k}\cap[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\Upsilon_n d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\right]\notag\\
&\hspace{0.5cm}\hspace{8cm}+2B_0 e^{2B_0 R}c_1\lambda^{-k}\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}
e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}.\notag
\end{align}
 
 
 
 
   
                                                         
             
                       
                                                 
                                              
     
                                                      
                                                                                             
                              
     
                                                        
                                                                                              
                                                                   
     
                                                         
                                                                                                    
                                
     
                                                                            
                                                                                 
                                                  
     
                                                                      
                                
     
                                                                            
                                                                                    
                                                  
     
                                                                      
                                 
   
Subtracting $c_1e^{2B_0 R}\lambda^{-k}\int_{D_{N,k}^c\cap[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]}e^{\xi\Upsilon_N} |\Upsilon_N| d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}$ from both sides, and dividing by \\$(1-c_1 e^{2B_0 R}\lambda^{-k})$, 
we obtain \eqref{e.D_n-small}, provided that
$
k>K_1(R):=\log_\lambda(2c_1e^{2B_0 R}).
$


We prove \eqref{e.lalala}. Suppose $\xi\in [-R,R]\setminus[-r,r]$. 
The left-hand-side of \eqref{e.lalala} is less than $\displaystyle \int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n<0]}
e^{\xi\overline{S}_n+|\xi|B_0}\left(\frac{|\xi\overline{S}_n|}{r}+B_0\right)d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}$. 

Since  $e^{t}|t|<1$ and $e^t\leq 1$ for all $ t\leq 0$, this integral is less than 
$$
e^{B_0 R}\left[\frac{1}{r}\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n<0]}
e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}|\xi\overline{S}_n|d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}+ B_0\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n<0]}
e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\right]\leq e^{B_0 R}\left(\frac{1}{r}+B_0\right).
$$

Next we  bound the right-hand-side of \eqref{e.lalala} from below. Recall that  $\overline{S}_n=S_n$ in distribution, therefore $\mathrm{Var}(\overline{S}_n)=V_n$. Set
$$\mathcal F_n(\xi):=\frac{1}{V_n}\log\mathbb E(e^{\xi\overline{S}_n})
=\frac{1}{V_n}\log\mathbb E(e^{\xi{S}_n}).$$ 

Recall that $\mathbb E(S_n)$ is bounded, and $V_n\to\infty$.  
By  Proposition \ref{PrFreeEn},
$\mathcal F_n(0)=0$, $\mathcal F_n'(0)=\mathbb E(\overline{S}_n)/V_n\to 0$, and  for some $N_1=N_1(R)$, $C_1=C_1(R)$ and all $\xi\in [-R,R]$, if $n>N_1$, then $\mathcal F_n''\geq C_1^{-1}$ on $[-R,R]$. So 
$$
\forall\xi\in [-R,R]\setminus[-r,r],\ \ \ \mathcal F_n(\xi)\geq \frac{\mathbb E(\overline{S}_n)}{V_n}\xi+\frac{1}{2C_1}\xi^2\geq \frac{r^2}{2C_1}-\frac{R|\mathbb E(S_n)|}{V_n}=\frac{r^2}{2C_1}-o(1).
$$
Thus $\exists N(r,R)$ such that for all $n>N(r,R)$, $\mathcal F_n(\xi)>\frac{r^2}{4C_1}$. It follows that
$$
\int e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\geq e^{-B_0}\int e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\geq \exp\left(\frac{r^2}{4C_1} V_n-B_0\right).
$$ 
Since $V_n\to\infty$, this is eventually larger than $e^{B_0 R}\left(\frac{1}{r}+B_0\right)$, proving \eqref{e.lalala}.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- sublem-6: body_md -->
\label{sl.Num-Denom}
For every $R>0$ there are constants  $c_3(R),C_3(k,R)$ $(k\geq 1)$  so that for all $k>K_3(R)$, $N>N_3(k,R)$, and $\xi\in [-R,R]\setminus[-r(k),r(k)]$, 
$$
\mathcal P_N'(\xi)=e^{\pm c_3(R)\lambda^{-k}}\left(\frac{\mathsf{Num}}{\mathsf{Denom}}\right)\pm C_3(k,R), \textrm{ where }
\displaystyle\mathsf{Num}:=\int_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_{k+1}^{n-k-1} A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0},$$ and 
$\displaystyle\mathsf{Denom} := \int_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n} A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}$.
<!-- end sublem-6 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
$
\displaystyle \mathcal P_N'(\xi)=\frac{d}{d\xi}\log\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}[e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}]=\frac{\mathsf N}{\mathsf D}$ where $\mathsf N:= \int e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\Upsilon_N d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}$ and $\mathsf D:= \int e^{\xi\Upsilon_N} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}$. 
 By \eqref{e.D_n-additional-small-denom},
$$
\mathsf D=  (1\pm c_2(R)\lambda^{-k})\int_{D_{N,k}} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}.
$$

By \eqref{e.lalala}, for some constant ${\widehat C}_3>1$,     
\begin{align*}
&\mathsf N=\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\Upsilon_N d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} \pm {{\widehat C}_3} 
 \mathsf D\\
 &=\int_{[\xi \overline{S}_n\geq 0]\cap D_{N,k}} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\Upsilon_N d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}+\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]\cap D_{N,k}^c} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\Upsilon_N d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\pm {{\widehat C}_3}  \mathsf D\notag\\
&=  (1\pm c_2(R)\lambda^{-k})\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]\cap D_{N,k}} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\Upsilon_N d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} \pm            
{{\widetilde C}_3} 
\mathsf D, \textrm{ by \eqref{e.D_n-small}. }                \notag \\
\end{align*}
Since $|\Upsilon_n-\overline{S}_n|\leq B_0$ ,  there are constants $c_3'(R)$ and $C_3'(k,R)$ so that
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf D&=e^{\pm c_3'(R)\lambda^{-k}}\int_{D_{N,k}} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\\
\mathsf N&=e^{\pm c_3'(R)\lambda^{-k}}\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]\cap D_{N,k}} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\overline{S}_n\, d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\pm C_3'(k,R)\mathsf D. \label{e.num-denom}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
We now use the identity $\Upsilon_N=\overline{S}_n-\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0+\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_{n,\ell}$ (Lemma \ref{l.Phi-Decomp}):
\begin{align*}
\mathsf D
&=e^{\pm c_3'(R)\lambda^{-k}}\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\left[e^{\xi\Upsilon_N} 1_{D_{N,k}}\right]
=e^{\pm c_3'(R)\lambda^{-k}}\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\left[\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\left(e^{\xi\Upsilon_N} 1_{D_{N,k}}\big|\overline{\mathcal F}_0^\infty\right)\right]\\
&=e^{\pm c_3'(R)\lambda^{-k}}\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\left[\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\left(e^{\xi(\overline{S}_n-\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0+\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_{n,\ell})}1_{D_{N,k}}\big|\overline{\mathcal F}_0^\infty\right)\right]\\
&=e^{\pm c_3'(R)\lambda^{-k}}\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\!\!\left[ e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}B_{N,k,\xi}\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\left(e^{-\xi\Delta{\mathfrak{z}}_0}\big|\overline{\mathcal F}_0^\infty\right)\right]\\
&= e^{\pm c_3'(R)\lambda^{-k}}\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\left[  e^{\xi\overline{S}_n} B_{N,k,\xi}\cdot e^{\pm c_0(R)\lambda^{-k}}A_{k,\xi}\right].  
\end{align*}
Similarly, if $\xi>0$, then
$$\displaystyle\mathsf N= e^{\pm c_3'(R)\lambda^{-k}} \mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\left[ 1_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n B_{N,k,\xi}\cdot e^{\pm c_0(R)\lambda^{-k}}A_{k,\xi}\right]\pm C_3'(k,R)\mathsf D,$$
and if $\xi<0$ we have the same estimate, but with $e^{\mp c_3'(R)\lambda^{-k}}$ instead of $e^{\pm c_3'(R)\lambda^{-k}}$.

Note that the terms inside expectation have constant sign  on their support. Therefore,  we can pull the $e^{\pm c_0(R)\lambda^{-k}}$ outside, and obtain with $c_3^\ast(R):=c_0(R)+c_3'(R)$, 
\begin{equation}\label{e.D}
\mathsf D=e^{\pm c_3^\ast(R)\lambda^{-k}}\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\left[  e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi}\right]\equiv e^{\pm c_3^\ast(R)\lambda^{-k}}\mathsf{Denom};
\end{equation}
Similarly, if $\xi>0$, then 
\begin{equation}\label{e.N} 
\mathsf N=e^{\pm c_3^\ast(R)\lambda^{-k}}\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\pm C_3'(k,R)\mathsf D.
\end{equation}
If $\xi<0$, replace $e^{\pm c_3^\ast(R)\lambda^{-k}}$ by $e^{\mp c_3^\ast(R)\lambda^{-k}}$. Henceforth, we only consider the case $\xi>0$. 
 
 The same calculations, but with $[\overline{S}_n<0]$ instead of $[\overline{S}_n\geq 0]$ show that 
\begin{align*}
&\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n< 0]\cap D_{N,k}} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}\overline{S}_n d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}=e^{\mp c_3^\ast(R)\lambda^{-k}}\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n< 0]} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(x),\textrm{ and therefore, }\\
&\left|\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n< 0]} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(x)\right|=e^{\pm c_3^\ast(R)\lambda^{-k}}\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n< 0]\cap D_{N,k}} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}|\overline{S}_n| d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\\
&\leq e^{c_3^\ast(R)}\left(\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n< 0]} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}|\Upsilon_N| d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}+B_0 \int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n< 0]} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\right)
\leq e^{c_3^\ast(R)}(B_0+1)\mathsf D, \textrm{ by \eqref{e.lalala}}. 
\end{align*}
Thus  $\displaystyle \int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n\geq 0]} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}$
\begin{align*}
&= \int_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}-\int_{[\xi\overline{S}_n< 0]} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\\
&= \int_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\pm  e^{c_3^\ast(R)}(B_0+1)\mathsf D\\
&= \int_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}(\overline{S}_{k+1}^{n-k-1}\pm 2k\sup_i\|f_i\|_\infty) A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\pm  e^{c_3^\ast(R)}(B_0+1)\mathsf D\\
&=\int_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_{k+1}^{n-k-1} A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\pm  e^{c_3^\ast(R)}(B_0+1)\mathsf D\\
&\hspace{5cm} \pm 2k\sup_i\|f_i\|_\infty\cdot \int_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} e^{\xi\overline{S}_n} A_{k,\xi} B_{N,k,\xi} d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\\
&=\mathsf{Num}\pm e^{2c_3^\ast(R)}(B_0+1)\mathsf{Denom}\pm 2k\sup_i\|f_i\|_\infty \mathsf{Denom},\textrm{ see \eqref{e.D}}.
\end{align*}
Plugging this into \eqref{e.N}, and collecting constants, we find that for some constants $c^\dagger_3(R)$ and $C_3^\dagger(k,R)$,
$
\mathsf N=e^{\pm c_3^\dagger(R)\lambda^{-k}} \mathsf{Num}\pm C_3^{\dagger}(k,R)\mathsf{Denom}.
$ This and \eqref{e.D} lead to 
$$
\mathcal P_N'(\xi)=\frac{\mathsf N}{\mathsf D}=e^{\pm c_3(R)\lambda^{-k}}\left(\frac{\mathsf{Num}}{\mathsf{Denom}}\right)\pm C_3(k,R),
$$
where $c_3(R)=c_3^\ast(R)+c_3^\dagger(R)$, and $C_3(k,R):=C_3^\dagger(k,R)e^{c_3^\ast(R)}$.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- sublem-7: body_md -->
\label{sl.rho-mixing}
For every $R>0$ there are constants $c_4(R)$  and  $C_4(k,R)$ $(k\geq 1)$ such that for all $k>K_3(R)$, $N>N_3(k,R)$ and $\xi\in [-R,R]\setminus [-r(k),r(k)]$, 
$$
\mathcal P_N'(\xi)=e^{\pm c_4(R)\lambda^{-k}}\bigl(\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)\pm C_{4}(k,R)\bigr).
$$
<!-- end sublem-7 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
Recall that $A_{k,\xi}$ is $\overline{\mathcal F}_0^k$-measurable, and $B_{N,k,\xi}$ is $\overline{\mathcal F}_{n-k}^{n+m(k)}$-measurable. Therefore, there are functions 
$\widehat{A}_{k,\xi}$ and $\widehat{B}_{N,k,\xi}$ such that 
$A_{k,\xi}=\widehat{A}_{k,\xi}(\overline{X}_0,\ldots, \overline{X}_k)$, and $B_{N,k,\xi}=\widehat{B}_{k,\xi}(\overline{X}_{n-k},\ldots, \overline{X}_{n+m(k)})$. 
 By Proposition \ref{Prop-Markov-Kernel}, the joint distribution of 
$\{\overline{X}_i\}_{i\geq 0}$ with respect to $\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}$ is equal to the joint distribution of the Markov chain $\{X_i\}_{i\geq 0}$. Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
&\mathsf{Num}=\mathbb E\left(e^{\xi S_n} S_{k+1}^{n-k-1} \widehat{A}_{k,\xi}(X_0,\ldots,X_k) \widehat{B}_{N,k,\xi}(X_{n-k},\ldots,X_{n+m(k)})\right),
\end{align*}
 where  $S_{i}^{j}=f_{i}(X_{i})+\cdots+f_{j}(X_{j})$ and $S_n=S_1^n$. 
  
 We  write for short
 $A_{k,\xi}=\widehat{A}_{k,\xi}({X}_0,\ldots, {X}_k)$, $B_{N,k,\xi}=\widehat{B}_{k,\xi}({X}_{n-k},\ldots, {X}_{n+m(k)})$, and 
$$
\mathsf{Num}=\mathbb E\left(e^{\xi S_n} S_{k+1}^{n-k-1} {A}_{k,\xi}{B}_{N,k,\xi}\right).
$$
 Note that integrand has the form $F(X_1,\ldots,X_M)$, with $M:=n+m(k)$. 

We would like to rewrite $\mathsf{Num}$ in terms of the change of measure $\{\widetilde{X}^\xi_i\}_{i\geq 0}$ from 
\S\ref{ss.change-of-measure}. Recall $h_i$ and $\mathsf{P}_i$ from Lemma \ref{LmAddPres} and \eqref{AddPres}, then  for any Borel  $F(x_0,\ldots,x_M)$, 
\begin{equation}\label{e.com-F}
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi(F(\widetilde{X}_0^\xi,\ldots,\widetilde{X}_M^\xi))=\mathbb E\left(e^{\xi{S}_M} \frac{h_{M}({X}_{M},\xi)}
{e^{\mathsf{P}_M(\xi)}h_{0}({X}_{0},\xi)}F({X}_0,\ldots,{X}_M)\right).
\end{equation}
 This leads to the identity 
$\displaystyle\mathsf{Num}=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi\biggl(e^{-\xi\widetilde{S}_{n+1}^{M}} \frac{e^{\mathsf{P}_{M}(\xi)}h_{0}(\widetilde{X}_{0}^\xi,\xi)}{h_{M}
(\widetilde{X}_{M}^\xi,\xi)} \widetilde{A}_{k,\xi} \cdot \widetilde{S}_{k+1}^{n-k-1}\cdot \widetilde{B}_{N,k,\xi}
\biggr)
$,
where $\widetilde{S}_i^j\!=\! f_i(\widetilde{X}_i^\xi)+\cdots+f_j(\widetilde{X}_j^\xi)$, $\widetilde{A}_{k,\xi}\!=\!\widehat{A}_{k,\xi}(\widetilde{X}_1^\xi,\ldots,\widetilde{X}_M^\xi)$.   
Let ${\mathcal F}_i^j$ denote  the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $\widetilde{X}^\xi_i,\ldots,\widetilde{X}^\xi_j$ (or equivalently, by $X_i,\ldots,X_j$). Rearranging terms, we have
\begin{align*}
\mathsf{Num}&=e^{\mathsf{P}_{M}(\xi)}\sum_{j=k+1}^{n-k-1}\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi\biggl( \underset{\mathcal F_0^{k}\textrm{-measurable}}{\underbrace{h_{0}(\widetilde{X}_{0}^\xi,\xi) \widetilde{A}_{k,\xi}}} \times f_j(\widetilde{X}_j^\xi)
\times
\underset{\mathcal F_{n-k}^{M}\textrm{-measurable}}{\underbrace{\frac{ \widetilde{B}_{N,k,\xi}e^{-\xi\widetilde{S}_{n+1}^{M}}}
{h_{M}(\widetilde{X}_{M}^\xi,\xi)}}}
\biggr).
\end{align*}

By Lemma \ref{l.uniform-Doeblin}, there is a constant ${\varepsilon}_0(R)$  such that 
$\{\widetilde{X}_i^\xi\}_{i\geq 0}$ is uniformly elliptic with the same ellipticity constant ${\varepsilon}_0(R)$   for every $|\xi|\leq R$.  By Corollary \ref{Cor-rho-mixing},  $\{\widetilde{X}_i^\xi\}_{i\geq 0}$ are exponentially $\rho$-mixing with the same mixing coefficients $C_{mix}=C_{mix}(R)>0$, $\theta=\theta(R)\in (0,1)$ for all $|\xi|\leq R$. 

Applying exponential $\rho$-mixing twice, first for the pair $\mathcal F_0^k, \mathcal F_j^{\infty}$, and then for the pair $\mathcal F_0^j, \mathcal F_{n-k}^\infty$, and noting that all functions in the expectation are uniformly bounded by a global constant, we obtain that for some constants $c_4'(k,R)$ $(k\geq 1)$, 
\begin{align*}
\mathsf{Num}&=\sum_{j=k+1}^{n-k-1}\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi\bigl( h_{0}(\widetilde{X}_{0}^\xi,\xi) \widetilde{A}_{k,\xi}\bigr)  \widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi(f_j(\widetilde{X}_j^\xi))
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi
\biggl(\frac{e^{\mathsf{P}_M(\xi)} \widetilde{B}_{N,k,\xi}e^{-\xi\widetilde{S}_{n+1}^{M}}}
{h_{M}(\widetilde{X}_{M}^\xi,\xi)}
\biggr)\pm c_4'(k,R)e^{P_M(\xi)}\\
&=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi(\widetilde{S}_{k+1}^{n-k-1})\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi\bigl( h_{0}(\widetilde{X}_{0}^\xi,\xi) \widetilde{A}_{k,\xi}\bigr)\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi
\biggl(\frac{ e^{\mathsf{P}_M(\xi)} \widetilde{B}_{N,k,\xi}e^{-\xi\widetilde{S}_{n+1}^{M}}}{h_{M}(\widetilde{X}_{M}^\xi,\xi)}
\biggr)\pm c_4'(k,R)e^{\mathsf{P}_M(\xi)}.
\end{align*}
Another application of exponential $\rho$-mixing gives constants $c_4''(k,R),c_4^\ast(k,R)$  for which 
\begin{align}
&\mathsf{Num}{=e^{\mathsf{P}_M(\xi)}\biggl[\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi(\widetilde{S}_{k+1}^{n-k-1})\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi\biggl( \frac{ h_{0}(\widetilde{X}_{0}^\xi,\xi) \widetilde{A}_{k,\xi} \widetilde{B}_{N,k,\xi}e^{-\xi\widetilde{S}_{n+1}^{M}}}{h_{M}(\widetilde{X}_{M}^\xi,\xi)}
\biggr)\pm (c_4'' \theta^{n-k}\|\widetilde{S}_{k+1}^{n-k-1}\|_\infty+ c_4')\biggr]}\notag\\
&=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi(\widetilde{S}_{k+1}^{n-k-1})\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi\biggl( h_{0}(\widetilde{X}_{0}^\xi,\xi) \widetilde{A}_{k,\xi}\frac{e^{\mathsf{P}_M(\xi)} \widetilde{B}_{N,k,\xi}e^{-\xi\widetilde{S}_{n+1}^{M}}}{h_{M}(\widetilde{X}_{M}^\xi,\xi)}
\biggr)\pm c_4^\ast(k,R)e^{\mathsf{P}_M(\xi)}\notag\\
&=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi(\widetilde{S}_{k+1}^{n-k-1})\mathbb E\left(e^{\xi{S}_n}
A_{k,\xi}B_{N,k,\xi}
\right)\pm c_4^\ast(k,R)e^{\mathsf{P}_M(\xi)}\quad
\textrm{ by \eqref{e.com-F}}
\notag\\
&=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi(\widetilde{S}_{k+1}^{n-k-1})
\times e^{\pm c_3^\ast(R)\lambda^{-k}}\mathsf{Denom}\pm c_4^\ast(k,R)e^{\mathsf{P}_M(\xi)},\textrm{ see \eqref{e.D}. }\notag\\
&=(\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi(\widetilde{S}_n)+O(k))\times   e^{\pm c_3^\ast(R)\lambda^{-k}}\mathsf{Denom}\pm c_4^\ast(k,R)e^{\mathsf C(R)m(k)}e^{\mathsf{P}_n(\xi)},\label{e.curly-N-final}
\end{align}
because $\displaystyle \sup_i\|f_i\|_\infty<\infty$ and $\displaystyle \sup_i \sup_{[-R,R]}p_i<\mathsf C(R)$, see Lemma \ref{LmAddPres}.


By \eqref{Pres1stDer}, there is a constant $\mathsf C(R)$ such that for every $\xi\in [-R,R]$, 
$$
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi(\widetilde{S}_n)=\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)\pm \mathsf C(R).
$$
By \eqref{Pres0thDer} and \eqref{Pres1stDer},  there is a constant $\mathsf C'(R)$ such that 
\begin{align*}
&e^{\mathsf{P}_n(\xi)}\leq \mathsf C'(R)\mathbb E(e^{\xi{S}_n})=\mathsf C'(R)\mathbb E_{\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}(e^{\xi\overline{S}_n})\leq e^{B_0}\mathsf C'(R)\int_{R_0} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}=e^{B_0}\mathsf C'(R)\cdot \mathsf{D}\\
&\leq e^{B_0+c_3^\ast(R)}\mathsf C'(R)\cdot \mathsf{Denom}, \textrm{ see  }\eqref{e.D}.
\end{align*}
Plugging these estimates in \eqref{e.curly-N-final}, and collecting constants, we find that for some constants $c_4^\dagger(R), C_4^\dagger(k,R)$ $(k\geq 1)$, 
$$
\frac{\mathsf{Num}}{\mathsf{Denom}}=e^{\pm c_4^\dagger(R)\lambda^{-k}}\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)\pm C_4^\dagger(k,R).
$$

We now add the assumptions that $k>K_3(R)$, $N>N_3(k,R)$, and $\xi\in [-R,R]\setminus[-r(k),r(k)]$, and invoke Sublemma \ref{sl.Num-Denom}, to obtain the result.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
Suppose 
$k\!\!>\!\!K_3(R)$, then $k\!\!>\!\!K_0(R)$.      
The assertion of the lemma holds for all $\xi\!\!\in\!\! [-r(k),r(k)]$, by Sublemma \ref{sl.small-xi}, and for all 
$\xi\!\!\in\!\! [-R,R]\setminus [-r(k),r(k)]$, by  Sublemma \ref{sl.rho-mixing}.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- lem-38: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-Uniform-Convexity}
Let $V_n:={\rm Var}(S_n)$.
For every $R>0$ there are $\underline{\delta}(R),\overline{\delta}(R), N(R)>0$ such that for all $n\geq N(R)$ and $N$ such that $\lfloor N/N_0\rfloor=n$,  \index{Pressure!second derivative and variance}\index{Geometric pressure!second derivative and variance}
$$
\mathcal P_N''(\xi), \mathsf{P}_n''(\xi)\in [ \underline{\delta}(R)V_n, \overline{\delta}(R)V_n]\textrm{ for all }\xi\in [-R,R].
$$
<!-- end lem-38 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
The assertion for $\mathsf{P}_n''$ is shown in Lemma \ref{LmPressure}, see \eqref{Pres2dDer}. We prove the assertion for $\mathcal P_N''$.
Consider the following three  probability measures on ${\mathsf{R}}_0$:
\begin{align*}
&\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}:=\textrm{ normalized Euclidean area}\ , \ 
\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}:=\frac{e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}{\int_{\mathsf{{\mathsf{R}}}_0} e^{\xi\Upsilon_N}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\ , \
\overline{m}_{\xi,n}:=\frac{e^{\xi \overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}{\int_{\mathsf{{\mathsf{R}}}_0} e^{\xi \overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}. 
\end{align*}
By Lemma \ref{l.Phi-Decomp},  $|\Upsilon_N-\overline{S}_n|\leq B_0$ with $B_0$ independent of $N$, so ${d\overline{m}_{\xi,N}}/{d\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}=e^{\pm 2B_0}$. 

By differentiation, 
$\mathcal P_N''(\xi)=\mathrm{Var}_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}(\Upsilon_N):=\int \Upsilon_N^2 d\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}-
\left(\int \Upsilon_N d\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}\right)^2.
$
 Using the identity $\mathrm{Var}(X+Y)=\mathrm{Var}(X)+\mathrm{Var}(Y)+2\mathrm{Cov}(X,Y)$ and  the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality $|\mathrm{Cov}(X,Y)|\leq\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(X)\mathrm{Var}(Y)}$, we obtain 
$$
\mathcal P_N''(\xi)=\mathrm{Var}_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n)
+O(1)+O(\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n)}).
$$
Thus to prove the lemma, it is sufficient to show that there is a constant $C(R)$ such that for all $n$ large enough, for all  $\xi\in [-R,R]$, 
$$
C(R)^{-1}V_n\leq \mathrm{Var}_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n)\leq C(R)V_n.
$$
Let $\widehat{\mu}_{\xi,N}:=\mathbb E_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n):=\int \overline{S}_n d\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}$,  $\overline{\mu}_{\xi,n}:=\mathbb E_{\overline{m}_{\xi,n}}(\overline{S}_n):=\int \overline{S}_n d\overline{m}_{\xi,n}$. 

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Lower Bound\/:} 
$\mathrm{Var}_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n)=\frac{\int e^{\xi\Upsilon_n}(\overline{S}_n-\widehat{\mu}_{\xi,N})^2 d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}  }{\int e^{\xi\Upsilon_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} }\geq e^{-2B_0|\xi|}\frac{\int e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}(\overline{S}_n-\widehat{\mu}_{\xi,N})^2 d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}  }{\int e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0} }.                                             
$
The expectation of a random variable $Y$ is the constant $\mu$ which minimizes $\mathbb E[(Y-\mu)^2]$, and the variance of $Y$ is the minimal  value  thus obtained. 

So  changing $\widehat{\mu}_{\xi,N}$ to $\overline{\mu}_{\xi,n}$ in the  integral {\em decreases} the fraction to $\mathrm{Var}_{\overline{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n)$, and 
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{Var}_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n)&\geq e^{-2B_0|\xi|}\mathrm{Var}_{\overline{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n)\equiv e^{-2B_0|\xi|}\left(\frac{\int e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n^2 d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}{\int e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}-\left(\frac{\int e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}\overline{S}_n d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}{\int e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}}\right)^2
\right)\\
&\equiv e^{-2B_0|\xi|}\frac{d^2}{d\xi^2}\left(\log \int e^{\xi\overline{S}_n}d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}\right)=e^{-2B_0|\xi|}\frac{d^2}{d\xi^2}\left(\log \mathbb E(e^{\xi{S}_n})\right).
\end{align*}
By Theorem 7.3 in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book} {(see also Proposition \ref{PrFreeEn})},
there is a constant $C(R)\!>\!1$ such that for all $n$ large enough,
\begin{equation}\label{e.F-is-unif-convex}
C(R)^{-1}V_n\leq \frac{d^2}{d\xi^2}\left(\log  \mathbb E(e^{\xi{S}_n})\right)\leq C(R)V_n\textrm{ for all }\xi\in [-R,R].
\end{equation}
In particular, for all $n$ large enough, $\mathrm{Var}_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n)\geq C(R)^{-1}e^{-2B_0R}V_n$. 


\medskip
\noindent
{\em Upper Bound\/:} Adding a constant does not change the variance, so 
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{Var}_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n)&=
\mathrm{Var}_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n-\overline{\mu}_{\xi,n})=
\mathbb E_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}[(\overline{S}_n-\overline{\mu}_{\xi,n})^2]-
\mathbb E_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}[(\overline{S}_n-\overline{\mu}_{\xi,n})]^2\\
&\leq \mathbb E_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}[(\overline{S}_n-\overline{\mu}_{\xi,n})^2]\leq e^{2B_0|\xi|}\mathbb E_{\overline{m}_{\xi,N}}[(\overline{S}_n-\overline{\mu}_{\xi,n})^2],
\textrm{ because $\frac{d\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}{d\overline{m}_{\xi,n}}\leq e^{2B_0|\xi|}$ }\\
&=e^{2B_0|\xi|}\mathrm{Var}_{\overline{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n)=
e^{2B_0|\xi|}\frac{d^2}{d\xi^2}\left(\log  \mathbb E(e^{\xi\overline{S}_n})\right)=
e^{2B_0|\xi|}\frac{d^2}{d\xi^2}\left(\log  \mathbb E(e^{\xi{S}_n})\right).
\end{align*}
By \eqref{e.F-is-unif-convex},  for all $n$ large enough, for all $\xi\in[-R,R]$, $\mathrm{Var}_{\widehat{m}_{\xi,N}}(\overline{S}_n)\leq C(R)e^{2B_0R}V_n$.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lem-39: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-An-Bn}
Let $A_n(\xi),B_n(\xi)$ be two $C^2$ convex functions on $\mathbb R$, satisfying the following conditions, for some sequence $V_n\to\infty$ and $M,\lambda>1$:
\begin{enumerate}[(C1)]
\item $\forall R>0$ $\exists$ $c(R)$, $K(R)$, $C(k,R)$ such that for all $k> K(R)$ and for all $n$ sufficiently large,  $A_n'=e^{\pm c(R)\lambda^{-k}}(B_n'\pm C(k,R))$ on $[-R,R]$;
\item $\forall R>0$ $\exists \underline{\delta}(R),\overline{\delta}(R)>0$ such that  $A_n'', B_n''\in[\underline{\delta}(R)V_n,\overline{\delta}(R) V_n]$ on $[-R,R]$;
\item $\exists M$ such that for all $n$, $|A_n'(0)| , |B_n'(0)|\leq M$. 
\end{enumerate}
Then for any sequence of numbers $z_n\in\mathbb R$: 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item The equation $A_n'(\xi)=z_n$ (resp. $B_n'(\xi)=z_n$) can have at most one solution. 
\item There is a bounded sequence of $\xi_n$ such that $A_n'(\xi_n)=z_n$ for all $n$ large enough, iff there is a bounded sequence of $\eta_n$ such that $B_n'(\eta_n)=z_n$ for all $n$ large enough. If this happens, $|\xi_n-\eta_n|\to 0$.
\item If  $A_n'(\xi_n)=B_n'(\eta_n)$ for all $n$ large enough, then $\xi_n\to +\infty$ iff 
$\eta_n\to +\infty$, and  $\xi_n\to -\infty$ iff  $\eta_n\to -\infty$.  
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-39 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
By (C2), $A_n'', B_n''>0$, therefore $A_n'$ and $B_n'$ are strictly increasing, therefore the equations $A_n'(\xi)=z_n$ and $B_n'(\xi)=z_n$ can have at most one solution. This is part 1.


Suppose $\exists \xi_n\in (-R,R)$ such that $A_n'(\xi_n)=z_n$ for all $n$ large enough, and let ${\varepsilon}$ be  an arbitrary positive number. 

Set
$\displaystyle {\varepsilon}_k:=\max_{\sigma=\pm 1} |e^{\sigma c(R+1)\lambda^{-k}}-1|=
e^{c(R+1)\lambda^{-k}}-1$, and choose $k=k({\varepsilon},R)$ so large that $k>K(R+1)$, and 
 \begin{align}\label{e.k-choice}
& e^{-c(R+1)\lambda^{-k}}\underline{\delta}(R+1)>{\varepsilon}_k(1+R\overline{\delta}(R))
\textrm{ and } {\varepsilon}_k<{\varepsilon} \underline{\delta}(R+2)/(R\overline{\delta}(R)).
 \end{align}
By  (C2) and (C3), 
\begin{equation}\label{e.A_n'-UB}
|A_n'|,|B_n'|\leq M+R\overline{\delta}(R)V_n\textrm{ on }[-R,R]. 
\end{equation}
Choose $N_0\!\!=\!\!N_0({\varepsilon},k,R)$ so that for all $n\!\!>\!\!N_0$, $V_n\!\!>\!\!M$, and (C2) holds with $R,R+1,R+2$. 
For such $n$, by the mean value theorem, 
for any $t=e^{\pm c(R+1)\lambda^{-k}}$, 
\begin{align*}
&tA_n'(R+1)\geq t\bigl(A_n'(R)+\underline{\delta}(R+1)V_n\bigr)
=A_n'(R)+t\underline{\delta}(R+1)V_n-
(1-t)A_n'(R)\\
&\geq A_n'(R)+V_n\left[t\underline{\delta}(R+1)-{\varepsilon}_k
\bigl(MV_n^{-1}+
R\overline{\delta}(R)\bigr)\right], \textrm{ by \eqref{e.A_n'-UB} and since $|1-t|\leq {\varepsilon}_k$ }\\
&\geq A_n'(R)+V_n\underset{\textrm{positive, by \eqref{e.k-choice}}}{\underbrace{\left[e^{-c(R+1)\lambda^{-k}}\underline{\delta}(R+1)-{\varepsilon}_k
\bigl(1+
R\overline{\delta}(R)\bigr)\right]}}>A_n'(R)\textrm{ }.
\end{align*} 

Thus 
$e^{\pm c(R+1)\lambda^{-k}}A_n'(R+1)\!\!>\!\!A_n'(R)\textrm{ for all $n\!\!>\!\!N_0$},
$ regardless of the sign of $A_n'(R+1)$ or the value of $t$, provided $t\!\!=\!\!e^{\pm c(R+1)\lambda^{-k}}$. 
Fix $N_1\!\!>\!\!N_0$ such that for all $n\!\!>\!\!N_1$, 
 $\underline{\delta}(R+2)V_n\!\!>\!\!C(k,R+1)$.
By  (C2), and then (C1),
\begin{align*}
&B_n'(R+2)\geq B_n'(R+1)+\underline{\delta}(R+2)V_n\\
&= \left(e^{\pm c(R+1)\lambda^{-k}}A_n'(R+1)\pm C(k,R+1)\right)+\underline{\delta}(R+2)V_n\\
&\geq e^{\pm c(R+1)\lambda^{-k}} A_n'(R+1)
>A_n'(R).
\end{align*}
Thus, for all $n$ large enough, $B'_n(R+2)>A_n'(R)$. 
By symmetry,  $B_n'(-R-2)\leq A_n'(-R)$ (apply the previous argument to the pair $(A_n(-t), B_n(-t))$). So  for all $n$ large,
$$
z_n=A_n'(\xi_n)\in (A_n'(-R),A_n'(R))\subset (B_n'(-R-2), B_n'(R+2)).
$$
By the intermediate value theorem, for such $n$  there exists $|\eta_n|\leq R+2$ such that $B_n'(\eta_n)=z_n$. By the first part of the lemma, these $\eta_n$ are unique.

Next we show that $|\xi_n-\eta_n|\to 0$. By the mean value theorem, either $\xi_n=\eta_n$, or 
 $\displaystyle
 \frac{|B_n'(\xi_n)-B_n'(\eta_n)|}{|\xi_n-\eta_n|}\geq \underline{\delta}(R+2) V_n$. Either way,  $\displaystyle |\xi_n-\eta_n|\leq \frac{|B_n'(\xi_n)-B_n'(\eta_n)|}{\underline{\delta}(R+2)V_n}$. 
 By (C1) and the choice of ${\varepsilon}_k$, 
 \begin{align*}
 &|B_n'(\xi_n)-B_n'(\eta_n)|=|B_n'(\xi_n)-A_n'(\xi_n)|=|(e^{\pm c(R+1)\lambda^{-k}}A_n'(\xi_n)\pm C(k,R+1))-A_n'(\xi_n)|\\
 &\leq C(k,R+1)+{\varepsilon}_k|A_n'(\xi_n)|
 \leq   C(k,R+1)+{\varepsilon}_k(M+R\overline{\delta}(R)V_n).
 \end{align*}
 Thus, 
$\displaystyle \limsup_{n\to\infty}|\xi_n-\eta_n|\leq
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{C(k,R+1)+{\varepsilon}_k(M+R\overline{\delta}(R)V_n)}
{\underline{\delta}(R+2) V_n}={\varepsilon}_k\times \frac{R\overline{\delta}(R)}{\underline{\delta}(R+2)}<{\varepsilon}
$,
see \eqref{e.k-choice}. Since ${\varepsilon}$ was arbitrary, $|\xi_n-\eta_n|\to 0$. 

This proves  direction $(\Rightarrow)$ in part (2) of the lemma. Direction $(\Leftarrow)$ follows by symmetry, after noting that   $(A_n,B_n)$ satisfies (C1)--(C3) iff  $(B_n,A_n)$ satisfies (C1)--(C3).

Part (3) of the lemma has a similar proof. Again it is enough to prove the implication $(\Rightarrow)$.  It is also sufficient to consider the case $\xi_n\to+\infty$, otherwise we work with $A_n(-\xi), B_n(-\xi)$. Suppose $A_n'(\xi_n)=B_n'(\eta_n)$. 

Fix $R>1$ arbitrary. Arguing as above but with $B_n$ replacing $A_n$, we construct $k=k(R)$ and $N_0$ so 
that for all $n>N_0$,  $e^{-c(R+2)\lambda^{-k}}B_n'(R+1)>B_n'(R)$.
Fix $N_1$ such that for all  $n>N_1$, $\xi_n>R+2$ and 
 $\underline{\delta}(R+2)V_n>C(k,R+2).$
By the mean value theorem,  $B_n'(R+2)\geq B_n'(R+1)+\underline{\delta}(R+2)V_n$, whence 
\begin{align*}
&B_n'(\eta_n)=A_n'(\xi_n)>A_n'(R+2)>e^{-c(R+2)\lambda^{-k}}(B_n'(R+2)
-C(k,R+2))\\
&>
e^{-c(R+2)\lambda^{-k}}(B_n'(R+1)+\underline{\delta}(R+2)V_n-C(k,R+2))
\!\!>\!\!e^{-c(R+2)\lambda^{-k}}B_n'(R+1)\!\!>\!\!B_n'(R).
\end{align*}
So  $\eta_n>R$ for all $n>\max\{N_0,N_1\}$. Since $R$ was arbitrary, $\eta_n\to +\infty$.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- head-6: body_md -->
The proposition follows from Lemma \ref{Lemma-An-Bn}, applied to  $A_k(\xi):=\mathcal P_{N_k}(\xi)$ and $B_k(\xi):=\mathsf{P}_{n_k}(\xi)$. The lemma is applicable: 

Take $V_k:={\rm Var}(S_k)$, then $V_k\to\infty$ by Proposition \ref{Prop-Var-Growth}. 

Condition (C1) is guaranteed by Lemma \ref{Lemma-is-it-really-this-hard-to-prove?}.

Condition (C2) is the content of  Lemma \ref{Lemma-Uniform-Convexity}. 

Condition (C3)  can be verified as follows. $\mathsf{P}_n'(0)$ is bounded, because $\mathsf{P}_n'(0)=\mathbb E(S_n)$ by construction, and $\mathbb E(S_n)=O(1)$ by Proposition \ref{Prop-Drift}. To see that  $\mathcal P_N'(0)$ is  bounded, we first observe by direct differentiation that  $\mathcal P_N'(0)=\int \Upsilon_N d\mu_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}$. By Lemma \ref{l.Phi-Decomp}, $|\Upsilon_N-\overline{S}_n|$ is uniformly bounded,  and $\overline{S}_n$ is equal to $S_n$ in distribution. Therefore  $\mathcal P_N'(0)=\mathbb E(S_n)+O(1)=O(1)$.\hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-6 -->
<!-- prop-11: body_md -->
\label{PrBulk}
If $\xi_N(\omega)\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}\xi$ and $\xi$ is  finite, then 
${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is generic for $\mu_\xi.$ If  $\xi$ is a finite limit point of $\xi_N(\omega)$ then $\mu_\xi$ is a historical measure for ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ (see Definition \ref{d.historical}).
<!-- end prop-11 -->
<!-- lem-40: body_md -->
\label{l.solution-xi}
Let $z_n$ be a sequence of real numbers. If there exists a  bounded sequence of $\xi_n\in\mathbb R$ such that $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)=z_n+O(1)$, then for all $n$ large enough there exist $\xi_n'\in\mathbb R$ such that $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n')=z_n$. Moreover, $\xi_n'=\xi_n+O(n^{-1})$.
<!-- end lem-40 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Suppose $|\xi_n|< R$ and $|\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)-z_n|\leq K$ for all $n$. By \eqref{Pres2dDer} and Proposition~\ref{Prop-Var-Growth}, there exists a positive constant $c$ such that $\mathsf{P}_n''>cn$ on $[-2R,2R]$, for all $n$ large enough. Necessarily,  
$
\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n+\frac{2K}{cn})>\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)+cn\cdot \frac{2K}{cn}\geq z_n-K+2K>z_n$. Similarly,   $
\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n-\frac{2K}{cn})<z_n$. By the intermediate value theorem, there exists $\xi_n'\in [\xi_n-\frac{2K}{cn},\xi_n+\frac{2K}{cn}]$ such that $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n')=z_n$. Since $P_n'$ is strictly increasing,  $\xi_n'$ is unique.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- lem-41: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-Pure-Seg-Ratio-Ergodic-Thm}
Suppose
$n_s$ is a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers, and $\xi_{n_s}, z_{n_s}, \xi$ are real numbers such that   $\mathsf{P}_{n_s}'(\xi_{n_s})=z_{n_s}$ and $\xi_{n_s}\to\xi$. 
 Let $W_{n_s}$ be a sequence of pure $E^s_{n_s}$-segments of bounded depth. If  
 $z_{n_s}(W_{n_s})=z_{n_s}+O(1)$, then   
\begin{equation}\label{e.engine2}
\forall \, \widetilde{C}_1,\widetilde{C}_2\in\mathfs G,\ \lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n_s}}\left\{\widetilde{\omega}\in W_{n_s}:  
(\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n_s-1}^{-1})
(\widetilde{\omega})\in\widetilde{C}_1\right\}}
{{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n_s}}\left\{\widetilde{\omega}\in W_{n_s}:  (\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n_s-1}^{-1})
(\widetilde{\omega})\in\widetilde{C}_2
\right\}}=\frac{M_\xi(\widetilde{C}_1)}{M_\xi(\widetilde{C}_2)}.
\end{equation}
For any other sequence of pure $E^s_{n_s}$-segments $W_{n_s}'$ as above,   
for all $\widetilde{C}\in\mathfs G$, for all $k$ sufficiently large,
\begin{equation}\label{e.engine2bis}
\frac{{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n_s}'}\left\{\widetilde{\omega}'\in W_{n_s}':  (\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ
\widetilde{\psi}_{n_s-1}^{-1})(\widetilde{\omega})\in\widetilde{C}
\right\}}
{{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n_s}}\left\{\widetilde{\omega}'\in W_{n_s}:  
(\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n_s-1}^{-1})(\widetilde{\omega})\in\widetilde{C}
\right\}}\asymp 1.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lem-41 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
We assume for simplicity that  $(n_s)_{s\geq 1}$ is the sequence $(1,2,3,\ldots)$, and write $n_s=n$. The routine modifications needed for the general case are left to the reader. 


We may assume  without loss of generality that $z_n(W_n)=z_n$ (otherwise we use Lemma~\ref{l.solution-xi} to change $\xi_n$ to $\xi_n'=\xi_n+O(n^{-1})$ such that $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n')=z_n(W_n)$). 

There is also no loss of generality in assuming $W_n$ has { fixed}  depth $k$, otherwise we split $\{W_n\}$ into a finite number of subsequences with this property. 
In this case,  $\pi(W_n)$ is a maximal $E^s_n$-segment in a cylinder $Q_n=\<b^{(n)}_{n-k},\ldots,\dot{b}^{(n)}_n\>$. 

Fix some 
 $\widetilde{C}=(D^{j}\circ\pi|_{\widetilde{F}_0}^{-1})\<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_\ell\>$, and define 
\begin{align*}
p_n(\widetilde{C})&:={\mathbb{P}}_{W_n}\left\{\widetilde{\omega}'\in W_n:  (\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})(\widetilde{\omega}')\in\widetilde{C}
\right\}.
\end{align*}
 Recall $X^{(n)}_i$ from \eqref{e.X-new}. By Lemma \ref{Lemma-f(X)},  
 $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(X^{(n)}_i(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}})))
 \!\!=\!\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n((\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\widetilde{\psi}_0)({\widetilde{\omega}}))\!-\!\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0({\widetilde{\omega}})$, so  for every ${\widetilde{\omega}}\in W_n$,
$$ 
 (\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})(\widetilde{\omega})\in\widetilde{C}
\Leftrightarrow  \left(\begin{array}{l}
{X}_i^{(n)}(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}}))=a_i\ (0\leq i\leq \ell)\\
                                                         
\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^n f_i(X^{(n)}_i(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}})))=z_n-j
\end{array}\right).
$$ 
Thus $p_n(\widetilde{C})$ is the probability of an elementary event in $W_n$, and by Lemma \ref{l.prob-of-elementry-event} 
\begin{align}
&p_n(\widetilde{C})={\mathbb{P}}\left[
\begin{array}{c}
S_n=z_n-j\\
{X}_0=a_0,\ldots, X_\ell=a_\ell
\end{array}
\bigg| 
{X}_{n-k}=b_{n-k}^{(n)},\ldots,{X}_{n}=b_{n}^{(n)}\right]\notag\\
&={\mathbb{P}}\left[
\begin{array}{c}
S_n=z_n-j\\
{X}_0=a_0,\ldots, X_\ell=a_\ell
\end{array}
\ ,\ 
{X}_{n-k}=b_{n-k}^{(n)},\ldots,{X}_{n}=b_{n}^{(n)}\right]\bigg/ \mu_0(Q_n).\label{e.engine3}
\end{align}

It is tempting to try to use  the mixing local limit theorem (Theorem \ref{ThLLTArrays}) to find $p_n(\widetilde{C})$,  but this result  assumes  that $\frac{z_n-\mathbb E(S_n)}{\sqrt{V_n}}$ converges to a finite limit, and  in our case $\frac{z_n-\mathbb E(S_n)}{\sqrt{V_n}}$ could tend to infinity.  
We will overcome this difficulty using the change of measure  discussed in  \S\ref{ss.change-of-measure}, and the assumptions  $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)=z_n$,  $\xi_n\to\xi$.

A direct calculation shows that 
\begin{equation}\label{e.change-of-measure-id}
{\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_0=a_0,\ldots,\widetilde{X}_n^{\xi_n}=a_n]=\frac{e^{\xi \sum_{i=1}^n f_i(a_i)}h_{n}(a_{n},\xi_n)}{e^{\mathsf{P}_n(\xi_n)}h_0(a_0,\xi_n)}{\mathbb{P}}\left(X_0=a_0,\ldots,X_n=a_n\right).
\end{equation}
After some algebraic manipulations this leads 
to the identity
\begin{align*}
&p_n(\widetilde{C})\!=\!\frac{e^{\mathsf{P}_n(\xi_n)} h_0(a_0,\xi_n)}
{e^{\xi_n(z_n-j)} h_n(b^{(n)}_n,\xi_n)\mu_0(Q_n)}{\mathbb{P}}\left[\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(\widetilde{X}_i^{\xi_n})=z_n-j,\!\begin{array}{l}
\widetilde{X}_i^{\xi_n}=a_i\ \   (0\leq i\leq \ell)\\  
\widetilde{X}_i^{\xi_n}=b_i^{(n)}
 (n-k\leq i\leq n)
\end{array}\!
\right]\!.
\end{align*}
$\widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_i$ is a  Markov chain, so if 
$\displaystyle w_n\!\!:=\!\!\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1} f_i(a_i)+\!\!\sum_{i={n-k+1}}^n f_i(b^{(n)}_i)$,\; 
$\displaystyle \widetilde{S}_{\ell}^{n-k}\!\!:=\!\!\sum_{i=\ell}^{n-k} f_i(\widetilde{X}_i^{\xi_n})$, then 
\begin{align}
&p_n(\widetilde{C})=   e^{\xi_n j} h_0(a_0,\xi_n){\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_0=a_0,\ldots,\widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_\ell=a_\ell]\notag\\
&\hspace{0.25cm}\times
{\mathbb{P}}\left[\begin{array}{l}
                  
\displaystyle\sum_{i=\ell}^{n-k} f_i(\widetilde{X}_i^{\xi_n})=z_n-w_n-j
\end{array}
\bigg|\begin{array}{l}
\widetilde{X}_\ell^{\xi_n}=a_\ell\\  
\widetilde{X}_{n-k}^{\xi_n}=b_{n-k}^{(n)}
\end{array}
\right] \label{e.p(C)}
\\&\hspace{0.25cm} 
\times \frac{{\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}_{n-k}^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_{n-k}|\widetilde{X}_\ell^{\xi_n}=a_\ell]}{{\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}_{n-k}^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_{n-k}]}\notag
\\
& \hspace{0.25cm} \times{\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}_{n-k}^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_{n-k}]\times{\mathbb{P}}
[\widetilde{X}_{n-k}^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_{n-k},\ldots,\widetilde{X}_n^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_n|\widetilde{X}_{n-k}^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_{n-k}]\times
\frac{e^{\mathsf{P}_n(\xi_n)-\xi_n z_n} }
{h_n(b^{(n)}_n,\xi_n)\mu_0(Q_n)}.\notag
\end{align}



The first term converges to $M_\xi(\widetilde{C})$, because $\xi_n\to\xi$ and the transition kernel of $\widetilde{X}^\xi_i$ given in \eqref{ProbXi} is continuous in $\xi$. The third term tends to one as $n\to\infty$ by $\phi$-mixing (Corollary \ref{Cor-phi-mixing}).
The fourth term does not depend on $\widetilde{C}$ and will cancel out in  \eqref{e.engine2}. It remains to analyze the second term. 

Let $\displaystyle\widetilde{V}_n^{\xi_n}:=\mathrm{Var}(\sum_{i=1}^{n} f_i(\widetilde{X}_i^{\xi_n}))$.

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Claim 1.\/}  
$
\displaystyle{\mathbb{P}}\left[\begin{array}{l}
                  
\displaystyle\sum_{i=\ell}^{n-k} f_i(\widetilde{X}_i^{\xi_n})=z_n-w_n-j
\end{array}
\bigg|\begin{array}{l}
\widetilde{X}_\ell^{\xi_n}=a_\ell\\  
\widetilde{X}_{n-k}^{\xi_n}=b_{n-k}^{(n)}
\end{array}
\right]=\frac{1+o(1)}{\sqrt{2\pi \widetilde{V}_n^{\xi_n}}}.
$

\noindent
{\em Proof of the Claim.\/}
 By Lemmas \ref{l.uniform-Doeblin} and Corollary \ref{Cor-rho-mixing}, 
$\mathrm{Var}(\widetilde{S}_\ell^{n-k})=\widetilde{V}_n^{\xi_n}+O(1)$, and  
by Lemma 7.21 in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book}, $\widetilde{V}_n^{\xi_n}\asymp V_n$. Thus $\mathrm{Var}(\widetilde{S}_\ell^{n-k})\asymp n$ (Proposition \ref{Prop-Var-Growth}). 

Since $f_i$ are uniformly bounded, $w_n=O(\ell+k)$. Next,  \eqref{Pres1stDer} and the assumption $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)=z_n$ lead to 
$$
\mathbb E(\widetilde{S}_\ell^{n-k})=\mathbb E(\widetilde{S}_1^n)+O(
\ell+k)\equiv\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_n}(S_n)+O(1)=\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)+O(1)=z_n+O(1).
$$
Thus $\displaystyle \frac{(z_n-w_n-j)-\mathbb E(\widetilde{S}_\ell^{n-k})}{\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(\widetilde{S}_\ell^{n-k})}}
=O\left(\frac{\ell+k+|j|}{n}\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0.$
Now we can apply the mixing local limit theorem (Theorem \ref{ThLLTArrays}) to the array


$$
\begin{array}{llllll}
\widetilde{X}_\ell^{\xi_{\ell+k}} &  &  & & &\textrm{given $\widetilde{X}^{\xi_{\ell+k}}_\ell=a_\ell$}\\
\widetilde{X}_\ell^{\xi_{\ell+k+1}} & \widetilde{X}_{\ell+1}^{\xi_{\ell+k+1}} & &  & &\textrm{given $\widetilde{X}^{\xi_{\ell+k+1}}_\ell=a_\ell$}\\
\widetilde{X}_\ell^{\xi_{\ell+k+2}} & \widetilde{X}_{\ell+1}^{\xi_{\ell+k+2}} & \widetilde{X}_{\ell+2}^{\xi_{\ell+k+2}} & & &
\textrm{given $\widetilde{X}^{\xi_{\ell+k+2}}_\ell=a_\ell$}\\
\vdots & \vdots &\vdots &\ddots& & \hspace{1.3cm}\vdots\\
\widetilde{X}_\ell^{\xi_n} & \widetilde{X}_{\ell+1}^{\xi_n} & \widetilde{X}_{\ell+2}^{\xi_n} & \cdots\cdots & \widetilde{X}_{n-k}^{\xi_n} 
&\textrm{given $\widetilde{X}^{\xi_{n}}_\ell=a_\ell$}
\end{array}
$$


The conditions of the theorem hold: Since $\xi_n\to\xi$, there exists some $R>0$ such that $\xi_n\in [-R,R]$ for all $n$.   Uniform ellipticity follows from Lemma \ref{l.uniform-Doeblin}.  
Irreducibility and the hereditary property follow from Lemmas  \ref{LmChange} and \ref{l.hereditary}. Finally, 
$\displaystyle {\mathbb{P}}\left[\widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_{n-k}=b^{(n)}_{n-k}\right]$ is bounded below, for the following reasons. 

We saw in the proof of Proposition \ref{Prop-Doeblin}, that there is a constant ${\varepsilon}_0'>0$ such that for all $i$, $a\in \mathfrak P_i$, and $b\in\mathfrak P_{i+2}$, there exists $c\in\mathfrak P_{i+1}$ such that 
$$
\pi_{i,i+1}(a,c)\pi_{i+1,i+2}(c,b)>({\varepsilon}_0')^2.
$$
Looking at \eqref{ProbXi} and Lemma \ref{LmAddPres}, we see that there is a constant ${\varepsilon}_1>0$ independent of $i,n,a,c$ such that 
$c
\pi_{i,i+1}^{\xi_n}(a_i,a_{i+1})\pi_{i+1,i+2}^{\xi_n}(a_{i+1},a_{i+2})>{\varepsilon}_1.
$
Thus 
\begin{align}
&{\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_{n-k}=b^{(n)}_{n-k}]  =
\sum_{a,c}{\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_{n-k-2}=a, \widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_{n-k-1}=c, \widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_{n-k}=b_{n-k}^{(n)}]\label{e.state-lower-bound-xi}\\
&=
\sum_{a,c}{\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_{n-k-2}=a]
\pi_{n-k-2,n-k-1}^{\xi_n}(a,c)\pi_{n-k-1,n-k}^{\xi_n}(c,b_{n-k}^{(n)})\geq {\varepsilon}_1 \sum_{a}{\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_{n-k-2}=a]={\varepsilon}_1.\notag
\end{align}
This completes the verification of the conditions of {Theorem \ref{t.ThLLT}}. Invoking the theorem, we obtain the claim.




\medskip
In summary,  $p_n(\widetilde{C})=[1+o(1)]M_\xi(\widetilde{C})c_n(W_n)$,  where
\begin{align}\label{e.12.6}
& c_n(W_n):=\frac{e^{\mathsf{P}_n(\xi_n)-\xi_n z_n}}{h_n(b^{(n)}_n,\xi_n)
\sqrt{2\pi \widetilde{V}_n^{\xi_n}}}\frac{{\mathbb{P}}
[\widetilde{X}_{n-k}^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_{n-k},\ldots,\widetilde{X}_n^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_n]}{\mu_0(Q_n)}
\end{align}
Since $c_n(W_n)$ is independent from $\widetilde{C}$,  ${p_n(\widetilde{C}_1)}/p_n(\widetilde{C}_2)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}{M_\xi(\widetilde{C}_1)}/{M_\xi(\widetilde{C}_2)}$.

We proved the first part of the lemma, \eqref{e.engine2}. 

For the second part, 
suppose $W_n'$ is another  sequence of pure $E^s_n$-segments of bounded depth and heights $z_n(W_n')=z_n+O(1)$. There is no loss of generality in assuming that $W_n'$ has fixed depth $k'$. Then $\pi(W_n')$ is a maximal $E^s_n$-segment in $Q_n':=\<c_{n-k'}^{(n)},\ldots,\dot{c}_n^{(n)}\>$. 
To prove \eqref{e.engine2bis}, it is sufficient to show:

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Claim 2.\/} 
 $c_n(W_n')\asymp c_n(W_n)$.  

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Proof of the Claim.\/} 
Let $\xi_n'$ be the solutions to $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n')=z_n(W_n')$. By Lemma \ref{l.solution-xi}, $|\xi_n'-\xi_n|=o(1/n)$. In particular, $\xi_n',\xi_n\to\xi$. We use the decomposition 
$$
\frac{c_n(W_n')}{c_n(W_n)}=
\underset{\mathrm{I}}{\underbrace{\frac{e^{\mathsf{P}_n(\xi_n')-\xi_n' z_n}}{e^{\mathsf{P}_n(\xi_n)-\xi_n z_n}}}}\cdot 
\underset{\mathrm{II}}{\underbrace{
\frac{h_n(b_n^{(n)},\xi_n)\sqrt{2\pi \widetilde{V}_n^{\xi_n}}}
{h_n(c_n^{(n)},\xi_n')\sqrt{2\pi \widetilde{V}_n^{\xi_n'}}}}}
\cdot
\underset{\mathrm{III}}{\underbrace{
\frac{\mu_0(Q_n)}{\mu_0(Q_n')}}}
\cdot
\underset{\mathrm{IV}}{\underbrace{
\frac{{\mathbb{P}}
[\widetilde{X}_{n-k'}^{\xi_n'}=c^{(n)}_{n-k'},\ldots,\widetilde{X}_n^{\xi_n'}=c^{(n)}_n]}{{\mathbb{P}}
[\widetilde{X}_{n-k}^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_{n-k},\ldots,\widetilde{X}_n^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_n]}}}.
$$

\medskip
$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{I}\asymp 1:}$
Choose some $R>0$ such that $\xi_n,\xi_n'\in [-R,R]$ for all $n$. 
By  \eqref{Pres1stDer}, $|\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)|=O(n)$ uniformly on $[-R,R]$, whence:
\begin{itemize}
\item  $z_n=O(n)$, and 
$
|(\xi_n-\xi_n')z_n|=O(n^{-1}n)=O(1).
$
\item  
$|\mathsf{P}_n(\xi_n)-\mathsf{P}_n(\xi_n')|=O(n\cdot |\xi_n-\xi_n'|)=O(n n^{-1})=O(1). 
$
\end{itemize}
Thus $|(\xi_n-\xi_n')z_n|+|\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n')-\mathsf{P}_n(\xi_n)|=O(1)$, and  $\mathrm{I}\asymp 1$. 

\medskip
$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{II}\asymp 1:}$ There are constants such that  $h_n(\cdot,\xi)=\mathsf{C}(R)^{\pm 1}$ and $\widetilde{V}^{\xi}_n= \mathsf{C}(R)^{\pm 1}V_n$ for all $\xi\in [-R,R]$, see Lemmas \ref{LmAddPres} and \ref{l.V-n-xi}.


\medskip
$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{III}\asymp 1:}$ $\mu_0(Q_n),\mu_0(Q_n')\asymp 1$, by Lemma \ref{Lemma-Cylinder-Area} (4).

\medskip
$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{IV}\asymp 1:}$  Choose $R$ such that $\xi_n,\xi_n'\in [-R,R]$ for all $n$, then it is easy to see using Lemma \ref{LmAddPres} that  $\pi_{j,j+1}^\xi(a,b)\asymp \pi_{j,j+1}(a,b)$ for $\xi\in [-R,R]$, uniformly in $j,a,b$.   

We saw above that ${\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_{n-k}=b^{(n)}_{n-k}]\in ({\varepsilon}_1,1]$. 
Also ${\mathbb{P}}[X_{n-k}=b^{(n)}_{n-k}]=\mu_0(b^{(n)}_{n-k})\asymp 1$, and $\pi_{j,j+1}^\xi(a,b)\asymp \pi_{j,j+1}(a,b)$ uniformly. So 
\begin{align*}
&{\mathbb{P}}
[\widetilde{X}_{n-k}^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_{n-k},\ldots,\widetilde{X}_n^{\xi_n}=b^{(n)}_n]={\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}^{\xi_n}_{n-k}=b^{(n)}_{n-k}]\prod_{j=n-k}^{n-1}\pi_{j,j+1}^{\xi_n}(b^{(n)}_j,b^{(n)}_{j+1})\\
&\asymp{\mathbb{P}}[X_{n-k}=b^{(n)}_{n-k}]\prod_{j=n-k}^{n-1}\pi_{j,j+1}(b^{(n)}_j,b^{(n)}_{j+1})=\mu_0(Q_n)\asymp 1.
\end{align*}
Similarly, ${\mathbb{P}}
[\widetilde{X}_{n-k'}^{\xi_n'}=c^{(n)}_{n-k'},\ldots,\widetilde{X}_n^{\xi_n}=c^{(n)}_n]\asymp \mu_0(Q_n')\asymp 1$.
So $\mathrm{IV}\asymp 1$.

\medskip
It follows that $c_n(W_n')/c_n(W)\asymp 1$.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- lem-42: body_md -->
\label{l.Extending-M-xi}
$M_\xi$ has a unique extension to a locally finite  measure $\nu_\xi$, which is locally flow invariant on $\mathfs G$. \index{Invariant Radon measures!$\mu_\xi$}
<!-- end lem-42 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
Fix  $\widetilde{C}\in\mathfs G$ of the form $(D^j\circ\pi|_{\widetilde{F}_0}^{-1})\<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_n\>$, and let $\widetilde{C}^u$ denote the bottom $E^u_0$-side of $\widetilde{C}$. Given $
W:=\widetilde{C}^u\cap (D^j\circ\pi|_{\widetilde{F}_0}^{-1})\<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_n; a_{n+1},\ldots,a_{n+\ell}\>
$, let 
$$
\zeta_{\widetilde{C}^u}(W):=\frac{e^{j}h_0(a_0,\xi)}{\ell^s(a_0)}{\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}^\xi_0=a_0,\ldots, \widetilde{X}^\xi_{n+\ell}=a_{n+\ell}].
$$
Each $W$ is a sub-segment of $\widetilde{C}^u$ with length $O(\lambda^{-(n+\ell)})$, and the collection of  $W$s is a semi-algebra  on $\widetilde{C}^u$, which --- since $\ell$ is arbitrary --- generates the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $\widetilde{C}^u$. By the Carath\'eodory's extension theorem, $\zeta_{\widetilde{C}^u}$ extends to a Borel measure on $\widetilde{C}^u$.

Set 
$\displaystyle \nu_{\xi,\widetilde{C}}:=\int_{\widetilde{C}^u}\mathfrak{l}|_{W^s(x,\widetilde{C})}\, d\zeta|_{\widetilde{C}^u}(x).
$ 
We claim that there is a measure $\nu_\xi$ on ${\mathsf{St}}$ such that $\nu_{\xi,\widetilde{C}}=\nu_\xi|_{\widetilde{C}}$ for all $\widetilde{C}$. If  
 $\widetilde{C},\widetilde{D}\in\mathfs G$ intersect with positive measure, then either $\widetilde{C}\subset\widetilde{D}$ or
 $\widetilde{D}\subset \widetilde{C}$, and  $j(\widetilde{D})=j(\widetilde{C})$, $|D^s|=|C^s|$, and  $a_0(\widetilde{C})=a_0(\widetilde{D})$. So
 $\zeta_{\widetilde{D}^u}|_{\widetilde{C}\cap\widetilde{D}}=\zeta_{\widetilde{C}^u}|_{\widetilde{C}\cap\widetilde{D}}$,  and $(\nu_{\xi,{\widetilde{C}}})|_{\widetilde{C}\cap \widetilde{D}}=\nu_{\xi,\widetilde{D}}|_{\widetilde{C}\cap\widetilde{D}}$.  Thus  $\nu_{\xi,\widetilde{C}}$ $(\widetilde{C}\in\mathfs G)$ have a common extension $\nu_\xi$. Clearly, $\nu_{\xi}$ is locally finite, locally flow invariant on $\mathfs G$, and  $\nu_\xi(\widetilde{C})=M_\xi(\widetilde{C})$ for all $\widetilde{C}\in\mathfs G$.

Every extension of $M_\xi$ to a measure which is  locally flow invariant on $\mathfs G$ must induce the same flux measure on $\widetilde{C}^u$, and is therefore  equal to $\nu_\xi$.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- lem-43: body_md -->
\label{l.Lemma-nu-xi-is-BL-measure}
Fix $T_k\to\infty$ and $\widetilde{\omega}\in{\mathsf{St}}$ whose forward $\phi$ orbit
does not hit a singularity, and suppose there is a locally finite  measure $\nu$ which is locally flow-invariant in $\mathfs G$, and so that for any  pair $(h_1,h_2)$ of indicator functions of sets in $\mathfs G$, 
$\int h_i d\nu\neq 0$, and 
\begin{equation}\label{e.RET}
\frac{\int_{0}^{T_k} h_1(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))\,dt}{\int_{0}^{T_k} h_2(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))\,dt}\xrightarrow[T\to\infty]{}\frac{\int h_1 d\nu}{\int h_2 d\nu};
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{e.BL-eqn}
\nu(h_i\circ D)=e^{\xi}\nu(h_i).
\end{equation}
Then   $\nu=\operatorname{const}\mu_\xi$ (whence $\nu$ is $\phi$-ergodic and invariant), and  
\eqref{e.RET}--\eqref{e.BL-eqn} hold for any pair of continuous functions with compact support such that $\int h_2 d\nu>0$.
<!-- end lem-43 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
Suppose $\widetilde{C}\in\mathfs G$. By \eqref{e.RET}, the orbit of ${\widetilde{\omega}}$
enters $\widetilde{C}$ and $\widetilde{C}^c$ infinitely many times. Therefore it crosses $\widetilde{C}$ infinitely many times. Each crossing takes a constant time equal to the length of the $E^s_0$-side of $\widetilde{C}$. 

Thus, if $h=1_{\widetilde{C}}$, then 
\begin{equation}\label{e.RET-conservative}
\int_{0}^\infty h(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))\,dt=\infty.
\end{equation}


By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Cylinder-Area}, the elements of  $\mathfs G_k$ are rectangles   with ``long``  $E^s_0$-side of length $\asymp 1$, and ``short`` $E^u_0$-side with length $O(\lambda^{-k})$. 
Call a piece of $\widetilde{C}$ cut by maximal $E^u_0$ segments in $\widetilde{C}$ an {\em $E^u_0$-slice}. Slices of elements of $\mathfs G_k$ are rectangles with $E^u_0$-sides of length $O(\lambda^{-k})$, and $E^s_0$-sides  which could be arbitrarily narrow.
Thus 
$
\mathfs H:=\{\textrm{$E^u_0$-slices of sets in $\mathfs G$}\}
$ generates the Borel $\sigma$-algebra. 

Let  $\widetilde{D}$ be an $E^u$-slice of $\widetilde{C}\!\in\!\mathfs G$. 
 $E^s_0$ is the direction of the flow, and geometric considerations show that  
$
\displaystyle \int_0^{T_k}\! 1_{\widetilde{D}}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt=\rho
{\int_0^{T_k} 1_{\widetilde{C}}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}+O(1)$,  where $\displaystyle\rho=\frac{\ell^s(\widetilde{D})}{\ell^s(\widetilde{C})}$.
By the local flow invariance, $\displaystyle \rho=\frac{\nu(\widetilde{D})}{\nu(\widetilde{C})}$, and by \eqref{e.RET-conservative}, 
$
\displaystyle \frac{\int_{0}^{T_k} 1_{\widetilde{D}}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))\,dt}{\int_{0}^{T_k} 1_{\widetilde{C}}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))\,dt}\xrightarrow[T\to\infty]{}\frac{\nu(\widetilde{D})}{\nu(\widetilde{C})}.
$

Repeating this argument for other slices of other elements of $\mathfs G$, and employing \eqref{e.RET} for pairs of indicators of  $\mathfs G$-elements, we deduce that  \eqref{e.RET} holds for all pairs of indicators of {\em slices} of   $\mathfs G$-elements. 

Since one can cover ${\mathsf{St}}^\ast$ by slices of $\mathfs G$-elements of { uniformly small diameter}, a standard approximation argument gives \eqref{e.RET} and  \eqref{e.RET-conservative} for all pairs of continuous functions with compact support and positive integrals. 

By \eqref{e.RET-conservative},  $\nu$ must be $\phi$-invariant.
The ergodic components of $\nu$ are all locally finite  measures.
By \cite{Hooper-Hubert-Weiss}, every $\phi$-ergodic invariant locally finite measure is proportional to $\mu_\xi$. Thus, by the ergodic decomposition theorem for conservative $\sigma$-finite invariant measures, there is a probability  measure $\eta$ on $\mathbb R$ such that 
$
\nu=\int_\mathbb R \mu_{\xi'}d\eta(\xi').
$
Recall that $D$ is the deck transformation which increases the ${\mathfrak{z}}$-coordinate by one.  If $\nu\circ D=e^{\xi}\nu$ on $\mathfs G$, then $\nu\circ D^j=e^{j\xi}\nu$ on $\mathfs G$ for all $j\in\mathbb Z$ (because $\mathfs G$ is $D$-invariant). Thus for every $\widetilde{C}\in\mathfs G$, $e^{j\xi}\nu(\widetilde{C})=\int_\mathbb R e^{j\xi'}\mu_{\xi'}(\widetilde{C})d\eta(\xi')$ for all $j\in\mathbb Z$. Necessarily, $\eta$ is the point mass at $\xi$,  $\nu$ is proportional to $\mu_\xi$, and $\nu$ is ergodic.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
Recall that $\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0=\widetilde{\Psi}_{nN_0}$. 
Suppose $\xi\in\mathbb R$, $\eta_N\to\xi$, and  $\mathcal P_{N}'(\eta_N)=z_{N}({\widetilde{\omega}})$. Specializing to the subsequence $N_n=nN_0$ and applying  Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}, we obtain finite numbers $\xi_n\to\xi$ such that $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)=z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})$. 





Fix $0<\varepsilon<0.01$, $k\geq 1$, and a  constant $L_0$ so large that for every $n$, any pure $E^s_n$-segment of depth $k$ has length less than $\varepsilon L_0$. This is possible by \eqref{e.c-over}. 


Let $A_T:=\{\phi^t(\widetilde\omega):0<t<T\}$.  Arguing as in the proof of the temporal CLT in Section \ref{ScProofBeck}, there is a  global constant $c>4$                               
and natural numbers $n=n(T)\asymp \log T$ $(T>0)$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{e.n(T)}
A_T^\ast:=(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(A_T) 
\textrm{  has length in $[L_0,cL_0]$.  }
\end{equation}
Since $|A_T^\ast|\leq cL_0$ is bounded and $|\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n-{\mathfrak{z}}|$ is uniformly bounded, 
$$
\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n(\cdot)=z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})+O(1)\textrm{ uniformly on }A_T^\ast.
$$

We denote the uniform distribution on $A_T^\ast$ by ${\mathbb{P}}_{A^\ast_T}$.  Since $\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0:A_T\to A_T^\ast$ is  affine, for every $\widetilde{C}\in\mathfs G$, 
\begin{align}
&\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T 1_{\widetilde{C}}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt=\frac{|A_T\cap \widetilde{C}|}{|A_T|}=\frac{|A_T^\ast\cap (\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{C})|}{|A_T^\ast|}\notag
\\
&={\mathbb{P}}_{A_T^\ast}\left\{\widetilde{\omega}'\in A_T^\ast:  (\widetilde{\psi}_0^{-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}^{-1})(\widetilde{\omega}')\in\widetilde{C}
\right\}.\label{e.sirena}
\end{align}

By Lemma \ref{l.approx-by-pure-segments}, we can approximate $A_T^\ast$  by finite unions of pure $E^s_n$-segments $W_{n,i}$ of  depth  $k$, which intersect $A_T^\ast$, and so that 
$$
\displaystyle 
\bigcup_{i=1}^{m_n}W_{n,i}\subset A_T^\ast\subset \bigcup_{i=1}^{m_n+2}W_{n,i}\ ; \  \frac{1}{|A_T^\ast|}\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}|W_{n,i}|{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}(\cdot)\leq {\mathbb{P}}_{A_T^\ast}(\cdot)\leq  \frac{1}{|A_T^\ast|}\sum_{i=1}^{m_n+2}|W_{n,i}|{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}(\cdot)
.
$$
Since $W_{n,i}\cap A_T^\ast\neq \varnothing$ and $|W_{n,i}|=O(1)$, their  heights satisfy $z_n(W_{n,i})=z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})+O(1)$. 


Thus, for any pair of sets $\widetilde{C}_1,\widetilde{C}_2\in\mathfs G$, 
\begin{align*}
&\frac{\int_0^T 1_{\widetilde{C}_1}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}
{\int_0^T 1_{\widetilde{C}_2}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}=
\frac{{\mathbb{P}}_{A^\ast_T}[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{C}_1)]}{{\mathbb{P}}_{A^\ast_T}[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{C}_2)]}\leq 
\frac{\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m_n+2}|W_{n,i}|{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{C}_1)]}{\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m_n}|W_{n,i}|{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{C}_2)]}\\
&\leq [1+o(1)]\frac{M_\xi(\widetilde{C}_1)}{M_\xi(\widetilde{C}_2)}\left[1+\frac{\sum_{i=m_n+1}^{m_n+2}|W_{n,i}|{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{C}_2)]}{\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}|W_{n,i}|{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{C}_2)]}
\right],\textrm{ by \eqref{e.engine2}}\\
&\leq [1+o(1)]\frac{M_\xi(\widetilde{C}_1)}{M_\xi(\widetilde{C}_2)}\left[1
+O\left(\frac{\sum_{i=m_n+1}^{m_n+2}|W_{n,i}|}{\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}|W_{n,i}|}\right)
\right],\textrm{ by \eqref{e.engine2bis}.}
   
                                                           
\end{align*}
By the choice of $L_0$,  
$\displaystyle \frac{\sum_{i=m_n+1}^{m_n+2}|W_{n,i}|}
{\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}|W_{n,i}|}\leq \frac{2\varepsilon L_0}{L_0-2\varepsilon L_0}<\frac{2\varepsilon}{1-2\varepsilon}
<3\varepsilon.$ So 
$$
\limsup_{T\to\infty} \frac{\int_0^T 1_{\widetilde{C}_1}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}
{\int_0^T 1_{\widetilde{C}_2}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}\leq \frac{M_\xi(\widetilde{C}_1)}{M_\xi(\widetilde{C}_2)}[1+O(\varepsilon)]=\frac{\nu_\xi(\widetilde{C}_1)}{\nu_\xi(\widetilde{C}_2)}[1+O(\varepsilon)],
$$
with $\nu_\xi$ as in Lemma \ref{l.Extending-M-xi}.
By symmetry, $\displaystyle \liminf_{T\to\infty} \frac{\int_0^T 1_{\widetilde{C}_1}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}
{\int_0^T 1_{\widetilde{C}_2}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}\geq \frac{\nu_\xi(\widetilde{C}_1)}{\nu_\xi(\widetilde{C}_2)}[1-O(\varepsilon)]$, 
and since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary,
$\displaystyle
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^T 1_{\widetilde{C}_1}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}
{\int_0^T 1_{\widetilde{C}_2}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}=\frac{\nu_\xi(\widetilde{C}_1)}{\nu_\xi(\widetilde{C}_2)},
$ for all $\widetilde{C}_1,\widetilde{C}_2\in\mathfs G$. 

This shows that $\nu_\xi$ satisfies condition \eqref{e.RET} of Lemma \ref{l.Lemma-nu-xi-is-BL-measure}. 
Condition \eqref{e.BL-eqn} holds as well, because $\nu_\xi|_{\mathfs G}=M_\xi$ and $M_\xi\circ D=e^\xi M_\xi$ by construction.
By Lemma \ref{l.Lemma-nu-xi-is-BL-measure}, $\widetilde{\omega}$ is generic for $\mu_\xi$.
This proves the first part of Proposition \ref{PrBulk}. 

\medskip
Suppose there are integers $N_k\to\infty$ and finite numbers  $\xi,\eta_{N_k}\in\mathbb R$  such that $\eta_{N_k}\to\xi$ and $\mathcal P_{N_k}'(\eta_{N_k})=z_{N_k}({\widetilde{\omega}})$. Let $N_0$ be the constant from \eqref{e.mat-prod-form}, and set $n_k:=\lfloor{N_k/N_0}\rfloor$. By Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}, there are  $\xi_{n_k}\to\xi$ such that $\mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(\xi_{n_k})=z_{N_k}({\widetilde{\omega}})$. 

Build the sequence of times $T_k\to\infty$ such that the length of 
$(\widetilde{\psi}_{n_k-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(A_{T_{n_k}})$ is between $L_0$ and $cL_0$. Proceeding as before, we  can show that 
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^{T_k} 1_{\widetilde{C}_1}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}
{\int_0^{T_k} 1_{\widetilde{C}_2}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}=\frac{\nu_\xi(\widetilde{C}_1)}{\nu_\xi(\widetilde{C}_2)}
\textrm{ for all $\widetilde{C}_1,\widetilde{C}_2\in\mathfs G$. }
$$
By Lemma \ref{l.Lemma-nu-xi-is-BL-measure}, $\nu_\xi$ is a historical measure of ${\widetilde{\omega}}$.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- prop-12: body_md -->
\label{PrEdge} If $\xi_N(\widetilde{\omega})$ does not converge to a finite limit as $N\to\infty$, then 
                                         
${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is not generic for any $\phi$-ergodic invariant locally finite measure on ${\mathsf{St}}.$
<!-- end prop-12 -->
<!-- lem-44: body_md -->
\label{l.Pure-Seg-Ratio-Edge-Case}
For every $Z_0>0$ there exists a constant $M_0$ as follows. 
Suppose
 $n_s$ is a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers, and 
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item 
$z_{n_s}$ is a sequence of integers such that for all $R>0$, for all $s$ large enough, either $z_{n_s}=\mathsf{P}_{n_s}'(\xi_{n_s})$ with $\xi_{n_s}>R$, or  $z_{n_s}\geq \lim\limits_{t\to +\infty}\mathsf{P}_{n_s}'(t)$;
\item $W_{n_s}, \overline{W}_{n_s}$ are two sequences of pure $E^s_{n_s}$-segments of bounded depths, and with heights $z_{n_s}(W_{n_s})$, $z_{n_s}(\overline{W}_{n_s})$  such that  $|z(W_{n_s})-z_{n_s}|, 
|z(\overline{W}_{n_s})-z_{n_s}|\leq Z_0$;  
\item ${\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n_s}}
[ (\widetilde{\psi}_{n_s-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{F}_0)]$ is positive for all $s$ large, where $\widetilde{F}_0=[\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0=0]$.
\end{enumerate}
 Then $\displaystyle {\mathbb{P}}_{\overline{W}_{n_s}}\left[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n_s-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)
 \left(\bigcup_{\ell=-M_0}^{M_0}D^{-\ell}\widetilde{F}_0\right)\right]$ is positive for all $s$ large, and 
 \begin{equation}\label{e.P-ratio}
 \lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n_s}}[
 (\widetilde{\psi}_{n_s-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{F}_0)]}
 {{\mathbb{P}}_{\overline{W}_{n_s}}[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n_s-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)
