 (\bigcup_{\ell=-M_0}^{M_0}D^{\ell}\widetilde{F}_0)]}=0.
 \end{equation}
The same conclusion holds if (a) is replaced by 
\begin{enumerate}[(a')]
\item
$z_{n_s}$ is a sequence of integers such that for all $R>0$, for all $s$ large enough, either 
$z_{n_s}=\mathsf{P}_{n_s}'(\xi_{n_s})$ with $\xi_{n_s}<-R$, or  $z_{n_s}\leq \lim\limits_{t\to -\infty}\mathsf{P}_{n_s}'(t)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-44 -->
<!-- sublem-8: body_md -->
\label{sl.blocks}
For all $L$ large enough, $\{0,\ldots, n\}$ splits into  segments $I_1,\ldots,I_{\nu_n}$, 
listed in increasing order, such that
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item For all $p\neq \nu_n$, $\displaystyle L\leq \mathrm{Var}\biggl(\sum_{n\in I_p}f_n(X_n)\biggr)\leq 2L$; 
                  
\item For all $p$, $\displaystyle 
 \bigg|{\rm Cov}\biggl(\sum_{n\in I_p} f_n(X_n), \sum_{m\not\in I_p} f_m(X_m)\biggr)\bigg|\leq 0.01 L$;
                  
\item 
$\displaystyle\sup_n ({\max_{1\leq p\leq \nu_n}} |I_p|/L)<\infty$;  
$\displaystyle\inf_n ({ \min_{1\leq p\leq \nu_n-1}} |I_p|/L)>0$; and  $\nu_n\asymp n$.
 \end{enumerate}
<!-- end sublem-8 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
The proof relies on the  exponential $\rho$-mixing property of $\{X_i\}_{i\geq 1}$ (Corollary \ref{Cor-rho-mixing}):  There exist constants $C_{mix}>1$ and $0<\rho<1$ such that for all $i,j$, 
$$
|\mathrm{Cov}(f_i(X_i),f_j(X_j))|\leq C_{mix}K^2\rho^{|i-j|}.
$$ 

Given integers $0<m<n$, let  $\displaystyle V_{m,n}:=\mathrm{Var}\bigl(\sum_{m< i\leq n}f_i(X_i)\bigr)$ and $V_k:=V_{1,k}$. Then 
$\displaystyle
V_{m,n}\geq V_n-V_m-\sum_{i=1}^{m}
\sum_{j=m+1}^n
C_{mix}K^2\rho^{j-i}\geq V_n-V_m-\operatorname{const}.
$ By  Proposition \ref{Prop-Var-Growth}, $V_n\asymp n$. 
Fixing $m$ and letting $n\to\infty$, we obtain
$V_{m,n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\infty$ for each $m$. 

At the same time, 
$\displaystyle
|V_{m,j+1}-V_{m,j}|\leq 2\sum_{i=m}^{j+1} |\mathrm{Cov}(f_{i}(X_{i}),f_{j+1}(X_{j+1}))|\leq \frac{C_{mix}K^2}{1-\rho} 
$. 
So 
\begin{equation}
\label{VmnIneq}
V_{m,n}\leq C_{mix}K^2(1-\rho)^{-1}(n-m).
\end{equation}



Suppose  $L>200C_{mix}K^2(1-\rho)^{-2}$. Then $V_{1,2}\leq L$, and by the previous  estimates there is some $n_1$ such that $L\leq V_{1,n_1}\leq 2L$. We let $I_1:=\{1,2,\ldots,n_1\}$. Similarly $V_{n_1+1,n_1+2}\leq L$, and there is $n_2>n_1$ such that $L\leq V_{n_1+1,n_2}\leq 2L$. Proceeding by induction, we obtain a partition of $\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ into increasing integer segments $I_1,\ldots,I_{\nu_n}$ which satisfy the first part  of the sublemma. 
 
The second part holds as well,  because  if $I_p=\{a,a+1,\ldots,b\}$, then
\begin{align*}
&\bigg|\mathrm{Cov}\biggl(\sum_{n\in I_p} f_n(X_n),\sum_{n\not\in I_p} f_n(X_n)\biggr)\bigg|\leq C_{mix}K^2\sum_{n=a}^b\biggl(\sum_{m=1}^{a-1}\rho^{n-m}+\sum_{m=b+1}^{\infty}
\rho^{m-n}\biggr)\\
&\leq 2C_{mix}K^2(1-\rho^{-1})^2<0.01 L.
\end{align*} 

 Let $|I_p|$ denote the ``length" (i.e. cardinality) of $I_p$, and let  
$\displaystyle V(I_p):=\mathrm{Var}\bigl(\sum_{j\in I_p}f(X_j)\bigr)$. 
 By the variance growth theorem for uniformly elliptic Markov chains 
 (Theorem \ref{LmVarCycles})
                                           
 there are constants $C_1,C_2$ (depending only on $K$ and the ellipticity constant ${\varepsilon}_0$ from Proposition~\ref{Prop-Doeblin}) such that 
$$
V(I_p)\geq C_1^{-1}\sum_{j\in I_p}u_j^2-C_2,\textrm{ where $u_j$ are the structure constants in \eqref{e.u}. }
$$
We saw in the proof of Lemma \ref{Lemma-D_N-Growth} that there exists a constant $m_0>0$ (independent of $n$ and $p$) so that for all $j$ there is $j\leq j'\leq j+m_0$ and an admissible hexagon at position $j'+2$ with non-zero balance (see p. \pageref{page-hexagon-claim}). The balance is an integer, so by Lemma \ref{lemma-Hex-Meas}, there is a positive constant $c_0$ such that $u_{j'}^2\geq c_0$.
Since the gaps between $j'$s such that $u_{j'}^2\geq c_0$ are of size less than $m_0$, $\sum_{j\in I_p}u_j^2\geq c_0(|I_p|-m_0)/m_0$, whence 
$$
2L\geq V(I_p)\geq C_1^{-1}c_0\frac{|I_p|-m_0}{m_0}-C_2.
$$
Taking $L$ much larger than $C_2+1$, we obtain $|I_p|\leq \operatorname{const} L$. 

By construction,  for all $p\!\!<\!\!\nu_n$, $V(I_p)\!\!\geq\!\! L$. 
By \eqref{VmnIneq}
$V(I_p)\leq C_{mix}K^2(1-\rho)^{-1}|I_p|$. So for all segments except perhaps the last one, 
$
|I_p|\geq \operatorname{const} L.
$
All constants are independent of $L$ and $n$.

It immediately follows that for fixed $L$, the number of segments is bounded above and below by constants time $n$.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- sublem-9: body_md -->
\label{sl.sub-optimal-exist}
 If $L$ is sufficiently large, then   for each $p<\nu_n$, for each optimal $I_p$  there exists
                                         
  a sub-optimal block with the same endpoints as $I_p$.
<!-- end sublem-9 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
Let $m_0$ be an  upper bound  for the gaps in the set  
 $$\{j\geq 3: \exists\textrm{  hexagons in $\mathrm{Hex}(j)$ with non-zero balance}\}$$ (see the proof of Claim 2 on page \pageref{page-hexagon-claim}).  By Sublemma \ref{sl.blocks}, the length of all the segments except perhaps the last one is bounded below by a constant times $L$. We choose $L$ so large, that $|I_p|>m_0+100$ for all $p$ except perhaps the last one. 

 
Suppose $I_p=\{a,a+1,\ldots,b\}$, and  $(x_a,\ldots,x_b)$ is optimal.
 Since $|I_p|>m_0+100$, 
 there exists some $\displaystyle a+4\leq i\leq b-3$,
and some hexagon $\left(y_{i-2} \begin{array}{cc} y_{i-1} & y_i\\
z_{i-1} & z_i
\end{array} z_{i+1}\right)\in \mathrm{Hex}(i)$ with non-zero balance. 
By  uniform ellipticity (Proposition \ref{Prop-Doeblin})
$$
\exists b_{i-3}\textrm{ such that } {\mathbb{P}}[(X_{i-4},X_{i-3},X_{i-2})=(x_{i-4},b_{i-3},y_{i-2})]\neq 0,$$
$$\exists b_{i+2}\textrm{ such that } {\mathbb{P}}[(X_{i+1},X_{i+2},X_{i+3})=(z_{i+1},b_{i+2},x_{i+3})]\neq 0.$$ 
By the Markov property, the following two blocks belong to $\Sigma(I_p)$:
$$
\underline{y}:=(x_a,\ldots,x_{i-4};b_{i-3};\ \ \ y_{i-2},y_{i-1},y_i,z_{i+1}\ \ \ ;  
 b_{i+2}; x_{i+3},\ldots,x_b);
$$
$$
\underline{z}:=(x_a,\ldots,x_{i-4} ;b_{i-3};\ \ \ y_{i-2},z_{i-1},z_i,z_{i+1}\  \ \ ; 
 b_{i+2} ; x_{i+3},\ldots,x_b).
$$
Since the balance of $\left(y_{n-2} \begin{array}{cc} y_{n-1} & y_n\\
z_{n-1} & z_n
\end{array} z_{n+1}\right)$ is not zero,  the sums $\displaystyle \sum_{i\in I_p}f_i$ along $\underline{y}$ and $\underline{z}$ are different. Therefore, at least one of $\underline{y},\underline{z}$ is sub-optimal.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- sublem-10: body_md -->
\label{sl.ManyMax}Given $\underline{x}\in\Omega^n$, let  $e_n(\underline{x})$ denote the number of segments $I_p$ inside $[0, n-k]$ such that $(x_i)_{i\in I_p}$ is sub-optimal. 
Then 
\begin{equation}
\label{ManyMax}
 \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n}\max \{e_n(\underline{x}):\underline{x}\in\Omega^n\}=0.
\end{equation}
<!-- end sublem-10 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
Assume by contradiction that \eqref{ManyMax} is false. Then  for some $\delta>0$,  there are $n_j\to\infty$ and  
$\underline{x}^{(j)} \in \Omega^{n_j}$ such that
${e_{n_j}(\underline{x}^{(j)})}>\delta{n_j}.$


We replace each sub-optimal $(x_i^{(j)})_{i\in I_p}$ in $[0,n_j-k]$ by an optimal block $(y_i)_{i\in I_p}$ with the same endpoints. The result is a word $\underline{y}\in\Sigma^n$ such that for all $j$ large enough,
$$
\sum_{i=0}^{n_j} f_i(y_i)\geq \sum_{i=0}^{n_j} f_i(x_i^{(j)})+e_{n_j}(\underline{x}^{(j)})\geq \widehat{z}_{n_j}+\delta n_j\equiv z_{n_j}(W_{n_j})+\delta n_j\equiv z_{n_j}+\delta n_j+O(1). 
$$
 Therefore, for all $j$ large enough,
 $\displaystyle \sum_{i=0}^{n_j} f_i(y_i)>z_{n_j}+\frac{1}{2}\delta n_j$.
Thus there exists an integer $m_j\geq \frac{1}{2}\delta n_j$ such that 
$\displaystyle {\mathbb{P}}(S_{n_j}=z_{n_j}+m_j)\!\neq \!0 $. 
Since the non-zero transition probabilities of $\{X_i\}$ are bounded away from zero 
(Proposition \ref{Prop-Markov-Kernel}), there exists  $\varkappa>0$ such that 
$$\displaystyle {\mathbb{P}}(S_{n_j}=z_{n_j}+m_j)\geq e^{-\varkappa n_j}.$$

Fix  $R>6\varkappa/\delta$. The function $F_n(t):=\log \mathbb E(e^{t S_n})$ is  convex,  analytic,  $F_n(0)=0$, and  $F_{n_j}(R)\geq \log(e^{R(z_{n_j}+m_j)}{\mathbb{P}}[S_{n_j}=z_{n_j}+m_j])>R(z_{n_j}+m_j)-\varkappa n_j\geq R \bigl(z_{n_j}+\frac{1}{3}\delta n_j\bigr)
 $, whence by convexity, 
$$F_{n_j}'(R)\geq \frac{F_{n_j}(R)-F_{n_j}(0)}{R}\geq z_{n_j}+\frac{1}{3}\delta n_j.$$
Employing \eqref{Pres1stDerLM} on the interval $[-R,R]$, we find that for all $j$ sufficiently large, 
$
\mathsf{P}_{n_j}'(R)\!\!\geq \!\! z_{n_j}.
$
 By strict convexity, $z_{n_j}\!\!<\!\! \limsup\limits_{t\to\infty}P_{n_j}'(t)$,  whence by condition (a), 
 for all $j$ large enough, there exists $\xi_{n_j}$  with $z_{n_j}\!\!=\!\!\mathsf{P}_{n_j}'(\xi_{n_j})$.  Now the strict monotonicity of $\mathsf{P}_{n_j}'$ implies that $\xi_{n_j}\!\!<\!\!R$ contradicting condition (a).
This contradiction proves \eqref{ManyMax}.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- sublem-11: body_md -->
\label{sl.DownSlope}                                              
                 
                  
$\displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{{\mathbb{P}}((X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in\Omega^n)}{{\mathbb{P}}((X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in{\widehat\Omega}^n(M))}=0.$
<!-- end sublem-11 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
We show that there are positive constants $c,\mathsf K, n_J$ $(J\in\mathbb N)$ so that
for each $J\in\mathbb N$ and $n>n_J$, there exist a subset ${\overline\Omega}^n \subset \Omega^n$
and $J$  maps
$ \displaystyle \Theta_1, \Theta_2, \dots, \Theta_J:{\overline\Omega}^n\mapsto  {\widehat\Omega}^n(M)$ as follows:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item  ${\mathbb{P}}[(X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in {\overline\Omega}^n]\geq (1/2){\mathbb{P}}[(X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in \Omega^n]$;
\item $\Theta_1({\overline\Omega}^n),\ldots, \Theta_J({\overline\Omega}^n)$ are  pairwise disjoint;
 \item For every $\underline{x}\in {\overline\Omega}^n$, $\mu_n(\Theta_j(\underline{x}))\geq c\mu_n(\underline{x})$;
\item Each point in the image of $\Theta_j$ has at most $\mathsf{K}$ 
$\Theta_j$-preimages.
\end{enumerate}

To see why this implies the sublemma, take $n>n_J$ and  use  (d) to split
$\displaystyle
{\overline\Omega}^n=\biguplus_{\ell=1}^{\mathsf K}{\overline\Omega}^n_{j,\ell}$ so that $\Theta_j$   is injective on each ${\overline\Omega}^n_{j,\ell}$. (We allow some of these sets to be empty. No deep measurable selection theorems are needed here,  ${\overline\Omega}^n$ is a finite set.) Then:
  \begin{align*}
 &{\mathbb{P}}[(X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in\widehat{\Omega}^n(M)]=\mu_n[\widehat{\Omega}_n(M)]\geq \sum_{j=1}^J \mu_n[\Theta_j({\overline\Omega}^n)],\textrm{ by (b)}\\
 &\geq \sum_{j=1}^J \int \frac{1}{\mathsf{K}}\sum_{\ell=1}^{\mathsf K}1_{\Theta_{j}({\overline\Omega}^n_{j,\ell})}\, d\mu_n=\frac{1}{\mathsf{K}}\sum_{j=1}^J \sum_{\ell=1}^{\mathsf K}\mu_n[{\Theta_j({\overline\Omega}_{j,\ell})}]\\
&\geq \frac{1}{\mathsf{K}}\sum_{j=1}^J \sum_{\ell=1}^{\mathsf K}c\mu_n[{\overline\Omega}_{j,\ell}],\textrm{ by (c) and the injectivity of $\Theta_j$ on ${\overline\Omega}_{j,\ell}$}\\
&=\frac{1}{\mathsf K} \sum_{j=1}^J c\mu_n({\overline\Omega}^n)=\frac{cJ}{\mathsf K}\mu_n({\overline\Omega}^n)=\frac{cJ}{\mathsf K}{\mathbb{P}}[(X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in {\overline\Omega}^n]
\\&
\geq \frac{cJ}{2\mathsf K}{\mathbb{P}}[(X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in \Omega^n] , \textrm{ by }(a). 
 \end{align*}
Thus $\displaystyle\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{{\mathbb{P}}((X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in\Omega^n)}{{\mathbb{P}}((X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in{\widehat\Omega}^n(M))}\leq \frac{2\mathsf K}{cJ}$ for all $J$, and the limit  must be zero.
 
We now construct $\Theta_1, \dots, \Theta_J.$
Call a {segment $I_j$} {\em typical} if \index{Typical segment}\index{Atypical segment}
$$
{\mathbb{P}}\left(\textrm{$(X_i)_{i\in I_j}$ is optimal}\big| (X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in \Omega^n \right)\geq c_J:=1-1/(10J),
$$
and {\em atypical} otherwise. 

The frequency of atypical segments tends to zero:
\begin{align*}
&\frac{1}{\nu_n}
\sum_{p=1}^{\nu_n}1_{\{j:I_j\textrm{ is atypical}\}}(p)\leq \frac{1}{\nu_n}\sum_{p=1}^{\nu_n}\frac{{\mathbb{P}}[(X_i)_{i\in I_p}\textrm{ is {\em sub}-optimal}|(X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in\Omega^n]}{1-c_J}\\
&=10J\mathbb E\left(\frac{1}{\nu_n}\sum_{p=1}^{\nu_n}1_{[(X_i)_{i\in I_p}\textrm{ is sub-optimal}]}(X_0,\ldots,X_n)\bigg|(X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in\Omega^n\right)\\
&\leq 10J\cdot \frac{n}{\nu_n}\cdot \frac{1}{n}\max_{\Omega^n}(e_n+k)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0\textrm{ by \eqref{ManyMax}, and since $\nu_n\asymp n$}. 
\end{align*} 

Necessarily, the frequency of typical segments tends to one. Fix $J\in\mathbb N$. Then for all $n$ sufficiently large, the first $J$ typical segments $I_{j_1},\ldots,I_{j_J}$ are all inside $[0,n-k-2]\cap[0,n-\overline{k}-2]$. Let
\begin{align*}
&{\overline\Omega}^n:=\{\underline{x} \in \Omega^n:  (x_i)_{i\in I_p}\textrm{ is optimal for every }p=j_1, \dots, j_J\},
\end{align*}
then ${\mathbb{P}}[(X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in {\overline\Omega}^n\, |\, (X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in \Omega^n]$
\begin{align*}
&\geq 1-\sum_{p\in \{j_1,\ldots,j_J\}} {\mathbb{P}}[(X_i)_{i\in I_{p}}\textrm{ is sub-optimal}\, |\, (X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in \Omega^n]\\
&\geq 1-J(1-c_J)\geq 0.9, \textrm{ (the summands are less than $1-c_J$ because of typicality). }
\end{align*}
So ${\mathbb{P}}[(X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in {\overline\Omega}^n]\geq 0.9{\mathbb{P}}[(X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in \Omega^n]$, giving us (a). 


Next we construct $\Theta_i$. 
Impose some arbitrary total order on each set $\mathfrak P_j$. 
For each $1\leq i\leq J$, let $\Theta_i$ be the map on $\overline{\Omega}^n$,  which
\vskip1mm 

\noindent
(1) 
replaces the  $j_i$ block of $\underline{x}\in \overline{\Omega}^n$ by the
lexicographically smallest sub-optimal segment  with the same endpoints. (Such segments exist by Sublemma \ref{sl.sub-optimal-exist}.) 

\vskip1mm 
\noindent
(2) replaces the suffix $(x_{n-\overline{k}-2},\ldots,x_n)$ by             
$(x_{n-\overline{k}-2},b,\underline{b}^{(n)})$, where $b$ is the minimal element of $\mathfrak P_{n-\overline{k}}$ such that 
$\displaystyle 
{\mathbb{P}}[(X_{n-\overline{k}-2},X_{n-\overline{k}-1},X_{n-\overline{k}})\!\!=\!\!(x_{n-\overline{k}-2},
b,{b}^{(n)}_{n-\overline{k}})]\neq 0
$
(such $b$ exists, because of uniform ellipticity.)
\vskip1mm
\noindent
Since $\|f_i\|_\infty\leq K$ and  $\Theta_i$ changes at most $c_1 L+\overline{k}+1$ coordinates, 
 $\Theta_i({\overline\Omega}^n)\subset {\widehat\Omega}^n(M)$. 

  $\Theta_1(\overline{\Omega}^n),\ldots,\Theta_J(\overline{\Omega}^n)$ are pairwise disjoint, since if $k\neq \ell$, then the $j_{k}$-th block in every element of $\Theta_{k}(\overline{\Omega}^n)$ is sub-optimal by construction, whereas the  $j_{k}$-th block in every element of $\Theta_{\ell}(\overline{\Omega}^n)$ is optimal by  choice of ${\overline\Omega}^n$.
  
  The Radon-Nikodym derivatives of  $\Theta_i$ are bounded away from zero by constants independent of $i,J$ and $n$, because $\Theta_i$ changes a bounded number of coordinates whilst respecting the admissibility of transitions, and the (non-zero) transition probabilities of the Markov chain $\{X_i\}$ are uniformly bounded below (Proposition \ref{Prop-Markov-Kernel}). 
  
   The same reasoning, but using the uniform boundedness of $|\mathfrak P_i|$,  allows one to bound the number of preimages of $\Theta_j$.
This completes the proof of (a)--(d).
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- head-7: body_md -->
A calculation similar  to the one leading to \eqref{e.engine3} shows that 
\begin{align*}
&{\mathbb{P}}_{W_n}\bigl[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{F}_0)\bigr]
={\mathbb{P}}_{W_n}\left\{\widetilde{\omega}\in W_n: \begin{array}{l}
                                                                          
\sum\limits_{i=1}^n f_i(X_i^{(n)}(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}})))=z(W_n)=\widehat{z}_n
\end{array}
\right\}\\
&
={\mathbb{P}}\left\{S_n=\widehat{z}_n,(X_{n-k},\ldots,X_n)=\underline{a}^{(n)}
\right\}/\mu_0(\<\underline{a}^{(n)}\>)\\
&={\mathbb{P}}((X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in\Omega^n)/\mu_0(\<\underline{a}^{(n)}\>)\asymp {\mathbb{P}}((X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in\Omega^n),
\end{align*}
because $\mu_0(\<\underline{a}^{(n)}\>)\asymp 1$, since  $\underline{a}^{(n)}$ has constant length.


By our assumptions,  $|z(\overline{W}_n)-\widehat{z}_n|\leq 2Z_0$. Let  $M_0:=M+2Z_0$. Then we also have
\begin{align*}
&{\mathbb{P}}_{\overline{W}_n}\left[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)
\biggl(\bigcup_{\ell=-M_0}^{M_0}
D^\ell \widetilde{F}_0)\biggr)\right]
={\mathbb{P}}_{\overline{W}_n}\left\{\begin{array}{c}
                                                     
|\sum\limits_{i=1}^n f_i(X_i^{(n)}(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}})))-z(\overline{W}_n)|\leq M_0
\end{array}
\right\}\\
&
\geq {\mathbb{P}}\left\{|S_n-\widehat{z}_n|\leq M\ , \ (X_{n-\overline{k}},\ldots,X_n)=\underline{b}^{(n)}
\right\}\big/\mu_0(\<\underline{b}^{(n)}\>)\\
&={\mathbb{P}}\bigl((X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in{\widehat\Omega}^n(M)\bigr)/\mu_0(\<\underline{b}^{(n)}\>)
\asymp {\mathbb{P}}((X_0,\ldots,X_n)\in{\widehat\Omega}^n(M)).
\end{align*}
Equation \eqref{e.P-ratio} now follows from Sublemma \ref{sl.DownSlope}.

This completes the proof assuming condition (a). If we replace (a) by (a'), a similar argument works, except that one needs to reverse the inequality in the definition of optimality in \eqref{e.def-of-optima}, and then update the proof of Sublemma \ref{sl.ManyMax} accordingly, working towards the inequalities $F_{n_j}'(-R)<z_{n_j}-\frac{1}{3}\delta n_j$ and $\mathsf{P}_n'(-R)\leq z_{n_j}$. 
\hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-7 -->
<!-- lem-45: body_md -->
\label{l.Generic-Good-For-Rectangles}
If $\widetilde{\omega}$ is generic for some  $\phi$-ergodic invariant locally finite measure $\mu$, then for any pair of horizontal rectangles ${\mathsf{R}}_i, {\mathsf{R}}_j$ with non-zero measure, 
$$
\displaystyle\frac{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_i}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_j}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}\xrightarrow[T\to\infty]{}\frac{\mu({\mathsf{R}}_i)}{\mu({\mathsf{R}}_j)}, \textrm{ and }\int_0^\infty 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_i}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt=\infty.
$$
A similar statement holds if ${\mathsf{R}}_i, {\mathsf{R}}_j$  are replaced by $D^i(\widetilde{F}_0)$, $D^j(\widetilde{F}_0)$.
<!-- end lem-45 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
The (small) difficulty is that the indicators of ${\mathsf{R}}_k$ and  $D^k(\widetilde{F}_0)$  
$(k=i,j)$ cannot be sandwiched between continuous functions with compact support,  because the singularities on their boundaries do not have compact neighborhoods. 


Geometric considerations
show that $\int_0^T 1_{\partial{\mathsf{R}}_k}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}'))dt=0$ for all $T$ and ${\widetilde{\omega}}'$, therefore by the ratio ergodic theorem, $\mu(\partial{\mathsf{R}}_k)=0$ $(k=i,j)$. 
Divide ${\mathsf{R}}_k$  into three horizontal strips: The top and bottom with width $\varepsilon\in (0,\frac{1}{3})$, and the middle, with width $1-2\varepsilon$. Let $\mathsf M_{\varepsilon,k}$ denote the middle strip. Since $\mu(\partial{\mathsf{R}}_k)=0$,  $\mu(\mathsf M_{k,{\varepsilon}})\xrightarrow[{\varepsilon}\to 0^+]{}\mu({\mathsf{R}}_k)$. 

 $\mathsf M_{\varepsilon,k}$ are bounded away from the singularities of the staircase, so their indicators can be sandwiched between  continuous functions with compact support, and  nearly the same integrals. 
 Therefore, for generic $\widetilde{\omega}$, 
$
\displaystyle \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^T 1_{\mathsf M_{\varepsilon,i}}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}
{\int_0^T 1_{\mathsf M_{\varepsilon,j}}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}
=\frac{\mu(\mathsf M_{\varepsilon,i})}{\mu(\mathsf M_{\varepsilon,j})}.
$
Moreover,  the numerator and denominator tend to infinity (see the proof of \eqref{e.RET-conservative}). Clearly, 
$$
\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_k}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt=(1-2\varepsilon)^{-1}\int_0^T 1_{\mathsf M_{\varepsilon,k}}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt+O(1).
$$ Thus, 
$
\displaystyle\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_i}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}
{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_j}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}
=\frac{\mu(\mathsf M_{\varepsilon,1})}{\mu(\mathsf M_{\varepsilon,2})}
$.
Passing to the limit ${\varepsilon}\to 0$, gives the first part of lemma for horizontal rectangles. The second part $\int_0^\infty 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_k}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt=\infty$ follows, as in the proof of \eqref{e.RET-conservative}. 

The case $D^k(\widetilde{F}_0)$ is handled in a similar way, using the sets $\mathsf M_{\varepsilon,k}$  in Figure \ref{Figure-M-sets}.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
Fix ${\widetilde{\omega}}\in{\mathsf{St}}$, and  define 
$$
\xi_n:=\begin{cases} -\infty & z_n({\widetilde{\omega}})\leq \lim\limits_{t\to -\infty} \mathsf{P}'_n(t)\\
+\infty & z_n({\widetilde{\omega}})\geq \lim\limits_{t\to\infty}\mathsf{P}'_n(t)\\
\textrm{the unique $\xi_n$ s.t.  $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)=z_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$} & z_n({\widetilde{\omega}})\in (\mathsf{P}'(-\infty),\mathsf{P}'_n(+\infty)).
\end{cases}
$$
The definition is proper, because $\mathsf{P}_n'$ is continuous and strictly increasing. 

By Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}, $\xi_N({\widetilde{\omega}})$  (defined in \eqref{e.xi-def}) converges to a finite limit iff $\xi_n$ converges to a finite limit.
Therefore, to prove Proposition \ref{PrEdge} it is sufficient to show that if $\xi_n$ does not converge  to a finite limit, then ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is not generic for any locally finite $\phi$-ergodic invariant measure. 
There are three cases
a to consider:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item  $\{\xi_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ is eventually finite and  bounded, but has  more than one limit point;
 
 \item  $\exists n_k\to\infty$ s.t. $|\xi_{n_k}|<\infty$ and $\xi_{n_k}\to\infty$,  or  $\xi_{n_k}=\infty$ for all $k$.
  
\item  $\exists n_k\to\infty$ s.t. $|\xi_{n_k}|<\infty$ and $\xi_{n_k}\to -\infty$, or  
   $\xi_{n_k}=-\infty$ for all $k$.
 \end{enumerate}
 
 
In case 1,   $\xi_N({\widetilde{\omega}})$ has several finite limit points (Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}),  therefore 
 $\widetilde{\omega}$ has  several different historical measures (Proposition \ref{PrBulk}), and   ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ cannot be generic. Next we consider cases 2 and 3.

Let $A_T({\widetilde{\omega}}):=\{\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}):0<t<T\}$.
Fix $0<{\varepsilon}<1$, $k\geq 1$ and a constant $L_0$ so large that for every $n$, any pure $E^s_n$-segment of depth $\ell$ has length less than ${\varepsilon} L_0$. We saw in the proof of Proposition \ref{PrBulk}, that there is a  constant $c>4$ such that for every $T$ there is $n\asymp\log T$ such that 
$
A_T^\ast({\widetilde{\omega}}):=(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(A_T)$  has length  $|A_T^\ast|\in [L_0,cL_0]$. 

For fixed $n$, $T\mapsto |(\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(A_T)|$ is continuous and strictly increasing. Therefore, for every $n$, there is $T_n$ such that 
$
|A^\ast_{T_n}|\in [L_0,cL_0], \textrm{ and } T_n\to\infty.
$
$T_n$ does not depend on ${\widetilde{\omega}}$. It is completely determined by $c,L_0$, and $\|d\widetilde{\psi}_i|_{E^s_i}\|$ $(i\geq 0)$.

By Lemma \ref{l.approx-by-pure-segments},  one can approximate $A_{T_n}^\ast$ by finite unions of pure $E^s_n$-segments $W_{n,i}$ of bounded depth which intersect $A_{T_n}^\ast$, so that 
$\displaystyle
\bigcup_{i=1}^{K_n} W_{n,i}\subset A^\ast_{T_n}({\widetilde{\omega}})\subset \bigcup_{i=1}^{K_n+2} W_{n,i}
$, and 
\begin{equation}\label{e.approx}
\frac{1}{|A_{T_n}^\ast|}\sum_{i=1}^{K_n}|W_{n,i}|{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}(\cdot)\leq {\mathbb{P}}_{A_{T_n}^\ast}(\cdot)\leq \frac{1}{|A_{T_n}^\ast|}\sum_{i=1}^{K_n+2}|W_{n,i}|{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n,i}}(\cdot).
\end{equation}
$K_n$ is bounded, and since $|W_{n,i}|$ and $|A_{T_n}^\ast|$ are uniformly bounded, there exists $Z_0$ finite so that  $|z_n(W_{n,i})-z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})|\leq Z_0$. (This is certainly true for the canonical $\mathbb Z$-coordinates; For the modified $\mathbb Z$-coordinates, use Lemma \ref{Lemma-Modified-Approx-Canonical}.)

Suppose first that $\exists k_j\uparrow\infty$ such that  ${\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n_{k_j}, i}}((\widetilde{\psi}_{n_{k_j}}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{F}_0))=0$ for each $1\leq i\leq K_{n_{k_j}}+2$. By \eqref{e.approx},  
${\mathbb{P}}_{A_{T_{n_{k_j}}}^\ast}[(\widetilde{\psi}_{n_{k_j}}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{F}_0)]=0$, whence  ${\mathbb{P}}_{A_{T_{n_{k_j}}}}(\widetilde{F}_0)=0$, whence  
$
\int_0^{\infty}1_{\widetilde{F}_0}(\phi^t ({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt=0
$.  
By Lemma \ref{l.Generic-Good-For-Rectangles}, ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is not generic. 

Suppose now that  for every $k$ large enough, there exists some $1\leq i_k\leq N_k+2$ such that   ${\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n_{k_j}, i}}((\widetilde{\psi}_{n_{k_j}}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{F}_0))\neq 0$. 

Then Lemma \ref{l.Pure-Seg-Ratio-Edge-Case} applies  with condition (a) in case 2 and condition (a') in case (3), and there exists a finite union $\widetilde{B}:=\bigcup_{\ell=-M_0}^{M_0}D^\ell\widetilde{F}_0$ such that 
$$
\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\sum\limits_{i=1}^{K_{n_k}+2}|W_{n_k,i}|{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n_k,i}}((\widetilde{\psi}_{n_{k_j}}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{F}_0))}
{{\mathbb{P}}_{W_{n_k,i_k}}((\widetilde{\psi}_{n_{k_j}}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{B}))}=0. 
$$
By \eqref{e.approx}, $\displaystyle\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{{\mathbb{P}}_{A_{T_{n_k}^\ast}}((\widetilde{\psi}_{n_{k_j}}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{F}_0))}
{{\mathbb{P}}_{A_{T_{n_k}^\ast}}((\widetilde{\psi}_{n_{k_j}}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{B}))}=0$, whence 
$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^{T_{n_k}} 1_{\widetilde{F}_0}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega})) dt}
{\int_0^{T_{n_k}} 1_{\widetilde{B}}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}\equiv\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{{\mathbb{P}}_{A_{T_{n_k}}}(\widetilde{F}_0)}{{\mathbb{P}}_{A_{T_{n_k}}}(\widetilde{B})}
=\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{{\mathbb{P}}_{A_{T_{n_k}}}((\widetilde{\psi}_{n_{k_j}}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{F}_0))}
{{\mathbb{P}}_{A_{T_{n_k}}}((\widetilde{\psi}_{n_{k_j}}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{B}))}
=0.
$$
Again, by Lemma \ref{l.Generic-Good-For-Rectangles}, ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ cannot be generic.  
In summary, ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is not generic for any locally finite $\phi$-ergodic invariant measure in any of the cases (1)--(3).
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
\label{RkMesClass}
\normalfont
Corollary \ref{c.Maharam-Measures} states that every locally finite $\phi$-ergodic invariant measure is proportional to a unique measure $\mu_\xi$ such that $\mu_\xi({\mathsf{R}}_0)=1$ and $\mu_\xi\circ D=e^{\xi}\mu_\xi$. We can now give an alternative proof of this claim, assuming $\alpha$ has bounded type. 

Given $\xi\in\mathbb R$, let $\nu_\xi$ denote the unique extension of  $M_\xi$ to a locally finite measure which is locally flow invariant on $\mathfs G$ (Lemma \ref{l.Extending-M-xi}). Looking at the definition of $M_\xi$, we see that $e^{-\xi}M_\xi\circ D=M_\xi$, and $0<M_\xi(\widetilde{F}_0)<\infty$. Since  $\nu_\xi$ is uniquely determined,  $e^{-\xi}\nu_\xi\circ D=\nu_\xi$. 
Also,  $\nu_\xi(\widetilde{F}_0)=M_\xi(\widetilde{F}_0)\in (0,\infty)$, whence $\nu_\xi({\mathsf{R}}_0)\in (0,\infty)$.

Suppose $\mu$ is a locally finite $\phi$-ergodic invariant measure.  Let ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ be a $\mu$-generic point. By Proposition \ref{PrEdge}, $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$ is bounded. The proof of Proposition \ref{PrBulk} shows (without relying on Corollary \ref{c.Maharam-Measures}) that if $\xi$ is a limit point of $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$, then $\nu_\xi$ is a historical measure for ${\widetilde{\omega}}$. But by genericity, the only historical measure for ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is $\mu$. So  $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})\to\xi$,  ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is $\nu_\xi$-generic, and  $\mu$ is proportional to $\nu_\xi$.  Necessarily, $\nu_\xi$ is ergodic and invariant, and we saw above that $\nu_\xi\circ D=e^{\xi}\nu_\xi$ and $0<\nu_\xi({\mathsf{R}}_0)<\infty$.  Setting $\mu_\xi=\nu_\xi/\nu_\xi({\mathsf{R}}_0)$, we obtain the result.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- head-8: body_md -->
It is convenient to start with the second part of the theorem, which says that if $\xi$ is a limit point of $\xi_N({\widetilde{\omega}})$ and  $|\xi|=\infty$, then there are two finite unions of horizontal rectangles $\mathsf F_1,\mathsf F_2$ and a sequence $T_n\to\infty$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{e.Prop-1.31-statement}
\frac{\int_0^{T_n}1_{\mathsf F_1}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}{\int_0^{T_n}1_{\mathsf F_2}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0.
\end{equation}
Suppose $N_k\to\infty$ and $\xi_{N_k}({\widetilde{\omega}})\to\infty$ (this includes the case when $\xi_{N_k}({\widetilde{\omega}})=\infty$ for infinitely many $k$).
Let $n_{k}:=\lfloor N_{k}/N_0\rfloor$. By Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}, for all $k$ large enough either $z_{n_k N_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})\geq \mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(\infty):=\lim\limits_{t\to\infty}\mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(t)$, or  
$z_{n_k N_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})\leq \mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(-\infty):=\lim\limits_{t\to -\infty}\mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(t)$, 
or  $\mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(\eta_{n_k})=z_{n_k N_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})$ for some $\eta_{n_k}$ such that $|\eta_{n_k}|\to\infty$. 


We claim that a similar statement holds for  $D^j(z_{n_k N_0}({\widetilde{\omega}}))$, for any $j\in\mathbb Z$. Fix $j\in\mathbb Z$.  Either for all $k$ large enough
$z_{n_k N_0}(D^j({\widetilde{\omega}}))\geq \mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(\infty)$ or  
$z_{n_k N_0}(D^j({\widetilde{\omega}}))\leq \mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(-\infty)$,  
or $\exists k_i\uparrow\infty$ and  $\exists\eta_{n_{k_i},j}$ such that $\mathsf{P}_{n_{k_i}}'(\eta_{n_{k_i},j})=z_{n_{k_i} N_0}(D^j({\widetilde{\omega}}))$. 

Necessarily, $|\eta_{n_{k_i},j}|\to\infty$. Otherwise (after passing to a further subsequence) $|\eta_{n_{k_i},j}|\leq R$ for all $i$. 
By Proposition \ref{Prop-Var-Growth} and \eqref{Pres2dDer}, there is a constant  $\mathsf C>0$ such that  $\mathsf{P}_n''\geq \mathsf C n$ everywhere on $[-(R+1),(R+1)]$, for all $n>\mathsf C$. If  also $n>|j|/\mathsf C$, then by the mean value theorem,
\begin{align*}
\mathsf{P}_{n_{k_i}}'(R+1)&>\mathsf{P}_{n_{k_i}}'(R)+\mathsf C n\geq \mathsf{P}_{n_{k_i}}'(\eta_{n_{k_i},j})+|j|\\
&=z_{n_{k_i}N_0}(D^j({\widetilde{\omega}}))+|j|= z_{n_{k_i}N_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})+j+|j|\geq z_{n_{k_i}}({\widetilde{\omega}})\\
\mathsf{P}_{n_{k_i}}'(-R-1)&<\mathsf{P}_{n_{k_i}}'(-R)-\mathsf C n\leq \mathsf{P}_{n_{k_i}}'(\eta_{n_{k_i},j})-|j|\\
&=z_{n_{k_i}N_0}(D^j({\widetilde{\omega}}))-|j|= z_{n_{k_i}N_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})+j-|j|\leq z_{n_{k_i}N_0}({\widetilde{\omega}}).
\end{align*}
It follows that the equation  $\mathsf{P}_{n_{k_i}}'(\eta)=z_{n_{k_i}N_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})$ has a solution in $[-(R+1),R+1]$. But the unique solution is $\eta_{n_{k_i}}$, and $|\eta_{n_{k_i}}|\to\infty$. 


Applying a diagonal argument, we obtain a subsequence $n_k^\ast\uparrow \infty$ such that for each $j\in\mathbb Z$, one of the following alternatives holds:
\begin{itemize}
\item $z_{n_k^\ast N_0}(D^j({\widetilde{\omega}}))\geq \mathsf{P}_{n_k^\ast}'(\infty)$ for all $k$ large enough, or
\item $z_{n_k^\ast N_0}(D^j({\widetilde{\omega}}))\leq \mathsf{P}_{n_k^\ast}'(-\infty)$ for all $k$ large enough, or
\item for all $k$ large enough, $z_{n_{k}^\ast N_0}(D^j({\widetilde{\omega}}))=\mathsf{P}_{n_{k}^\ast}'(\eta_{n_{k}^\ast,j})$ for some 
$\eta_{n_{k}^\ast,j}\in\mathbb R$, and $\eta_{n_{k}^\ast,j}$ converges to a limit in $\{-\infty,\infty\}$. 
\end{itemize}





We now argue as in the proof of Proposition \ref{PrEdge}, and construct $T_k\to\infty$ such that 
$|\widetilde{\psi}_{n_k^\ast-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0(A_{T_k})|\in [L_0,cL_0]$ (with $c,L_0$ as in that proof). 
Again, one can use Lemma \ref{l.Pure-Seg-Ratio-Edge-Case} to produce constants $M_j<\infty$ such that 
$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^{T_k} 1_{\widetilde{F}_0}(\phi^t(D^j(\widetilde{\omega}))) dt}
{\int_0^{T_k} 1_{\widetilde{B}_j}(\phi^t(D^j(\widetilde{\omega})))dt}=0,\textrm{ where }
 \widetilde{B}_j:=\bigcup_{|i|\leq M_j}D^i(\widetilde{F}_0).
$$
Since $\phi^t\circ D=D\circ\phi^t$, $\displaystyle
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^{T_k} 1_{D^{-j}\widetilde{F}_0}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega})) dt}
{\int_0^{T_k} 1_{D^{-j}\widetilde{B}_j}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}=0$ for all $j\in\mathbb Z$, and it follows that  for all $N$, 
$\displaystyle
\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^{T_k} 1_{\bigcup_{|j|\leq N}D^{-j}\widetilde{F}_0}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega})) dt}
{\int_0^{T_k} 1_{\bigcup_{|j|\leq N}D^{-j}\widetilde{B}_j}(\phi^t(\widetilde{\omega}))dt}=0.
$

By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Modified-Approx-Canonical}, there is a  constant $N$ such that 
$\displaystyle
\bigcup_{|j|\leq N}D^{-j}\widetilde{F}_0\equiv \big[|\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0|\leq N\big]\!\!\supset\!\! [{\mathfrak{z}}\!\!=\!\!0]\!\!=\!\!{\mathsf{R}}_0$. 
Similarly, there is a constant $N'$ such that 
$\displaystyle \bigcup_{|j|\leq N}D^{-j}\widetilde{B}_j \subset \big[|{\mathfrak{z}}|\leq N'\big]
$. Then \eqref{e.Prop-1.31-statement} holds with $\mathsf F_1:={\mathsf{R}}_0$, and 
$\displaystyle \mathsf F_2:=\bigcup_{|i|\leq N'}{\mathsf{R}}_i$.

\medskip
Next we prove the  first part of the theorem, which says that for every $\xi$ finite, $\xi$ is a limit point of $\xi_N({\widetilde{\omega}})$ iff $\mu_\xi$ is a historical measure of ${\widetilde{\omega}}$. 

Direction ($\Rightarrow$) follows from Proposition \ref{PrBulk}. To see direction $(\Leftarrow)$, suppose $\mu_\xi$ is a historical measure.  
The proof of Lemma \ref{l.Generic-Good-For-Rectangles} can be easily extended to show that for some sequence $T_k\to\infty$, for any pair of horizontal rectangles ${\mathsf{R}}_k, {\mathsf{R}}_\ell$, 
\begin{equation}\label{e.R-k-R-l}
\frac{\int_0^{T_k} 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_k}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}{\int_0^{T_k} 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_\ell}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}\xrightarrow[k\to\infty]{}e^{(k-\ell)\xi}. 
\end{equation}
Define integers $n_k:=n(T_k)$, as in the proof of Propositions \ref{ScBulk} and \ref{ScEdge}, so that $A_{T_k}^\ast:=(\widetilde{\psi}_{n_k-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(A_{T_k})$ has length in $[L_0,cL_0]$. By the argument above, $\xi_{n_k N_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})$ has no infinite limit points. By \eqref{e.R-k-R-l} and the proof of Proposition \ref{ScBulk}, the only possible finite limit point is $\xi$.\hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-8 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
The theorem asserts the equivalence of the  conditions
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is $\mu_\xi$-generic;
\item $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})\to\xi$;
\item $\forall k,\ell\in\mathbb Z$, $\lim\limits_{T\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_k}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_\ell}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}=e^{\xi(k-\ell)}$. 
\end{enumerate}
(a)$\Rightarrow$(b):                                          
By Proposition \ref{PrEdge}, $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$ must converge to a finite limit. By Proposition~\ref{PrBulk}, this limit must be $\xi$.  

\smallskip
\noindent
(b)$\Rightarrow$(a) due to Proposition \ref{ScBulk}.

\smallskip
\noindent
(b)$\Rightarrow$(c) By Proposition \ref{PrBulk}, ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ a generic point of  $\mu_\xi$. By Lemma \ref{l.Generic-Good-For-Rectangles}, 
$$\lim\limits_{T\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_k}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_\ell}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}=\frac{\mu_\xi({\mathsf{R}}_k)}{\mu_\xi({\mathsf{R}}_\ell)}=\frac{\mu_\xi(D^{k-\ell}({\mathsf{R}}_\ell))}{\mu_\xi({\mathsf{R}}_\ell)}=e^{\xi(k-\ell)}.
$$

\smallskip
\noindent
(c)$\Rightarrow${(b)} By (c), $
\liminf\limits_{T\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^T 1_{\mathsf F_1}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}{\int_0^T 1_{\mathsf F_2}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}>0$ for any pair of finite unions of horizontal rectangles $\mathsf F_1, \mathsf F_2$. 
Therefore, by Theorem \ref{t.historical-crit}, all the limit points of $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$ are finite. 
Suppose $\eta$ is a finite limit point. By Proposition \ref{PrBulk}, $\mu_\eta$ is a historical measure of ${\widetilde{\omega}}$, and there exists some $T_n\to\infty$ so that $\lim\limits_{T\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_k}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_\ell}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}=e^{\eta(k-\ell)}$. Necessarily $\eta=\xi$. Thus all the limit points of $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$ equal $\xi$, a statement which is equivalent to (b).
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- lem-46: body_md -->
\label{Lemma-Solution}
For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $\delta>0$ such that if $|z_n/n|<\delta$, then for all $n$ large enough, there exists $\xi_n\in [-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]$ such that $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)=z_n$.
<!-- end lem-46 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{LmPressure} and Proposition \ref{Prop-Var-Growth} $\mathsf{P}_n(0)=0$, $\mathsf{P}_n'(0)=\mathbb E(S_n)=O(1)$, $V_n\asymp n$, and for some positive constant $c$, $\mathsf{P}_n''(\xi)\geq c n$ on $[-1,1]$ for all $n$ large enough. Therefore, for all $0<{\varepsilon}<1$,  
$$
\mathsf{P}_n'(\varepsilon)\geq \mathsf{P}_n'(0)+cn\varepsilon=cn\varepsilon+O(1)\textrm{ and }\mathsf{P}_n'(-1)\leq P_n'(0)-cn\varepsilon=-cn\varepsilon+O(1).
$$
Thus, if $|z_n/n|<\frac{1}{2}c\varepsilon$ and $n$ is large enough,  then 
$
\mathsf{P}_n'(-\varepsilon)<z_n<\mathsf{P}_n'(\varepsilon).
$

Since $\mathsf{P}_n$ is analytic and strictly convex, there exists a unique solution to the equation $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)=z_n$, and $|\xi_n|<\varepsilon$.
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- head-9: body_md -->
The theorem asserts the equivalence  of the  conditions
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is $\mu_0$-generic;
\item $z_n({\widetilde{\omega}})/n\to 0$;
\item $\displaystyle \forall k,\ell\in\mathbb Z,\ \lim_{T\to \infty} \frac{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_k} (\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}})) dt}
{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_\ell} (\phi^t ({\widetilde{\omega}})) dt}=1$.
\end{enumerate}
The equivalence (a)$\Leftrightarrow$(c) is a special case of Theorem \ref{t.Char-mu-xi-Gen}, and was proved above. It remains to prove (a)$\Leftrightarrow$(b).  Let $z_n:=z_n({\widetilde{\omega}}), \xi_n:=\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$. 

Suppose (b). 
By Lemma \ref{Lemma-Solution},  $\exists \eta_n\to 0$
such that $\mathsf{P}_{n}'(\eta_n)=z_n$. By Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}, $\xi_N({\widetilde{\omega}})\to 0$, and ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is $\mu_0$-generic by Theorem \ref{t.Char-mu-xi-Gen}. 

Suppose (a), then Theorem \ref{t.Char-mu-xi-Gen} and Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure} tell us that  $z_n=\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)$ where $\xi_n\to 0$. By \eqref{Pres1stDer} and 
Proposition~\ref{Prop-Var-Growth}, $\mathsf{P}_n'(0)=\mathbb E(S_n)=O(1)$,  and for all the $n$ such that $\xi_n=0$, $z_n/n=\mathbb E(S_n)/n=O(1/n)\to 0$. 
For the  $n$ such that $\xi_n\neq 0$, we have 
$$
\frac{z_n}{n}=\frac{\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)-\mathsf{P}_n'(0)}{n}+O(n^{-1})=\frac{1}{n}
\cdot\frac{\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)-\mathsf{P}_n'(0)}{\xi_n}\cdot\xi_n+O(n^{-1}).
$$ 
For all large $n$, $|\xi_n|\!\!<\!\!1$.
By the mean value theorem, $\displaystyle \frac{1}{n}\left|\frac{\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n)-\mathsf{P}_n'(0)}{\xi_n}\right|\leq \frac{1}{n}\sup_{[-1,1]}\mathsf{P}_n''$,  and this quantity is bounded above  
 (see \eqref{Pres2dDer} and recall that $V_n\asymp n$). Thus again $z_n/n=O(|\xi_n|+n^{-1})\to 0$.  It follows that $z_n/n\to 0$ for the full sequence of $n$. \hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-9 -->
<!-- head-10: body_md -->
Without loss of generality $\alpha\in [0,1)$, and   $\beta=2\alpha-1\in (-1,1)$. Expand $\beta$ into its even continued fraction expansion: $\beta=[0; 2m_1,\ldots]$. Theorem \ref{t.char-of-equidist-seq} states that $D_N(\alpha)$ is equidistributed in $\frac{1}{2}\mathbb Z$ iff $\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n [\operatorname{sgn}(m_{2j})-\operatorname{sgn}(m_{2j-1})]\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0$. 

Suppose $D_N(\alpha)$ is equidistributed in $\frac{1}{2}\mathbb Z$.  Then $D_N(\alpha)$ attains any value in $\frac{1}{2}\mathbb Z$  at least once, and therefore 
$$\limsup\limits_{N\to\infty}D_N(\alpha)=\infty\textrm{ and }
\liminf\limits_{N\to\infty}D_N(\alpha)=-\infty.
$$ Since $|D_N(\alpha)\!-\!D_{N+1}(\alpha)|\!\leq\! \frac{1}{2}$,  $D_N(\alpha)$ attains any value in $\frac{1}{2}\mathbb Z$ infinitely many times, and
\begin{equation}\notag
\forall k\in\mathbb Z,\ \#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha)=\frac{1}{2}k\}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\infty.
\end{equation}


Let ${\widetilde{\omega}}_0$ denote the midpoint of the top side of horizontal rectangle ${\mathsf{R}}_0$. By \eqref{e.Lin-Flow-1},
\begin{equation}\label{e.1.11}
\forall k\in\mathbb Z,\ \int_{-1}^{n-1} 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_{k}}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}_0))dt=\#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha)=\frac{1}{2}k\}.
\end{equation}
Necessarily, $\int_{-1}^{n-1} 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_{k}}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}_0))dt\to\infty$, and the equidistribution of $D_N(\alpha)$ translates to the statement that 
$\displaystyle \forall k,\ell\in\mathbb Z,\ \lim_{T\to \infty} \frac{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_k} (\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}})) dt}
{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_\ell} (\phi^t ({\widetilde{\omega}})) dt}=1$. 

By Theorem \ref{CrLebGen}, $\displaystyle\frac{z_n({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)}{n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0.$ 
Theorem \ref{ThDriftOfOrigin}, proved in Appendix \ref{Appendix-Twist}, says that 
$
\displaystyle z_n({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{nN_0}[\operatorname{sgn}(m_{2k})-\operatorname{sgn}(m_{2k-1})],$  with $N_0$ as in \eqref{e.mat-prod-form}. 
It follows that 
\begin{equation}\label{e.lari}
\displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^{n}[\operatorname{sgn}(m_{2k})-\operatorname{sgn}(m_{2k-1})]\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0.
\end{equation}

Conversely, \eqref{e.lari} implies that $z_n({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)/n\to 0$, whence by Theorem \ref{CrLebGen},   ${\widetilde{\omega}}_0$ is $\mu_0$-generic, and 
$\displaystyle \forall k,\ell\in\mathbb Z,\ \lim_{T\to \infty} \frac{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_k} (\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}})) dt}
{\int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_\ell} (\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}})) dt}=1.$
The numerator and denominator must tend to infinity, see the argument leading to \eqref{e.RET-conservative}. Therefore, by \eqref{e.1.11},
$$
\forall k,\ell\in\mathbb Z, \ \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha)=\frac{1}{2}k\}}
{\#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha)=\frac{1}{2}\ell\}}=1,
$$
and $D_N(\alpha)$ is equidistributed in $\frac{1}{2}\mathbb Z$.
\hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-10 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
The theorem states that if  $D_N(\alpha,x+I)$ is tilted, i.e. 
$$
\forall k,\ell\in\mathbb Z,\ \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha,x+I)=\frac{1}{2}k\}}{\#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha,x+I)=\frac{1}{2}\ell\}}=\rho(k/2,\ell/2)>0,
$$
then $D_N(\alpha,x+I)$ it is exponentially tilted, i.e.  $\rho(s,t)=\exp[\eta(s-t)]$ for some $\eta\in\mathbb R$.

Assume $D_N(\alpha,x\!+\!I)$ is tilted. One shows, as in the previous proof, that 
$
\forall k\in\mathbb Z
$, 
$
\ \#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha,x+I)=\frac{1}{2}k\}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\infty.
$

Let ${\widetilde{\omega}}={\widetilde{\omega}}_{-x}:=\omega(-x,0)\in{\mathsf{St}}$ be the initial condition of $\phi$,  corresponding to the initial condition $(-x,0)$ for the cylinder map, as in   Theorem \ref{t.HHW}. By \eqref{e.Lin-Flow-2}, 
\begin{align}
&\forall k,\ell\in\mathbb Z,\ \int_{-1}^{n-1} 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_{k}}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt=\#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha,x+I)=\frac{1}{2}k\}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\infty,\notag\\
&\underset{n\in\mathbb N}{\lim_{n\to\infty}}\frac{\int_{-1}^{n-1} 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_{k}}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}{\int_{-1}^{n-1} 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_{\ell}}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}
={\lim_{n\to\infty}}\frac{\#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha,x+I)=\frac{1}{2}k\}}{\#\{1\leq N\leq n: D_N(\alpha,x+I)=\frac{1}{2}\ell\}}=\rho(k/2,\ell/2)>0,\notag\\
&\hspace{-0.3cm}\textrm{ and therefore, }\underset{T\in\mathbb R}{\lim_{T\to\infty}}\frac{\int_{0}^{T} 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_{k}}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}{\int_{0}^{T} 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_{\ell}}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}=\rho(k/2,\ell/2)>0. \label{e.rho-limit}
\end{align}
In particular,   $\displaystyle {\liminf_{T\to\infty}}\frac{\int_{0}^{T} 1_{\mathsf F_1}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}{\int_{0}^{T} 1_{\mathsf F_2}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}>0$ whenever $\mathsf F_1,\mathsf F_2$ are finite unions of  horizontal rectangles.
By Theorem \ref{t.historical-crit}, all the limit points of $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$ must be finite. 

Let $\xi_1,\xi_2$ be two finite limits points of  $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$. By Proposition \ref{PrBulk}, there are 
{$T_n^j\to\infty$  such that 
$\displaystyle
\frac{\int_{0}^{T_n^j} 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_{k}}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}{\int_{0}^{T_n^j} 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_{\ell}}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt}\to 
e^{\xi_j(k-\ell)}.$}
                                                                                                                                                       
By \eqref{e.rho-limit}, $e^{\xi_1(k-\ell)}=\rho(k/2,\ell/2)=e^{\xi_2(k-\ell)}$, and $\xi_1=\xi_2$. Thus $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$ converges to a finite limit $\xi$.  By Theorem \ref{t.Char-mu-xi-Gen} and \eqref{e.rho-limit}, $\rho(k/2,\ell/2)=e^{\xi(k-\ell)}$ for all $k,\ell\in\mathbb Z$.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- head-11: body_md -->
The theorem states the existence of sequences $z_n^\xi\in\mathbb Z$ such that ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is $\mu_\xi$-generic iff $z_n({\widetilde{\omega}})=z_n^\xi+o(n)$. Equivalently, if $\widetilde{\omega}'$ is generic for $\mu_\xi$, then
\begin{equation}\label{LmGenPair}
\textrm{ $\forall{\widetilde{\omega}}'',\ \widetilde{\omega}''$ is generic for $\mu_\xi$ iff 
$\frac{z_N(\widetilde{\omega}'')-z_N(\widetilde{\omega}')}{N}\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}0$.}
\end{equation}
(Take $z_n^\xi:=z_n({\widetilde{\omega}}')$.)
 Let $z_n':=z_{nN_0}(\widetilde{\omega}')$ and $z_n'':=z_{nN_0}(\widetilde{\omega}'')$. Let $\xi_n',\xi_n''$ be the solutions to the equations $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n')=z_n'$,  
 $\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n'')=z_n''$.


\medskip
\noindent
{\bf $(\Rightarrow)$:} 
Suppose $\widetilde{\omega}''$ is generic for $\mu_\xi$. By Theorem \ref{t.Char-mu-xi-Gen} and Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}, $\xi_n', \xi_n''\to \xi$.  In particular, $\xi_n'$ and $\xi_n''$  both eventually lie in the interval $[\xi-1,\xi+1]$. By Lemma~\ref{LmPressure} and Proposition~\ref{Prop-Var-Growth}, there are positive constants $c_1,c_2$ such that for all $n$ large enough,  $c_1<\mathsf{P}_n''/n<c_2$ on $[\xi-1, \xi+1]$.  
By the mean value theorem,
$$ \frac{|z_n''-z_n'|}{n}                                                                                                 
\leq \biggl(\sup_{[\xi-1,\xi+1]}\frac{\mathsf{P}_n''}{n}\biggr)\cdot|\xi_n''-\xi_n'|\leq c_2|\xi_n''-\xi_n'|. 
$$
Since $\xi_n', \xi_n''\to \xi$, ${|z_n''-z_n'|}/{n}\to 0$. Since $z_N({\widetilde{\omega}}')=z_{\lfloor N/N_0\rfloor}'+O(1)$ and $z_N({\widetilde{\omega}}'')=z_{\lfloor N/N_0\rfloor}''+O(1)$, $|z_N({\widetilde{\omega}}')-z_N({\widetilde{\omega}}'')|/N\to 0$. 

\medskip
\noindent
$(\Leftarrow)$: Suppose $|z_N({\widetilde{\omega}}')-z_N({\widetilde{\omega}}'')|/N\to 0$, then 
 ${|z_n''-z_n'|}/{n}\to 0$. Fix $0<{\varepsilon}<1$. By Theorem \ref{t.Char-mu-xi-Gen}, Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}, and the  $\mu_\xi$-genericity of ${\widetilde{\omega}}'$, $\xi_n'\to\xi$. Therefore, for all $n$ large enough, $|\xi_n'-\xi|<\varepsilon$. By  assumption,  for all $n$ large enough, $|z_n''-z_n'|<c_1 n \varepsilon$. 
By the convexity of $\mathsf{P}_n$, for such $n$,  
$$
\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n'+\varepsilon)\geq \mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n')+c_1 n\varepsilon=z_n'+c_1 n \varepsilon>z_n''; 
$$
$$
\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n'-\varepsilon)\leq \mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n')-c_1 n\varepsilon=z_n'-c_1 n \varepsilon<z_n''. 
$$
So $z_n''\in [\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n'-\varepsilon),\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n'+\varepsilon)]$. Since $P_n$ is analytic and strictly convex on $[\xi-1,\xi+1]$, there is a unique finite solution $\xi_n''$ to the equation $z_n''=\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi_n'')$, and $|\xi_n''-\xi_n'|<\varepsilon$ for all $n$ sufficiently large. Since $\varepsilon$ was arbitrary and $\xi_n'\to\xi$, $\xi_n''\to\xi$. By Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}, $\xi_N({\widetilde{\omega}}'')\to\xi$, and by Theorem \ref{t.Char-mu-xi-Gen} $\widetilde{\omega}'$ is generic for $\mu_\xi$.
This concludes the proof of \eqref{LmGenPair}, and the proof of Theorem \ref{CrDriftSeq}.
\hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-11 -->
<!-- lem-47: body_md -->
\label{LmTurtle}\ 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item If $z_n:=z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})$, $\mathsf{P}_n'(\eta_n)=z_n$, and $\eta_n$ is bounded, then $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty} (\eta_{n+1}-\eta_n)=0.$ 
\item If  $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})$ are bounded, then
$\displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty} [\xi_{n+1}({\widetilde{\omega}})-\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})]=0.$ 
\end{enumerate}
