Let $\xi>0$. The theorem states that there are $a_T(\xi)\asymp \sqrt{\log T}$ 
and  $b_T$ satisfying
$(1-c)\log T\leq b_T(\xi)\leq \log T$ with $0<c<1$ as follows:
Suppose $h\in L^1(\mu_\xi)$ is non-negative and let $\varphi:{\mathsf{St}}\to\mathbb R$ be a  smooth,  compactly supported,  non-negative function such that  $\int\varphi d\mu_\xi=1$. If  ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ is sampled randomly from the probability measure $\varphi d\mu_\xi$,    then 
$$
\frac{\log \int_0^T h(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt-b_T(\xi)}{a_T(\xi)}\xrightarrow[T\to\infty]{\textrm{dist}}\mathcal N. 
$$
This includes  the case $h=1_{{\mathsf{St}}_{-}}$, because 
$\displaystyle
\|1_{{\mathsf{St}}_{-}}\|_{L^1(\mu_\xi)}
=\sum_{k=1}^\infty e^{-\xi k}<\infty
$
{ (recall that $\mu_\xi\circ D=e^{\xi}\mu_\xi$, and $\mu_\xi({\mathsf{R}}_0)=1$,
see Corollary \ref{c.HHW}). }


As in the proof of Theorem \ref{ThLT-ZD}, it is sufficient to consider $h=1_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}$ and $\varphi$ proportional to the indicator of a set of the form $D^j (\pi|_{\widetilde{F}_0})^{-1}\<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_n\>$. We consider the case $j=n=0$ and leave the (routine) modification needed in the general case to the reader.


{It is sufficient to consider ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ which are $\mu_\xi$-generic, because  $\mu_\xi$-a.e. ${\widetilde{\omega}}$ are like that. By Theorem \ref{t.Char-mu-xi-Gen}, $\xi_n({\widetilde{\omega}})\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\xi$ $\mu_\xi$-almost everywhere. 
By Proposition \ref{p.Bikhoff-Sums-Estimate}, there are  integers $n=n(T)\asymp \log T$ such that for $\mu_\xi$-a.e. ${\widetilde{\omega}}$,
\begin{equation}\label{e.pre-Taylor}
\frac{\log \int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt-\log T}{\sqrt{V_n}}=-\sqrt{V_n} \; 
\mathsf{H}_n\left(\frac{z_{nN_0} ({{\widetilde{\omega}}})}{V_n}\right)
+O\left(\frac{\log n}{\sqrt{n}}\right).
\end{equation}
The error estimate uses the bound $V_n\asymp n$ from Proposition \ref{Prop-Var-Growth}.

Let  $\displaystyle z_n^\xi:=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}(\widetilde{S}^\xi_n),$ the expectation of $S_n$ with respect to the change of measure ${\mathbb{P}}^{\xi}$. By \eqref{Pres1stDer}, $z_n^\xi=\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)+O(1)$, and by \eqref{Pres2dDer} and the estimate $V_n\asymp n$, there exists $R>0$ such that $\frac{z_n^\xi}{V_n}\asymp 1$, and that $\frac{z_n^\xi}{V_n}$ belong to the intervals $[\overline{a}^R_n,\overline{b}^R_n]$ from Lemma \ref{l.rate-function}. It follows that 
$\displaystyle
\sqrt{V_n}\mathsf{H}_n\left(\frac{z_n^\xi}{V_n}\right)\asymp\sqrt{V_n}\left(\frac{z_n^\xi-\mathbb E(S_n)}{{V_n}}\right)^2\asymp \sqrt{V_n}\asymp\sqrt{\log T}.
$

In addition, since  $z_n^\xi=\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)+O(1)$ and  $\mathsf{H}_n'$ is uniformly bounded on $[\overline{a}^R_n,\overline{b}^R_n]$, 
\begin{align*}
&\mathsf{H}_n'\left(\frac{z_n^\xi}{V_n}\right)=\mathsf{H}_n'\left(\frac{\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)}{V_n}+o(1)\right)=\mathsf{H}_n'\left(\frac{\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)}{V_n}\right)+o(1)=\xi+o(1), 
\end{align*}
where the last identity is because  $\mathsf{H}_n$ is the Legendre transform of $\mathsf{P}_n/V_n$.

Finally, by Lemma \ref{l.rate-function}, $\sup |\mathsf{H}_n''|=O(1)$ on $[\overline{a}^R_n,\overline{b}^R_n]$, and $\mathsf{H}_n$ is real-analytic on a neighborhood of $[\overline{a}^R_n,\overline{b}^R_n]$.
Expanding the right-hand-side of \eqref{e.pre-Taylor} into the Taylor expansion, and rearranging terms, we obtain 
\begin{align*}
&\frac{\log \int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt-\log T}{\sqrt{V_n}}+\sqrt{V_n}\mathsf{H}_n\left(\frac{z_n^\xi}{V_n}\right)=\\
&
=
-\mathsf{H}_n'\left(\frac{z_n^\xi}{V_n}\right)\frac{z_{nN_0}({ {\widetilde{\omega}}})-z_n^\xi}{\sqrt{V_n}}+
O\left(\frac{(z_n^\xi-z_{nN_0}({ {\widetilde{\omega}}}))^2}{\sqrt{V_n^3}} \right)+O\left(\frac{\log\log T}{\sqrt{\log T}}\right)\\
&=-(\xi+o(1))\sqrt{\frac{\widetilde{V}^\xi_n}{V_n}}\left[\frac{z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})-z_n^\xi}{\sqrt{\widetilde{V}^\xi_n}}+
O\left(\frac{\widetilde{V}^\xi_n}{V_n^{3/2}}\left(\frac{z_n^\xi-z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})}{
\sqrt{\widetilde{V}^\xi_n}} \right)^2\right)\right]+O\left(\frac{\log\log T}{\sqrt{\log T}}\right),
\end{align*}
where $\widetilde{V}^\xi_n:={\rm Var}(\widetilde{S}^\xi_n)$. 
By Lemma \ref{l.V-n-xi}, $\widetilde{V}^\xi_n\asymp V_n$, so $\widetilde{V}^\xi_n\asymp n\asymp\log T$

By Lemma \ref{l.uniform-Doeblin}, the Markov chain $\{\widetilde{X}_n^\xi\}$ is uniformly elliptic, and since $z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})=\widetilde{S}^\xi_n+O(1)$ in distribution (Lemma \ref{l.Phi-Decomp}), 
{ $\frac{z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})-z_n^\xi}{\sqrt{\widetilde{V}^\xi_n}}$ converges in distribution to $\mathcal N$.
Therefore 
$\frac{\widetilde{V}^\xi_n}{V_n^{3/2}}\left(\frac{z_n^\xi-z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})}{
\sqrt{\widetilde{V}^\xi_n}} \right)^2$ converges to $0$ in probability. Hence}
the term in the square brackets converges in distribution to $\mathcal N$. Letting 
\begin{align*}
& a_T(\xi):={\sqrt{V_n}/\xi}, \textrm{ and } 
b_T(\xi):=\log T-V_{n}\mathsf{H}_{n}\left(\frac{z_n^\xi}{V_n}\right)
\end{align*}
we obtain  $\displaystyle \frac{\log \int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt-b_T(\xi)}{a_T(\xi)}\xrightarrow[T\to\infty]{\textrm{dist}}\mathcal N$. 


The denominator satisfies the bounds 
$ a_T(\xi)=\sqrt{V_n}/\xi\asymp \sqrt{n}/\xi\asymp \sqrt{\log T}$. 
In particular, $\displaystyle \frac{\log \int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt-b_T(\xi)}{\log T}$ converges in probability to zero. 

Recall that  $\displaystyle \mu_\xi[{\mathfrak{z}}\leq 1]=\sum_{k\geq -1} e^{-k\xi}<\infty$, therefore $1_{[{\mathfrak{z}}\leq 1]}\in L^1(\mu_\xi)$, and by the   ratio ergodic theorem
$\displaystyle
\log \int_0^T 1_{{\mathsf{R}}_0}(\phi^t({\widetilde{\omega}}))dt=\mathbb{I}_T({\widetilde{\omega}})+\operatorname{const}+o(1)\ \ \textrm{$\mu_\xi$-a.e.}
$
with $\mathbb{I}_T({\widetilde{\omega}})$ as in Theorem \ref{CrLogOTDetXi}. It follows that 
$\displaystyle \frac{\mathbb{I}_T({\widetilde{\omega}})-b_T(\xi)}{\log T}$ converges in probability to zero. However, by Theorem \ref{CrLogOTDetXi}, $\displaystyle \frac{\mathbb{I}_T({\widetilde{\omega}})-\mathbb{I}_T^\xi}{\log T}$ converges in probability (indeed a.e.) to zero. Necessarily, $b_T(\xi)=\mathbb{I}_T^\xi+o(\log T)$. It now follows from Theorem \ref{CrLogOTDetXi} that for some $0<c(\xi)<1$, for all $T$ large enough, $(1-c(\xi))\log T\leq b_T(\xi)\leq \log T$. }

\label{LmBetaCont}
There exists constants $\mathsf{K}(R)>1$ such that 
if $\beta',\beta''\in\Lambda_6$ satisfy $m_i(\beta')=m_{i+i_0N_0}(\beta'')$ for all  
$2n_1 N_0\leq i \leq  2 n_2 N_0$,   then
$$
\left|\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi_{\beta'}\left(\sum_{n=n_1}^{n_2-1} f_{n,\beta'}(\widetilde{X}^\xi_{n,\beta'})\right)-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\xi_{\beta''}\left(\sum_{n=n_1+i_0}^{n_2+i_0-1} f_{n,\beta''}(\widetilde{X}^\xi_{n,\beta''})\right)\right|\leq \mathsf{K}\textrm{ for all }\xi\in [-R,R].
$$

<!-- proof-78: body_md -->
Let $m_i$ be the common value of $m_i(\beta')$ and $m_{i+i_0 N_0}(\beta'')$, for $2n_1 N_0\leq i\leq 2n_2 N_0$. 
By the proof of Proposition \ref{Prop-Contracting-Automorphisms}, for every $n_1\leq n\leq n_2-1$, 
$
\widetilde{\psi}_{n,\beta'}=\widetilde{\psi}_{n+i_0,\beta''}=
$ the unique homogeneous automorphism with zero drift and derivative 
\begin{align*}
&A_{N_0}([0;2m_{2nN_0+1}, 2m_{2nN_0+2},\ldots])
=\\
&\hspace{1cm}{\tiny{\left(
       \begin{array}{cc}
         1 & -2m_{2(n+1)N_0} \\
         0 & 1 \\
       \end{array}
     \right)
     \left(
       \begin{array}{cc}
         1 & 0 \\
         -2m_{2(n+1)N_0-1} & 1 \\
       \end{array}
     \right)
     \cdots
      \left(
       \begin{array}{cc}
         1 & -2m_{2nN_0+2} \\
         0 & 1 \\
       \end{array}
     \right)
     \left(
       \begin{array}{cc}
         1 & 0 \\
         -2m_{2nN_0+1} & 1 \\
       \end{array}
     \right)}}.
\end{align*}
Equations   \eqref{e.E-k} show that  the slopes of $E^t_{n,\beta'},E^u_{n+i_0,\beta''}$ $(t=u,s)$ are numbers whose even continued fraction expansion agrees on the first $2N_0 d(n)$ coordinates, where 
$$
 d(n):=
 \min(n-n_1, n_2-n).
$$
Since $\beta',\beta''\in\Lambda_6$, there is a global constant $\theta_1\in (0,1)$ such that 
$$
|\measuredangle(E^t_{n,\beta'},E^t_{n+i_0,\beta''})|\leq C\theta_1^{d(n)} \textrm{ for all $n_1\leq n\leq n_2$ and  
$t=u,s$}$$
(see Lemmas \ref{l.v-contracts} and \ref{l.limit-cfe-exists}). 

Let $\Pi_{n,\beta}:=\Pi(E^s_{n,\beta},E^u_{n,\beta})$ be the polygons from Figure  \ref{Figure-Pi(n)} on page \pageref{Figure-Pi(n)}. The angles and sides of    $\Pi_{n,\beta'}$ and $\Pi_{n+i_0,\beta''}$ are the same up to errors of size $O(\theta_1^{d(n)})$, $n_1\leq n\leq n_2$.  

Recall that  $\Pi_{n,\beta}$ is partitioned into two parallelograms $Q_{1,\beta}(n), Q_{2,\beta}(n)$ as Figure \ref{Figure-Pi(n)}. 
Since $\beta',\beta''\in\Lambda_6$, the lengths of the $u$-sides of $Q_{i,\beta}(n)$ are bounded below. Necessarily, for some global constant $\mathsf k\in\mathbb N$ and  for all $n_1+\mathsf k\leq n\leq n_2-\mathsf k$, $\widetilde{\psi}_{n,\beta'}(Q_{i,\beta'}(n))$ and $\widetilde{\psi}_{n+i_0,\beta''}(Q_{i,\beta''}(n+i_0))$ wrap around $Q_{j,\beta'}(n+1)$ and $Q_{j,\beta''}(n+i_0+1)$ the same number of times. Thus the Markov partitions $\mathfrak P_{n,\beta'}, \mathfrak P_{n+i_0,\beta''}$ can be enumerated by
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}\label{e.P-enumerate}
&Q_{\beta',1,1}^n, \ldots,Q_{\beta',1,N_{1}(n)}^n;
Q_{\beta',2,1}^n, \ldots,Q_{\beta',2,N_{2}(n)}^n \\
&Q_{\beta'',1,1}^{n+i_0}, \ldots,Q_{\beta'',1,N_{1}(n)}^{n+i_0};
Q_{\beta'',2,1}^{n+i_0}, \ldots,Q_{\beta'',2,N_{2}(n)}^{n+i_0} \ \ \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
with the same $N_i(n)$. 
Moreover, by making $\mathsf k$ sufficiently large we can  guarantee that the incidence matrices  $(t^{(n)}_{\beta',a,b}), (t^{(n+i_0)}_{\beta'',a,b})$ in \eqref{e.incidence-matrix} are the same, i.e.
$$
\psi_{n,\beta'}(\mathrm{int}(Q_{\beta',i,j}^n))\cap \mathrm{int}(Q_{\beta',k,\ell}^{n+1})\neq \varnothing\Leftrightarrow \psi_{n+i_0,\beta''}(\mathrm{int}(Q_{\beta'',i,j}^{n+i_0}))\cap \mathrm{int}(Q_{\beta'',k,\ell}^{n+i_0+1})\neq \varnothing.
$$
To see this recall that $\psi_{n,\beta'}=\psi_{n+i_0,\beta''}$. Next, note that the infimum of the stable widths of $\psi_n(\mathrm{int}(Q_{\beta,i,j}^n))$ over all $\beta\in\Lambda_6$, and $i,j,n$  is a positive number $\delta$ (bounded geometry). Therefore,  
if $\psi_n(\mathrm{int}(Q_{\beta,i,j}^n))\cap \mathrm{int}(Q_{\beta,k,\ell}^{n+1})\neq \varnothing$ then this intersection contains $u$-fibres within distance at least $\delta/2$ from the boundary of $Q_{\beta,k,\ell}^n$. By passing from $(n,\beta')$ to $(n+i_0,\beta'')$ we are perturbing $\psi_{n,\beta'}(\mathrm{int}(Q_{\beta,i,j}^n))$ and $\mathrm{int}(Q_{\beta',k,\ell}^{n+1})$ by a an amount uniformly bounded by $O(\theta_1^{d(n)})=O(\theta_1^{\mathsf k})$ so the non-emptiness of the intersection is preserved. 

For similar reasons, if $\mathsf k$ is sufficiently large and $n_1+\mathsf k\leq n\leq n_2-\mathsf k$, then 
$$
f_{n,\beta'}=f_{n+i_0,\beta''}.
$$

Finally, we claim that if $\mathsf k$ is sufficiently large and $n_1+\mathsf k\leq n\leq n_2-\mathsf k$, then the transition kernels from Proposition \ref{Prop-Markov-Kernel} satisfy
\begin{equation}
\label{TrPrClose}
\pi_{\beta',n,n+1}-\pi_{\beta'',n+i_0,n+i_0+1}=O\left(\theta_1^{d(n)}\right) \textrm{ for all }n_1+\mathsf k\leq n\leq n_2-\mathsf k.
\end{equation}
Indeed, $\displaystyle\pi_{\beta',n,n+1}(Q_{\beta',i,j}^n,Q_{\beta',k,\ell}^{n+1})=\frac{\mu_0[\psi_{n,\beta'}(Q_{\beta',i,j}^n)\cap Q_{\beta',k,\ell}^{n+1}]}{\mu_0[Q_{\beta',k,\ell}^{n+1}]}$,  and  $$\displaystyle\pi_{\beta'',n+i_0,n+i_0+1}(Q_{\beta'',i,j}^{n+i_0},Q_{\beta'',k,\ell}^{n+i_0+1})=\frac{\mu_0[\psi_{n,\beta''}(Q_{\beta'',i,j}^{n+i_0})\cap Q_{\beta'',k,\ell}^{n+i_0+1}]}{\mu_0[Q_{\beta'',k,\ell}^{n+i_0+1}]}.$$ By the previous discussion, the numerators and the denominators  are  equal  up to error $O(\theta_1^{d(n)})$, and by Lemma \ref{Lemma-Bounded-Geometry-Gamma(M)}, the denominator is bounded away from zero for $\beta\in\Lambda_6$.  

Now we consider the change of measure in \S \ref{ss.change-of-measure}, starting with the functions $h_{n,\beta}(\cdot,\xi)$ from Lemma \ref{LmAddPres}. These functions are constructed in the proof of Lemma~7.3 in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book}, as follows. Using the enumeration \eqref{e.P-enumerate}, we identify $\mathfrak P_{n,\beta}$ with a set $\mathfrak S_n$ independent of $\beta$, and $\pi_{\beta,n,n+1}$ with Markov kernels on $\mathfrak S_n\times\mathfrak S_{n+1}$. Let 
\begin{itemize}
\item $V_{n}:=\ell^\infty(\mathfrak S_n)$;
\item $\mathcal{C}_{n}:=\{h\in V_{n}: h\geq 0\}$;
\item $L_{n,\beta}^\xi:V_{n+1}\to V_{n}$, $(L_{n,\beta}^\xi h)(a)=\sum_{b\in\mathfrak S_{n+1}}e^{\xi f_{n+1}(b)}\pi_{\beta,n,n+1}(a,b)h(b)$. 
\end{itemize}
It is shown in the proof of Lemma~7.3 in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book} that the limits 
$\displaystyle \lim_{\ell\to\infty} L_{n+1,\beta}^\xi\cdots L_{n+\ell,\beta}^\xi 1$ exist, and that $h_n(\cdot,\xi)$ can be taken to be of the form $\displaystyle e^{c_n\xi}\times \lim_{\ell\to\infty} L_{n+1,\beta}^\xi\cdots L_{n+\ell,\beta}^\xi 1$ for suitable $c_n$. The choice of $c_n$ does not affect $\pi_{\beta,n,n+1}^\xi$.

The existence of the limit is proved in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book} by first showing that $L_{n,\beta}^\xi$ maps the closure of $\mathcal{C}_{n+1}$ into the interior of $\mathcal{C}_n$, and that $L_{n,
\beta}^\xi L_{n+1,\beta}^\xi: \mathcal{C}_{n+2}\to \mathcal{C}_n$ are uniform contractions in the Hilbert-Birkhoff metric. 
The contraction rate $\theta_2\in (0,1)$ is uniform in $\beta$ and $n$, provided  $\beta\in \Lambda_6$. Thus,
$$
h_{n,\beta}^\xi=C_n[(L_{n+2,\beta}^\xi \cdots L_{n_2-\mathsf k,\beta}^\xi 1+O(\theta_2^{d(n)})],
$$
where $C_n$ are positive proportionality constants. Comparing these expressions for $\beta=\beta',\beta''$ using \eqref{TrPrClose}, we conclude that for some global constants $\theta_3\in (0,1)$, $\mathsf{K}'(R)$,  for all $|\xi|\leq R$, for all $n_1+\mathsf k\leq n\leq n_2-\mathsf k$, 
$
\|h_{\beta',n}^\xi-h_{\beta'',n+i_0}^\xi\|_\infty=\mathsf{K}'(R)\theta_3^{d(n)}
$, 
and so
$ 
\|\pi_{\beta',n,n+1}^\xi-\pi_{\beta'',n+i_0,n+i_0+1}^\xi\|\leq O\left(\theta_3^{d(n)}\right) $
uniformly for $|\xi|\leq R.$ 

Using the identity  $f_{n,\beta'}=f_{n+i_0,\beta''}$, we see by direct calculations that for some constant $\mathsf{K}(R)$, if $|\xi|\leq R$, then (after identifying the state spaces $\mathfrak P_{n,\beta'}$ and $\mathfrak P_{n+i_0,\beta''}$ as in \eqref{e.P-enumerate})
$$
\left|
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta'}\left(\sum_{n=n_1+\mathsf k}^{n_2-\mathsf k}f_{n,\beta'}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{n,\beta'})\bigg| \widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{n_1+\mathsf k,\beta'}\right)-
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta''}\left(\sum_{n=n_1+i_0+\mathsf k}^{n_2+i_0-\mathsf k}f_{n,\beta''}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{n,\beta''})\bigg| \widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{n_1+i_0+\mathsf k,\beta''}\right)
\right|\leq \mathsf{K}(R).
$$
All Markov chains associated to $\beta',\beta''\in\Lambda_6$ are uniformly elliptic with the same ellipticity constant ${\varepsilon}_0$ (Proposition \ref{Prop-Doeblin}).  Therefore by Lemma \ref{l.uniform-Doeblin}, the Markov chains 
 $\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{n,\beta'}, \widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{n,\beta''}$ are uniformly elliptic with the same ellipticity constant ${\varepsilon}_0$ for all $\xi\in [-R,R]$ and $\beta',\beta''\in\Lambda_6$. It now follows from Corollary \ref{Cor-phi-mixing} that for some constant $\mathsf{K}'=\mathsf{K}'(R)$, for all $\beta',\beta''$ as above, 
$$
\left|
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta'}\left(\sum_{n=n_1+\mathsf k}^{n_2-\mathsf k}f_{n,\beta'}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{n,\beta'})\right)-
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta''}\left(\sum_{n=n_1+i_0+\mathsf k}^{n_2+i_0-\mathsf k}f_{n,\beta''}
(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{n,\beta''})\right)
\right|\leq \mathsf{K}(R).
$$
By Lemma \ref{Lemma-f(X)} there is a constant $\mathsf{K}''$ such that for all $\beta\in\Lambda_6$, $\sup_{i\geq 1}|f_{i,\beta}|\leq \mathsf{K}''$. So
$$
\left|
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta'}\left(\sum_{n=n_1}^{n_2}f_{n,\beta'}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{n,\beta'})\right)-
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta''}\left(\sum_{n=n_1+i_0}^{n_2+i_0}f_{n,\beta''}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{n,\beta''})\right)
\right|\leq \mathsf{K}(R)+4\mathsf{K}'',
$$
and the lemma follows.
<!-- end proof-78 -->

\label{LmPres23} \ 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item $\exists\eta_{n,\beta_3}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0$ such that 
$\mathsf{P}_{n,{\beta_3}}'(\eta_{n,{\beta_3}})=z_{n,\beta_3}$.
\item For every $\xi\in\mathbb R$, for all $n$ large enough, $\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta_2}'(\xi)<z_{n,\beta_2}$.

<!-- proof-79: body_md -->
Let  $\beta=\beta_3$. By Corollary \ref{CrOrigin},   ${\widetilde{\omega}}_0$ is $\mu_0$-generic. By Theorem \ref{t.Char-mu-xi-Gen}, $\xi_{n,\beta_3}({\widetilde{\omega}})\to 0$. 
By Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}, $\eta_{n,\beta_3}$ eventually exists, and  $\eta_{n,\beta_3}\to 0$.


Now consider   $\beta=\beta_2$.  By Theorem \ref{ThDriftOfOrigin}   
$
z_{n,\beta_2}=nN_0
$. Suppose first that for all $n$ large enough, there are no $\xi_n$ such that $\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta_2}'(\xi_n)\geq z_{n,\beta_2}$, then part (2) of the lemma holds automatically. Otherwise, there are $n_k\uparrow\infty$ and $\xi_{n_k}\in\mathbb R$ such that $\mathsf{P}_{n_k,\beta_2}'(\xi_{n_k})\geq z_{n_k,\beta_2}$.
 Since $\mathsf{P}_{n_k,\beta_2}'(0)=\mathbb E(S_{n,\beta_2})=O(1)$ and $\mathsf{P}_{n_k,\beta_2}'(\xi_{n_k})\geq z_{n_k,\beta_2}\to\infty$, there must exist $\eta_{n_k}\in\mathbb R$ such that $\mathsf{P}_{n_k,\beta_2}'(\eta_{n_k})=z_{n_k,\beta_2}$. We will show that $\eta_{n_k}\to\infty$, and deduce part~(2) from the strict convexity of  $\mathsf{P}_{n_k,\beta_2}$ for large $k$ (Lemma \ref{LmPressure}).
 
Write ${\beta_2}=2\alpha_2-1$, where 
$
\alpha_2:=\sqrt{2}-1$. Since $\alpha_2=\sqrt{2}\mbox{$\,\mathrm{mod}\,$} 1
$,   $D_n(\alpha_2)=D_n(\sqrt{2})$. It is shown in  \cite{Boshernitzan-Ralston} that $D_n(\sqrt{2})$ is uniformly bounded below. By \eqref{e.Lin-Flow-1}, ${\mathfrak{z}}[\phi_{\beta_2}^t({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)]$ is  bounded below, and  none of the $\mu_\xi$ can be  historical for ${\widetilde{\omega}}_0$. 
By Theorem \ref{CrHist} and  Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}, $\eta_{n_k}$ cannot have finite limit points. It follows that $|\eta_{n_k}|\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\infty.$
Since 
 $\mathsf{P}_{n_k,\beta_2}'(\eta_{n_k})=z_{n_k,\beta_2}\to+\infty$ and 
 $\mathsf{P}_{n_k,\beta_2}'(0)=O(1)$,  $\eta_{n_k}>0$, whence $\eta_{n_k}\to\infty.$
<!-- end proof-79 -->

\label{l.14.3} For all $\beta\in\Lambda_6$
there are  constants $c_\beta(R),\mathsf C_\beta(R)>0$ such that for all $\xi\in [-R,R]$, for all $L$ sufficiently large, for all $n$
$$
\left|\mathsf{P}_{L,\beta}'(\xi)-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{L}f_{k,\beta}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{k,\beta})\right)\right|\leq \mathsf C_\beta(R)\ \textrm{ and }\ \mathsf{P}_{L,\beta}''(\xi)\geq c_\beta(R)L.
$$

\label{l.Dima-Trick}
For every $C,r,R>0$,  for all  $L\in\mathbb N$ large enough and  $\beta\in \Lambda_6$, 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item  If $(2m_{2nN_0}(\beta),\ldots,2m_{2(n+L)N_0}(\beta))=(-6,6,\ldots,-6,6)$ and $\xi\leq R$, then 
\begin{equation}\label{e.Dima-Trick-1}
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta}\left(\sum_{k=n+1}^{n+L}f_{k,\beta}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{k,\beta})\right)< z_{n+L,\beta}-z_{n,\beta}-C.
\end{equation}
\item  If $(2m_{2nN_0}(\beta),\ldots,2m_{2(n+L)N_0}(\beta))=(2,6,\ldots,2,6)$ and $\xi>r$, then 
\begin{equation}\label{e.Dima-Trick-2}
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta}\left(\sum_{k=n+1}^{n+L}f_{k,\beta}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{k,\beta})\right)> z_{n+L,\beta}-z_{n,\beta}+C.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-52 -->
<!-- proof-80: body_md -->
Choose constants $\mathsf{K}:=\mathsf{K}(R+1)$, $c_{\beta}=c_{\beta}(R+1)$ and $\mathsf C_\beta(R+1)$ as in the previous lemmas. By Lemma \ref{LmPres23} there exists  $L_1$ so that if $\ell>L_1$, then 
$$\mathsf{P}_{\ell,\beta_2}'(R+1)<z_{\ell,\beta_2},\textrm{ and }\mathsf{P}_{\ell,\beta_3}'(\eta_{\ell,\beta_3})=0\textrm{ for some }\eta_{\ell,\beta_3}\in (-r/2,r/2).$$ 
If $(2m_{2nN_0}(\beta),\ldots,2m_{2(n+L)N_0}(\beta))=(-6,6,\ldots,-6,6)$ and $\xi\leq R$, then for all $L$
\begin{align*}
&\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta}\left(\sum_{k=n+1}^{n+L}f_{k,\beta}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{k,\beta})\right)\leq \mathsf{K}+
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta_2}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{L}f_{k,\beta_2}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{k,\beta_2})\right),\textrm{ by Lemma \ref{LmBetaCont}}\\
&\leq \mathsf{K}+2\mathsf C_{\beta_2}(R)+
\mathsf{P}_{L,\beta_2}'(\xi),\textrm{ by Lemma \ref{l.14.3}}\\
&\leq \mathsf{K}+2\mathsf C_{\beta_2}(R)+\mathsf{P}_{L,\beta_2}'(R)
\leq \mathsf{K}+2\mathsf C_{\beta_2}(R)+\mathsf{P}_{L,\beta_2}'(R+1)-c_{\beta_2}(R+1)L\\
&< \mathsf{P}_{L,\beta_2}'(R+1)-C, \textrm{ provided }L>(C+\mathsf{K}+2\mathsf C_{\beta_2}(R))/c_{\beta_2}(R+1)\\
&\leq z_{L,\beta_2}-C,\textrm{ provided $L>L_1$} \\
&=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^{LN_0}[\operatorname{sgn} m_{2j}(\beta_2)-\operatorname{sgn} m_{2j-1}(\beta_2)]-C \textrm{ by Theorem \ref{ThDriftOfOrigin}}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=nN_0}^{(n+L)N_0}[\operatorname{sgn} m_{2j}(\beta)-\operatorname{sgn} m_{2j-1}(\beta)]-C=z_{n+L,\beta}-z_{n,\beta}-C. 
\end{align*}
Thus, part (1) holds whenever  $L>\max\{L_1, (\mathsf{K}+2\mathsf C_{\beta_2}(R))/c_{\beta_2}(R)\}$. 

 If $(2m_{2nN_0}(\beta),\ldots,2m_{2(n+L)N_0}(\beta))=(2,6,\ldots,2,6)$ and $\xi>r$,   then 
\begin{align*}
&\hskip-25mm
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta}\left(\sum_{k=n+1}^{n+L}f_{k,\beta}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{k,\beta})\right)\geq -\mathsf{K}+
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta_3}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{L}f_{k,\beta_3}(\widetilde{X}^{\xi}_{k,\beta_3})\right)\\
&\hskip-25mm
\geq -\mathsf{K}-2\mathsf C_{\beta_3}(R)+\mathsf{P}_{L,\beta_3}'(\xi)
\geq -\mathsf{K}-2\mathsf C_{\beta_3}(R)+\mathsf{P}_{L,\beta_3}'(r)\\
&\hskip-25mm
\geq -\mathsf{K}-2\mathsf C_{\beta_3}(R)+\mathsf{P}_{L,\beta_3}'(r/2)+c_{\beta_3}(R)L(r/2)\\
&\hskip-25mm
\geq \mathsf{P}_{L,\beta_3}'(r/2)+C,\textrm{ provided $L>(2/r)(C+\mathsf{K}+2\mathsf C_{\beta_3}(R))/c_{\beta_3}(R)$}\\
&\hskip-25mm
\geq z_{L,\beta_3}+C,\textrm{ provided $L>L_1$}
\end{align*}
\hskip7mm$=z_{n+L,\beta}-z_{n,\beta}+C$ by the assumption on the even CFE of $\beta$ and Theorem \ref{ThDriftOfOrigin}.
<!-- end proof-80 -->
<!-- lem-53: body_md -->
\label{l.V-beta-xi-growth}
For every $R>0$ there exist $C_1,C_2>1$ such that for all $\beta\in\Lambda_6$, $|\xi|\leq R$, and  $n$, $C_1^{-1} n-C_2\leq \widetilde{V}_{n,\beta}^\xi\leq C_1 n +C_2.$
<!-- end lem-53 -->
<!-- proof-81: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{Lemma-f(X)},  $\displaystyle K:=\sup_{\beta\in\Lambda_6}\sup_n \|f_{n,\beta}\|<\infty$. 

By Proposition \ref{Prop-Doeblin}, there exists ${\varepsilon}_0'>0$ independent of $\beta$ such that  $\{X_{n,\beta}\}$ are uniformly elliptic with the same ellipticity constant ${\varepsilon}_0'$ for every $\beta\in\Lambda_6$. 
By  Lemma \ref{LmAddPres},\index{Change of measure!density estimates} there are constants $C(R)$ so that for all $\beta\in\Lambda_6$, $|\xi|\leq R$, and $n\in\mathbb N$,  
\begin{equation}\label{e.RN-est}
C_1(R)^{-1}\leq \frac{d\pi^\xi_{\beta,n,n+1}}{d\pi_{\beta,n,n+1}}\leq C_1(R). 
\end{equation}
It follows that for some constant ${\varepsilon}_0>0$, for all $\beta\in\Lambda_6$ and $|\xi|\leq R$, $\{\widetilde{X}_{n,\beta}\}$ are uniformly elliptic with the same ellipticity constant ${\varepsilon}_0$. 

Let  $u_{n,\beta}(\xi)$ denote the structure constants  associated to $\{\widetilde{X}_{n,\beta}^\xi\}$  in  \eqref{e.u}. By Theorem~\ref{LmVarCycles}, there are $C_2,C_3$ depending only on ${\varepsilon}_0$ and $K$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{e.v-beta-n-xi-ineq}
C_2^{-1}\sum_{k=3}^n u_{k,\beta}^2(\xi)-C_3\leq \widetilde{V}_{n,\beta}^\xi\leq C_2 \sum_{k=3}^n u_{k,\beta}^2(\xi)+C_3. 
\end{equation}



The same argument leading to the  equation array \eqref{e.state-lower-bound-xi} gives a constant ${\varepsilon}_1>0$ such that ${\mathbb{P}}[\widetilde{X}^\xi_{n,\beta}=a]$ is either zero or bigger than ${\varepsilon}_1$,  for all $\beta\in\Lambda_6$, $|\xi|\leq R$, and $n\in\mathbb N$. This and  \eqref{e.RN-est} imply that the hexagon measures of $\{\widetilde{X}_{n,\beta}^\xi\}$ and $\{{X}_{n,\beta}\}$ are equal up to a density which is uniformly bounded away from zero and infinity by constants independent of $\beta$ and $\xi$. It follows that there is a positive constant $C_4$ such that 
$$
C_4^{-1}\leq u_{k,\beta}(\xi)/u_{k,\beta}(0)\leq C_4\textrm{ for all $\beta\in\Lambda_6$, $|\xi|\leq R$, and $n\in\mathbb N$.}
$$

Looking at \eqref{e.v-beta-n-xi-ineq}, we see that for some $C_5,C_6$, for all $\beta\in\Lambda_6$, $|\xi|\leq R$, and $n\in\mathbb N$, 
$$
C_5^{-1}\sum_{k=3}^n u_{k,\beta}^2-C_6\leq \widetilde{V}_{n,\beta}^\xi\leq C_5 \sum_{k=3}^n u_{k,\beta}^2+C_6.
$$
Here $u_{k,\beta}:=u_{k,\beta}(0)$, the structure constants of $\{X_{n,\beta}\}$. 
By Theorem \ref{Theorem-D_N-Growth}, there are constants $C_7,C_8$ such that for all $\beta\in\Lambda_6$, 
$\displaystyle C_7^{-1}n-C_8\leq \sum_{k=3}^n u_{n,\beta}^2\leq C_7 n+C_8$, and the lemma follows.
<!-- end proof-81 -->
<!-- lem-54: body_md -->
\label{l.nu(R)}
For every $R>0$, there exist constants $\nu_1(R)$ and $v(R)>0$  such that for all $n>\nu_1(R)$, $\beta\in\Lambda_6$, and $0\!<\!\xi_1\!<\!\xi_2\!<\!R$,\;\;
               
$\displaystyle 
                        
                                                                                                                   
                           
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_2}_{\beta}(\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_2})-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_1}_{\beta}(\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1})\geq v(R)(\xi_2-\xi_1)n.
$
<!-- end lem-54 -->
<!-- proof-82: body_md -->
Fix $R>0$. 
By Lemma \ref{LmAddPres}, there is constant $\mathsf C$ such that  for every $\beta\in\Lambda_6$, $|\xi|\leq R$, and $n\in\mathbb N$,   
$\mathsf C(R)^{-1}\leq h_{n,\beta}(\cdot,\xi)\leq \mathsf C(R)$. If  $|\xi_1|,|\xi_2|\leq R$, then 
\begin{align*}
1&=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_2}_\beta(1)=\mathbb E_\beta\left(\frac{e^{\xi_2 S_{n,\beta}} h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_2)}{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_2)}h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_2)}\right)\\
&=\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta\left(\frac{e^{\xi_1 S_{n,\beta}}h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_1)}{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_1)}h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_1)}\cdot \frac{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_1)}h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_1)}{h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_1)}\frac{h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_2)}{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_2)}h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_2)}\cdot  e^{(\xi_2-\xi_1)S_{n,\beta}}\right)\\
&= \mathsf C(R)^{\pm 4} e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_1)-\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_2)}\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_1}_\beta(e^{(\xi_2-\xi_1)S_{n,\beta}}), \textrm{ whence}
\end{align*}
\begin{equation}\label{e.delta-P-id}
e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_2)-\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_1)}=\mathsf C(R)^{\pm 4} \widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_1}_\beta(e^{(\xi_2-\xi_1)S_{n,\beta}}).
\end{equation}

Similarly, writing $\eta:=\xi_2-\xi_1$ and $\widehat{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1}:={S}_{n,\beta}-\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1}(\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1})$ we have 
\begin{align}
&\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_2}_\beta (\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_2})-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_1}_\beta (\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1})=
\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_2} \left(\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_2}-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_1}_\beta (\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1})\right)
={\mathbb E}_\beta \left(\widehat{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1}\cdot \frac{e^{\xi_2 S_{n,\beta}} h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_2)}{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_2)}h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_2)}\right)\notag\\
&={\mathbb E}_\beta \left(\widehat{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1} e^{\eta S_{n,\beta}}e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_1)-\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_2)}\cdot \frac{e^{\xi_1 S_{n,\beta}} h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_1)}{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_1)}h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_1)}\cdot \frac{h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_2)h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_1)}{h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_1)h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_2)}\right) \notag\\
&=\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left(\widehat{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1} e^{\eta S_{n,\beta}}\cdot\frac{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_1)}}{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_2)}}\cdot \frac{h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_2)h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_1)}{h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_1)h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_2)}\right)
\geq \frac{\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left(\widehat{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1} e^{\eta S_{n,\beta}}\right)}{\mathsf C(R)^{8} \widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left(e^{\eta S_{n,\beta}}\right)},\textrm{ by \eqref{e.delta-P-id}} \notag
\end{align}
\begin{align}
&=\mathsf C(R)^{-8} \frac{\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left(\widehat{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1} e^{\eta \widehat{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1}}\right)}{ \widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left(e^{\eta \widehat{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1}}\right)}=\mathsf C(R)^{-8}\int_0^\eta \frac{d}{d\theta}\left[\frac{\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left(\widehat{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1} e^{\theta \widehat{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1}}\right)}{ \widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left(e^{\theta \widehat{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1}}\right)}\right]d\theta \notag\\
&=\mathsf C(R)^{-8}\int_0^\eta \frac{d}{d\theta}\left[\frac{\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left({S}_{n,\beta} e^{\theta {S}_{n,\beta}}\right)}{ \widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left(e^{\theta {S}_{n,\beta}}\right)}\right]d\theta.\label{e.Newton-Leibnitz-Trick}
\end{align}

To  calculate the integrand, it is convenient to use the following elementary fact: 
\begin{sublem*}
(\cite[Lemma 7.22]{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book}).
Let $X,Y$ be bounded random variables on the same probability space $\Omega$,  such that $\mathrm{Var}(X)<\infty$ and $C^{-1}y\leq Y\leq Cy$ for some constants $C>1$, $y>0$. Then the variance of $X$ with respect to the measure $\frac{Yd{\mathbb{P}}}{\mathbb E(Y)}$, given by \index{Change of measure!variance estimates}
$$
{\rm Var}^Y(X):=\frac{\mathbb E(X^2 Y)}{\mathbb E(Y)}-\left(\frac{\mathbb E(XY)}{\mathbb E(Y)}\right)^2, 
$$ 
satisfies the bounds $C^{-4}{\rm Var}(X)\leq {\rm Var}^Y(X)\leq C^{4}{\rm Var}(X)$. 
\end{sublem*}
\noindent
{\em Proof }
Let $(X_1,Y_1)$, $(X_2,Y_2)$ be two independent copies of $(X,Y)$, then \\
${\rm Var}^Y(X)=\frac{1}{2}\frac{\mathbb E[(X_1-X_2)^2 Y_1 Y_2]}{\mathbb E(Y_1 Y_2)}=C^{\pm 4} \frac{1}{2}\mathbb E[(X_1-X_2)^2]=C^{\pm 4}{\rm Var}(X)$.
\hfill$\square$

\smallskip 
Let $Y_\theta\!\! :=\!\!\frac{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_1)}}{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_1+\theta)}}\cdot \frac{h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_1)h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_1+\theta)}{h_{n,\beta}(X_{n,\beta},\xi_1+\theta)h_{1,\beta}(X_{1,\beta},\xi_1)}
\!\!=\!\!\mathsf C(R)^{\pm 4}\frac{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_1)}}{e^{\mathsf{P}_{n,\beta}(\xi_1+\theta)}}$.
By direct differentiation
\begin{align*}
&\frac{d}{d\theta}\left[\frac{\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left({S}_{n,\beta} e^{\theta {S}_{n,\beta}}\right)}{ \widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta \left(e^{\theta {S}_{n,\beta}}\right)}\right]=
\frac{\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta \left(({S}_{n,\beta})^2 e^{\theta {S}_{n,\beta}}\right)}{ \widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left(e^{\theta {S}_{n,\beta}}\right)}
-\left[\frac{\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left({S}_{n,\beta} e^{\theta {S}_{n,\beta}}\right)}{ \widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1} \left(e^{\theta {S}_{n,\beta}}\right)}\right]^2\\
&\!\!=\!\!\frac{\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1+\theta} \left(({S}_{n,\beta})^2 Y_\theta\right)}{ \widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1+\theta} \left(Y_\theta\right)}
\!-\!\left[\frac{\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1+\theta} \left({S}_{n,\beta}Y_\theta\right)}{ \widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1+\theta} \left(Y_\theta\right)}\right]^2
   
\!\!\!\!=\!\!{\rm Var}^{Y_\theta}(\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1+\theta})\geq 
\frac{{\rm Var}(\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1+\theta})}{\mathsf C(R)^4}
\!\!=\!\!\frac{\widetilde{V}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1+\theta}} {\mathsf C(R)^4}
.
\end{align*}
If $0\leq \theta\leq \eta$, then $\xi_1+\theta\in [\xi_1,\xi_2]\subset [0,R]$, and by Lemma \ref{l.V-beta-xi-growth}, there are constants $C_1(R), C_2(R)>0$  such that for all $\beta\in\Lambda_6$ and $0\leq \theta\leq \eta$, 
$
\widetilde{V}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1+\theta}\geq C_1(R)^{-1}n-C_2(R).
$
Looking at \eqref{e.Newton-Leibnitz-Trick}, we deduce that if $\eta:=\xi_2-\xi_1>0$, and $n>2C_1(R)C_2(R)$,  then
$\displaystyle
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_2}_\beta (\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_2})-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_1}_\beta (\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1})\geq 
\mathsf C(R)^{-12}\int_0^\eta \widetilde{V}_{n,\beta}^{\xi_1+\theta}d\theta
\geq 
                                            
\frac{n(\xi_2-\xi_1)}{2\mathsf C(R)^{12}C_1(R)}>0. 
$.
<!-- end proof-82 -->
<!-- sublem--1: body_md -->
(\cite[Lemma 7.22]{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book}).
Let $X,Y$ be bounded random variables on the same probability space $\Omega$,  such that $\mathrm{Var}(X)<\infty$ and $C^{-1}y\leq Y\leq Cy$ for some constants $C>1$, $y>0$. Then the variance of $X$ with respect to the measure $\frac{Yd{\mathbb{P}}}{\mathbb E(Y)}$, given by \index{Change of measure!variance estimates}
$$
{\rm Var}^Y(X):=\frac{\mathbb E(X^2 Y)}{\mathbb E(Y)}-\left(\frac{\mathbb E(XY)}{\mathbb E(Y)}\right)^2, 
$$ 
satisfies the bounds $C^{-4}{\rm Var}(X)\leq {\rm Var}^Y(X)\leq C^{4}{\rm Var}(X)$.
<!-- end sublem--1 -->
<!-- lem-55: body_md -->
\label{l.P1-P3}
Suppose $0<\xi<\xi+1<R$. 
 There exist positive integers $n_0, N_0, L,c_0$ and  even integers $b_1,b_2,\ldots\in \{2,6,-6\}$ such that for every $n> n_0$ and $\beta\in [0;b_1,\ldots,b_{nLN_0}]$, the following  holds:
\begin{enumerate}[(P1)]
\item $\exists!\xi_{nL,\beta}\in [0,R]$ such that  $\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}_{nL,\beta}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}})=z_{nL,\beta}$;
\item Suppose $n> n_0+1$, then 
\begin{enumerate}[--]
\item If $\xi_{(n-1)L,\beta}\leq \xi$, then $\xi_{nL,\beta}>\xi_{(n-1)L,\beta}$
\item If $\xi_{(n-1)L,\beta}\geq  \xi+\frac{c_0}{n-1}$, then $\xi_{nL,\beta}<\xi_{(n-1)L,\beta}$
\item If $\xi_{(n-1)L,\beta}\in (\xi, \xi+\frac{c_0}{n-1})$, then $|\xi_{nL,\beta}-\xi|\leq \frac{c_0}{n-1}$.
\end{enumerate}
\item  Suppose $n> n_0+1$, then $|\xi_{nL,\beta}-\xi_{(n-1)L,\beta}|<c_0/(n-1)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-55 -->
<!-- lem-56: body_md -->
\label{l.beta-is-nice}
Let $b_i$ be as in the previous lemma, and set $\beta=[0;b_1,b_2,b_3,\ldots]$. Then $\xi_{nL,\beta}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\xi$.
<!-- end lem-56 -->
<!-- proof-83: body_md -->
We fix once and for all the following constants:
\begin{itemize}
\item $N_0$, a positive  even integer independent of $\beta\in\Lambda_6$ as in \eqref{e.mat-prod-form}. 
\item $K$, a constant such that $|f_{n,\beta}|\leq K$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$ and $\beta\in\Lambda_6$ (Lemma \ref{Lemma-f(X)}).
\item $\mathsf K$, the constant $\mathsf K(R)$ from Lemma \ref{LmBetaCont}.
\item $E$, a positive integer such that $|\mathbb E_\beta(S_{n,\beta})|\leq E$ for all $n\geq 1$ and $\beta\in\Lambda_6$. Such a constant exists because of Proposition \ref{Prop-Drift}. 
\item $\nu(R)\in\mathbb N$ and $v(R)>0$ such that for all $n\geq \nu(R)$ and $\beta\in\Lambda_6$, 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\forall 0<\xi_1<\xi_2<R+1$, $\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_2}(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_2}_{n,\beta})>\widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^{\xi_1}(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_1}_{n,\beta})+v(R)(\xi_2-\xi_1)n$ (Lemma \ref{l.nu(R)});
\item Thus, $\eta\mapsto \widetilde{\mathbb E}_\beta^\eta(\widetilde{S}^\eta_{n,\beta})$ is increasing on $[0,R]$, and 
\item  $\forall \eta\in [\xi,R]$,  $\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\eta_\beta(\widetilde{S}^\eta_{n,\beta})>v(R)\xi n-E$. 
\end{enumerate}
\item $L$, a positive  integer such that \eqref{e.Dima-Trick-1} and \eqref{e.Dima-Trick-2} hold with $C:=\max\{E,2\mathsf K\}$, and so that $L>\max\{1,\nu(R),E/N_0,1/v(R)\}$.
\item $M:=4(N_0+K+\mathsf K)$.
\item  $c_0:=M/v(R)$.
\item $n_0$, a positive integer such that 
$\displaystyle n_0>\max\left\{\frac{2E+LN_0}{v(R)\xi}, \frac{M}{v(R)}\right\}$.
\end{itemize}

Define the strings
$\displaystyle
\underline{B}_{\sqrt{2}}=(\,\underset{2LN_0}{\underbrace{-6,6,\ldots,-6,6}}\,)\ ,\ \underline{B}_{\sqrt{3}}=(\,\underset{2LN_0}{\underbrace{2,6,\ldots,2,6}}\,).
$ 
The sequence $(b_1,b_2,b_3,\ldots)$ will be a concatenation $(\underline{B}_1,\underline{B}_2,\ldots)$ where $\underline{B}_i=\underline{B}_{\sqrt{2}}$ or $\underline{B}_{\sqrt{3}}$. 

First we declare that $\underline{B}_1,\cdots,\underline{B}_{n_0}:=\underline{B}_{\sqrt{3}}$, and $\underline{B}_{n_0+1}:=\underline{B}_{\sqrt{2}}$. 
Let us see  (P1). Suppose $\beta\in [0;\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_{n_0+1}]$, then 
\begin{align*}
z_{(n_0+1) L,\beta}&=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{(n_0+1) LN_0} [\operatorname{sgn}(b_{2k}(\beta))-\operatorname{sgn}(b_{2k-1}(\beta))]\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{n_0 LN_0} [\operatorname{sgn}(6)-\operatorname{sgn}(2)]+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{LN_0} [\operatorname{sgn}(6)-\operatorname{sgn}(-6)]=LN_0;\\
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^0_{\beta}(\widetilde{S}^0_{(n_0+1) L})&<z_{(n_0+1)L,\beta},\textrm{ because }\widetilde{\mathbb E}^0_{\beta}(\widetilde{S}^0_{(n_0+1) L,\beta})\leq E<LN_0;\\
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta}(\widetilde{S}^\xi_{(n_0+1) L,\beta})&>z_{(n_0+1)L,\beta},\textrm{ because  } \widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}_{\beta}(\widetilde{S}^\xi_{(n_0+1) L,\beta})>v(R)\xi n_0-E>LN_0.
\end{align*}
The function $\eta\mapsto \widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\eta}_{\beta}(\widetilde{S}^\eta_{(n_0+1) L,\beta})$ is continuous (Lemma \ref{LmAddPres}), and strictly increasing on $[0,R]$ (since $(n_0+1)L>\nu(R)$). Therefore there exists a unique $\xi_{(n_0+1)L,\beta}\in [0,R]$ such that $\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{(n_0+1)L,\beta}}_{\beta}(\widetilde{S}^\xi_{(n_0+1) L,\beta})=z_{(n_0+1)L,\beta}$. This shows (P1) for $n=n_0+1$. (P2) and (P3) hold vacuously for $n=n_0+1$. 

\medskip
Assume by induction that we have already constructed  $\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_n\in \{\underline{B}_{\sqrt{2}},\underline{B}_{\sqrt{3}}\}$ with $n\geq n_0$, so that   properties (P1)--(P3) hold. We define 
$$
\underline{B}_{n+1}:=
\begin{cases}
\underline{B}_{\sqrt{2}} & \exists\gamma\in [0;\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_n]\cap \Lambda_6$ s.t.  $\xi_{nL,\gamma}\leq \xi;\\
\underline{B}_{\sqrt{3}} & \forall\gamma\in [0;\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_n]\cap \Lambda_6$,   $\xi_{nL,\gamma}>\xi.
\end{cases}
$$
We claim that (P1)--(P3) hold for $n+1$. 


\medskip
\noindent
{\bf Case 1.\/} Suppose  $\exists\gamma\in [0;\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_n]\cap \Lambda_6$ s.t.  $\xi_{nL,\gamma}\leq \xi$. 
Then  $\underline{B}_{n+1}=\underline{B}_{\sqrt{2}}$. 

 Fix $\beta\in [0;\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_{n+1}]\cap \Lambda_6$. By Theorem \ref{ThDriftOfOrigin}, $z_{nL,\beta}=z_{nL,\gamma}$, and
 \[z_{(n+1)L,\beta}=z_{nL,\beta}+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{LN_0} [\operatorname{sgn}(6)-\operatorname{sgn}(-6)]=z_{nL,\beta}+LN_0=z_{nL,\gamma}+LN_0.
\]
By Lemma \ref{LmBetaCont}, $\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{nL,\beta})=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{\gamma}(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{nL,\gamma})\pm \mathsf K=z_{nL,\gamma}\pm\mathsf K=z_{nL,\beta}\pm\mathsf K$.\\
By Lemma \ref{l.Dima-Trick}(1), 
$\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{(n+1)L,\beta}-\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{nL,\beta})
\!\!<\!\! z_{(n+1)L,\beta}-z_{ nL,\beta}-C\leq z_{(n+1)L,\beta}-z_{ nL,\beta}
-2\mathsf K.$\\
Adding the two inequalities, we obtain  
$$\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{(n+1)L,\beta})<z_{(n+1)L,\beta}.$$


Let $M:=4(N_0+K+\mathsf K)$ and  $\eta:=\xi_{nL,\gamma}+\frac{M}{2v(R) n}$. Note that $\eta\leq \xi+{\frac{1}{2}}<R$. Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\eta}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\eta}_{(n+1)L,\beta})&\geq \widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\eta}_\beta(\widetilde{S}_{nL,\beta}^\eta)-KL
\geq \widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}_{nL,\beta}^\eta)+{v(R)(\eta-\xi_{nL,\gamma})nL}-KL\\
&=z_{nL,\beta}\pm\mathsf K+ML-KL=(z_{(n+1)L,\beta}-LN_0)\pm\mathsf K+ML-KL\\
&>z_{(n+1)L,\beta}+L(M-N_0-K-\mathsf K)>z_{(n+1)L,\beta}.
\end{align*}
By the intermediate value theorem, 
\begin{equation}\label{e.sol-interval}
\exists!\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}\in \left(\xi_{nL,\gamma}\ ,\ \xi_{nL,\gamma}+\frac{M}{2v(R) n}\right)\;\; \textrm{ s.t. }
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{(n+1)L,\beta})=z_{(n+1)L,\beta}.
\end{equation}
Note that $0<\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}<\xi+\frac{M}{v(R)n_0}\leq\xi+1$, therefore $\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}\in [0,R]$. 

If 
$\xi_{nL,\beta}\leq \xi$, then we can repeat the previous argument with $\gamma:=\beta$,  and obtain 
$$
\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}>\xi_{nL,\beta}
\ , \  |\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}-\xi_{nL,\beta}|\leq \frac{M}{v(R) n}.
$$



If $\xi_{nL,\beta}\geq \xi+\frac{M}{v(R)n}$, then $\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}<\xi_{nL,\gamma}+\frac{M}{v(R)n}<\xi+\frac{M}{v(R)n}\leq \xi_{nL,\beta}$, and 
$$
\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}<\xi_{nL,\beta}.
$$

If $\xi_{nL,\beta}\in(\xi,\xi+\frac{M}{v(R)n})$, then  we cannot determine whether $\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}<\xi_{nL,\beta}$. But we can estimate 
$|\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}-\xi|$, as follows. We saw above that 
$$
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{nL,\beta})=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{\gamma}(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{nL,\gamma})\pm \mathsf K=z_{nL,\gamma}\pm\mathsf K=z_{nL,\beta}\pm\mathsf K.
$$
Since  $z_{nL,\beta}=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_{nL,\beta})$,  this leads to 
 $
 |\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{nL,\beta})-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_{nL,\beta})|\leq \mathsf K.
 $
However   $ |\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\gamma}}_{nL,\beta})-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_{nL,\beta})|\geq v(R)|\xi_{nL,\gamma}-\xi_{nL,\beta}|nL$. By our assumptions,  $\xi_{nL,\gamma}$ and $\xi_{nL,\beta}$ are on opposite sides of $\xi$, so  
$
|\xi_{nL,\gamma}-\xi|<\frac{\mathsf K}{v(R)nL}<\frac{M}{4v(R)nL}.  
$ By  \eqref{e.sol-interval},
\[
|\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}-\xi|<|\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}-\xi_{nL,\gamma}|+|\xi_{nL,\gamma}-\xi|<\frac{3M}{4v(R) n}<\frac{M}{v(R)n}\equiv \frac{c_0}{n}
\]
We obtained (P1) and (P2) for $n+1$. 

Next we check (P3). By definition 
\begin{align*}
&\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}}_{nL,\beta})
=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}}_{(n+1)L,\beta})\pm KL=z_{(n+1)L,\beta}\pm KL
=z_{nL,\beta}\pm 2KL\\
&=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_{nL,\beta})\pm 2KL.
\end{align*}
Therefore $v(R) n{L}|\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}-\xi_{L,\beta}|<|\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}}_{nL,\beta})-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_{nL,\beta})|<2KL$, whence 
$|\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}-\xi_{L,\beta}|<\frac{2KL}{v(R) nL}<c_0/n$. 

\medskip
\noindent
{\bf Case 2.}  Suppose $\forall\gamma\in [\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_n]$, $\xi_{nL,\gamma}>\xi$. Then $\underline{B}_{n+1}=\underline{B}_{\sqrt{3}}$. 

Fix $\beta\in [0;\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_{n+1}]$.
By Lemma \ref{l.Dima-Trick}(2), 
\begin{align*}
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_{(n+1)L,\beta})&=
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_{L,\beta})+\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_{(n+1)L,\beta}-\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_{nL,\beta})\\
&>z_{nL,\beta}+ [z_{(n+1)L,\beta}-z_{nL,\beta}+C]>z_{(n+1)L,\beta}+C>z_{(n+1)L,\beta}.
\end{align*}
Also,  
 $\displaystyle
z_{(n+1)L,\beta}=z_{nL,\beta}+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{LN_0}[\operatorname{sgn}(6)-\operatorname{sgn}(2)]=z_{nL,\beta}
$, so by the choice of $n_0$,
\begin{align*}
z_{(n+1)L,\beta}&=z_{nL,\beta}=
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_{nL,\beta})>v(R)\xi_{nL,\beta}nL-E>v(R)\xi n_0 L
-E>E>\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{0}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{0}_{nL,\beta}).
\end{align*}
So $\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{0}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{0}_{nL,\beta})<z_{(n+1)L,\beta}
<\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL,\beta}}_{(n+1)L,\beta})
$. Recalling that $\eta\mapsto \widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\eta}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\eta}_{(n+1)L,\beta})$ is continuous and strictly increasing on $[0,R]$, we find that 
$$
\exists!\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}\in (0,\xi_{nL,\beta})\textrm{ s.t. }
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}}_\beta(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}}_{(n+1)L,\beta})=z_{(n+1)L,\beta}.
$$
Since $\xi_{nL,\beta}\in [0,R]$ by the induction hypothesis, 
$\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}\in [0,R]$ and we have established (P1) for $n+1$.

(P3) for $n+1$ can be proved as in Case 1. 

We check (P2). 
In Case 2, $\xi_{nL,\beta}>\xi$, and we saw  above that 
$\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}<\xi_{nL,\beta}$. 
It remains to check that $\xi_{nL,\beta}\in (\xi,\xi+\frac{c_0}{n})\Rightarrow |\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}-\xi|<c_0/n$.

On the one hand, 
$
\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}<\xi_{nL,\beta}<\xi+\frac{c_0}{n}$. On the other hand,  
by (P3) for $n+1$, 
$
\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}=\xi_{nL,\beta}-|\xi_{nL,\beta}-\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}|
>\xi-\frac{c_0}{n}
$. 
So  $|\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}-\xi|<\frac{c_0}{n}$ as required. 

\noindent
This completes the inductive construction of $\underline{B}_i$. Set $(b_1,b_2,\ldots):=(\underline{B}_1,\underline{B}_2,\ldots)$.
<!-- end proof-83 -->
<!-- proof-84: body_md -->
Let $\underline{B}_i$ be the sequence of blocks constructed in the previous proof, and set
$
\beta:=[0;\underline{B}_1,\underline{B}_2,\ldots].
$

We claim that $\underline{B}_i$ is not  equal to $\underline{B}_{\sqrt{2}}$ for all $i$ large enough. Otherwise, $\underline{B}_{n}=(-6,6,\ldots,-6,6)$ for all $n>n_1$. Fix $C>|z_{n_1,\beta}|+Kn_1$, then by Lemma \ref{l.Dima-Trick}(1), for all $n$ large enough, for all $\eta\leq R$, 
$$
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\eta_\beta(\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^\eta)<z_{n,\beta}-z_{n_1,\beta}-C+Kn_1<z_{n,\beta}.
$$  
Necessarily, $\xi_{nL,\beta}>R$ for all $n$ large enough, in contradiction to (P1). 

Similarly, $\underline{B}_i$ is not  equal to $\underline{B}_{\sqrt{3}}$ for all $i$ large enough.  Otherwise, $\underline{B}_{n}=(2,6,\ldots,2,6)$ for all $n>n_1$. Fix $C>|z_{n_1,\beta}|+Kn_1$ and $r>0$ arbitrarily small, then by Lemma \ref{l.Dima-Trick}(2), for all $n$ large enough, for all $r<\eta\leq R$, 
$$
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^\eta_\beta(\widetilde{S}_{n,\beta}^\eta)>z_{n,\beta}-z_{n_1,\beta}+C-Kn_1>z_{n,\beta}.
$$  
Necessarily, $\xi_{nL,\beta}<r$ for all $n$ large enough, and $\xi_{nL,\beta}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0$. But this is impossible, because by (P2), this sequence is increases when its values drop below $\xi$.  


We are now ready to show that $\xi_{nL,\beta}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\xi$.
Consider the following  three cases:

(A)  $\forall\gamma\in [0;\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_n]\cap \Lambda_6$, $\xi_{nL,\gamma}\leq \xi$.   This case cannot happen  for all $n$ large enough, because $\underline{B}_n$ is not eventually constant equal to $\underline{B}_{\sqrt{2}}$.

(B) $\forall\gamma\in [0;\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_n]\cap\Lambda_6$, $\xi_{nL,\gamma}>\xi$. This case cannot happen  for all $n$ large enough, because  $\underline{B}_n$ is not   eventually constant equal to $\underline{B}_{\sqrt{3}}$. 

(C) $\exists\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in [0;\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_n]\cap\Lambda_6$ such that  $\xi_{nL,\gamma_1}<\xi<\xi_{nL,\gamma_2}$. 



Arguing as in Case 1 in the proof of the previous lemma, it is possible to show that in Case (C), if $n>n_0$, then   all the $\xi_{nL,\gamma}$ with $\gamma\in  [0;\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_n]\cap\Lambda_6$ are within  distance $c_0/n$ from each other. In particular $\xi_{nL,\gamma_1}, \xi_{nL,\gamma_2}$ and $\xi_{nL,\beta}$ are all within distance $c_0/n$ from each other. Since $\xi_{nL,\gamma_i}$ are on opposite sides of $\xi$, 
$|\xi_{nL,\gamma_i}-\xi|<c_0/n$, whence also 
$
|\xi_{nL,\beta}-\xi|<c_0/n.$


Similarly, if at time $n$ we are in case (A) and in time $n+1$ we are in case (B) (or the opposite), then $\xi$ is between $\xi_{nL,\beta}$ and $\xi_{(n+1)L,\beta}$, whence  $|\xi_{nL,\beta}-\xi|<c_0/n$ by (P3).



 By the foregoing discussion 
there is an infinite sequence $n_k$ such that
$|\xi_{n_k L,\beta}-\xi|\leq \frac{c_0}{n_k}.$ 
Therefore to complete the proof
it suffices to show that  if for some sufficiently
large ${\overline n}$, 
$|\xi_{{\overline n} L,\beta}-\xi|\leq c_0/{\overline n}$, then 
\begin{equation}
\label{Trap}
|\xi_{n L,\beta}-\xi|\leq c_1/({\overline n}-1)\textrm{ for all $n>{\overline n}$, where $c_1:=2c_0+1$.}
\end{equation}

We prove this by induction. The base $n={\overline n}$ holds by assumption, so we just need to establish the step
of induction. So suppose that the claim holds for $n-1$.

If $\xi_{(n-1)L,\beta}\in (\xi, \xi+\frac{c_0}{n-1})$
 then \eqref{Trap} holds by the third
condition in (P2).

If $\xi-c_0/({\overline n}-1)\leq \xi_{(n-1)L, \beta}<\xi$, then \eqref{Trap} holds 
since
$$\displaystyle \xi-c_0/({\overline n}-1)\leq \xi_{(n-1)L, \beta}\overset{(P2)}{<}\xi_{nL, \beta}\overset{(P3)}{<}\xi_{(n-1)L, \beta}+c_1/(n-1)<\xi+c_0/({\overline n}-1) .$$
The case where
$\xi+\frac{c_0}{n-1}<\xi_{(n-1)L,\beta}<\xi+c_1/({\overline n}-1)$ 
can be analyzed similarly. This completes the proof of \eqref{Trap} and finishes the proof of the lemma.
<!-- end proof-84 -->
<!-- head-17: body_md -->
Let $\beta:=[0;\underline{B}_1,\underline{B}_2,\ldots]$ as above. Henceforth we work with this $\beta$ only, and drop the subscripts $\beta$. 

Let  ${\widetilde{\omega}}_0$ be the midpoint of the top of rectangle ${\mathsf{R}}_0$.  
Note that $z_{NN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)=z_{N,\beta}$ (see \eqref{e.z-n}).
We saw above that there exist $\xi_{nL}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\xi$ such that $\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_{nL}}(\widetilde{S}^{\xi_{nL}}_{nL})=z_{nL,\beta}$. 
 For integers $N\in [nL,(n+1)L)$, let  $\eta_N:=\xi_{nL}$ and $z_{N,\beta}:=z_{NN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0)$.  Then it is easy to see using the uniform boundedness of the jump functions that 
$$
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\eta_{N}}(\widetilde{S}^{\eta_{N}}_{N})=z_{N,\beta}+O(1)\textrm{ for all }N.
$$  
By Lemma \ref{l.14.3}, 
$
\mathsf{P}_N'(\eta_N)=z_{N,\beta}+O(1), \textrm{ and }\eta_N\to\xi. 
$
By Lemma \ref{l.solution-xi}, there are $\eta_N'\to\xi$ such that 
$
\mathsf{P}_N'(\eta_N')=z_{NN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}}_0).
$
Looking at the proof of Proposition \ref{PrBulk}, we see that ${\widetilde{\omega}}_0$ must be  $\mu_\xi$-generic for the linear flow with velocity ${\beta\choose 1}$. \hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-17 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
\label{RemZeroNG}
\normalfont
A slight modification of the construction   allows to build an irrational of bounded type $\alpha$, for which $D_N(\alpha)$  is not $\rho$-equidistributed for any $\rho$. To do so fix two thresholds ${\widehat\xi}_1$ and ${\widehat\xi}_2$ so that ${\widehat\xi}_1<{\widehat\xi}_2$, and build  a sequence of blocks equal to $\underline{B}_{\sqrt{2}}$ or $B_{\sqrt{3}}$ as follows. We start with
block $\underline{B}_{\sqrt{3}}$. Then  we will keep adding blocks $\underline{B}_{\sqrt{2}}$
until the time $k_1$ when $\xi_{k_1L,\gamma}>{\widehat\xi}_2$ for all $\gamma\in [\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_{k_1}]$. Then we  keep adding  blocks $\underline{B}_{\sqrt{3}}$ until the time $k_2$ when $\xi_{k_2 L,\gamma}<{\widehat\xi}_1$ for all $\gamma\in [\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_{k_2}]$. Then we switch back again to blocks $\underline{B}_{\sqrt{2}}$ until $\xi_{k_3 L,\gamma}>{\widehat\xi}_2$ for all $\gamma\in [\underline{B}_1,\ldots,\underline{B}_{k_1}]$, and so on. 
A modification of the  proof of Theorem \ref{t.exp-tilted-exist} shows if  $\beta$ has even CFE $[0;\underline{B}_1,\underline{B}_2,\cdots]$, then ${\widetilde{\omega}}_0$  has a historical measure $\mu_\xi$ for $\phi_\beta$,   for every $\xi\in [{\widehat\xi}_1, {\widehat\xi}_2].$ It follows that $D_N(\alpha)$ is not $\rho$-equidistributed for any $\rho$.
We leave the details to the reader.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- lem-57: body_md -->
\label{LmHDUpper} 
For some $c_1>0$, for all ${\overline \xi}>0$ sufficiently close to zero, for every  $E^u_0$-segment $W$,
$\displaystyle {\mathrm{HD}}(S_{\overline \xi}\cap W)\leq 1-c_1 {\overline \xi}^2. $
<!-- end lem-57 -->
<!-- proof-85: body_md -->
It is sufficient to prove the lemma for  pure $E^u_0$-segments with depth zero and height zero (in particular 
 $\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0\!\!\equiv\!\! 0$ on $W$, and $\pi(W)$ is a maximal $u$-fibre in some $\<\dot{a}_0\>\!\!\in\! \mathfrak P_0$). 
Fix some constant $C$ such that for all $n\!\!\geq\!\! 0$ and for all $\eta\!\!\in\!\! [0,R]$,
$\sup|\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n-{\mathfrak{z}}|\!\!<\!\!C$ and 
$\left|\mathsf{P}_n'(\eta)-\left.\frac{d}{d\xi}\right|_{\xi=\eta}\log\mathbb E(e^{\xi S_n})\right|<C
$, 
see Lemmas \ref{Lemma-Modified-Approx-Canonical} and \ref{LmPressure}.

By Theorem \ref{t.historical-crit} and  
Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure},  if ${\widetilde{\omega}}\in S_{{\overline \xi}}\cap W$, then for some  $n_k\uparrow\infty$, there are   $\eta_{n_k}\to{\overline \xi}$ such that  $\mathsf{P}_{n_k}'(\eta_{n_k})=z_{n_kN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})$.
 
 Since ${\overline \xi}>0$ and $\mathsf{P}_n$ are strictly convex with second derivative bounded below by $\operatorname{const} n$ on $[{\overline \xi}/2,{\overline \xi}]$, there exists $k_0$ such that  for  all $k\geq k_0$,  $z_{n_kN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})=\mathsf{P}_{n_k}'({\overline \xi})>\mathsf{P}_{n_k}'({\overline \xi}/2)+10C$, 
whence $\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{n_k}({\widetilde{\omega}})-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0({\widetilde{\omega}})\geq \mathsf{P}_{n_k}'({\overline \xi}/2)+8C$. By the definition of the jump functions, 
$
\displaystyle \overline{S}_{n_k}({\widetilde{\omega}})\equiv\sum_{j=1}^{n_k} f_{j}\big(X^{(0)}_j(\pi({\widetilde{\omega}}))\big)=\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_{n_k}({\widetilde{\omega}})-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0({\widetilde{\omega}})\geq \mathsf{P}_{n_k}'({\overline \xi}/2)+8C.
$
Thus, $$\displaystyle S_{\overline \xi}\subset\bigcap_{n_0} \bigcup_{n\geq n_0} K_n,\textrm{ where }
K_n:=\{{\widetilde{\omega}}\in W: \overline{S}_n({\widetilde{\omega}})>\mathsf{P}_{n}'({\overline \xi}/2)+8C\}.
$$

Each $K_n$ is a union of non-overlapping $E^s_0$-segments $I_{j,n}$, which project isometrically to  maximal unstable segments in cylinders of the form 
$
A_{j,n}=\<\dot{a}_0^{j,n},\ldots,a_{n}^{j,n}\>
$, $a_0^{j,n}=a_0$. In particular,  $|I_{j,n}|=\ell^u(A_{j,n})\geq\operatorname{const} e^{-\kappa n}$, where $\kappa>0$ comes from a uniform upper bound on the expansion of the automorphisms $\psi_i$ in the unstable direction, and the constant comes from a uniform lower bound on the unstable side of the Markov rectangles in $\mathfrak P_n$ for all $n$. It follows that for all $j,n$, and $0<s<1$,
$$
|I_{j,n}|^{1-s}\leq \operatorname{const} |I_{j,n}|e^{\kappa n s}. 
$$

By construction, $S_{{\overline \xi}}$ is covered by $\{I_{j,n}\}$, and 
\begin{align*}
&\sum_{j,n}|I_{j,n}|^{1-s}\leq  \operatorname{const}\sum_n e^{\kappa n s}\sum_j |I_{j,n}|\leq
\operatorname{const}\sum_n  e^{\kappa n s} {\mathbb{P}}_W[\overline{S}_n({\widetilde{\omega}})>\mathsf{P}_n'({\overline \xi}/2)+8C]  \\
&\leq
\operatorname{const}\sum_n  e^{\kappa n s} {\mathbb{P}}_W\biggl[\overline{S}_n({\widetilde{\omega}})>\frac{d}{d\xi}\bigg|_{\xi={\overline \xi}/2}\log\mathbb E(e^{\xi S_n})+7C\biggr]  \\
&\equiv \operatorname{const} \sum_n e^{ n \kappa s} {\mathbb{P}} \biggl[{S}_n>\frac{d}{d\xi}
\bigg|_{\xi={\overline \xi}/2}\log\mathbb E(e^{\xi S_n})+7C\bigg| X_0=a_0\biggr]\\
&\leq \operatorname{const} \sum_n e^{ n \kappa s} {\mathbb{P}} \biggl[{S}_n>\frac{d}{d\xi}\bigg|_{\xi={\overline \xi}/2}\log\mathbb E(e^{\xi S_n})+7C\biggr],\textrm{because $a_0$ is constant}\\
&\leq \operatorname{const} \sum_n e^{ n \kappa s} {\mathbb{P}}\left[S_n>V_n\mathcal F_n'({\overline \xi}/2)\right],
\textrm{ where }\mathcal F_n(\eta):=\frac{1}{V_n}\log \mathbb E(e^{\eta S_n}).
\end{align*}
Let $\mathcal{I}_n$ denote  the {\em rate functions,}\index{Rate functions} equal by definition to the   Legendre transforms of $\mathcal F_n$. By the bounds on $\mathcal{I}_n$ in  Proposition \ref{PrRateFn}, and  Chernoff's bounds,
 there is a positive constant $c_1$ such that for all  ${\overline \xi}\in [-R,R]$, 
${\mathbb{P}}[S_n>V_n\mathcal F_n'({\overline \xi}/2)]=O(e^{-c_1 n{\overline \xi}^2+o(n)}).
$
So
$\displaystyle    \sum_{j,n} |I_{j,n}|^{1-s}\!\!\leq\!\! \operatorname{const}\sum_n e^{n(\kappa s-c_1 {\overline \xi}^2)+o(n)}<\infty$ for  $\displaystyle s\!\!<\!\!\frac{c_1 {\overline \xi}^2}{\kappa}.$ Thus 
 $\mathrm{HD}(S_{{\overline \xi}})\leq 1-c_1\kappa^{-1}{\overline \xi}^2$.
<!-- end proof-85 -->
<!-- lem-58: body_md -->
\label{l.delta-pressure-is-uni-conv}
For every $R>0$ there are constants $\mathsf{C},n_0>0$ such that for all $k,n>n_0$ and $|\xi|\leq R$, 
$\mathsf C^{-1} n\leq \mathrm{Var}(\widetilde{S}_{k+n}^\xi-\widetilde{S}_k^\xi)\leq \mathsf C n$ and 
 $\mathsf{C}^{-1}n\leq \mathsf{P}''_{k+n}(\xi)-\mathsf{P}''_{k}(\xi)\leq \mathsf{C}n$.
<!-- end lem-58 -->
<!-- proof-86: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{l.uniform-Doeblin}, the Markov chains $\{\widetilde{X}_i^\xi\}_{i\geq k}$ are  uniformly elliptic with the same ellipticity constant for all $|\xi|\leq R$. 
By Theorem \ref{LmVarCycles}, 
there are  constants $C_1,C_2>0$  such that for all $k,n\geq n_0$, and for every $|\xi|\leq R$,  
$$
C_1 \sum_{j=k+3}^k u_j^2(\xi)-C_1< \mathrm{Var}(\widetilde{S}_{k+n}^\xi-\widetilde{S}_k^\xi)<C_1 \sum_{j=k+3}^k u_j^2(\xi)+C_2,
$$
where $u_j(\xi)$ are the structure constants of $\{\widetilde{X}_i^\xi\}_{i\geq 1}$. 

For $|\xi|\leq R$, the hexagon measures of  $\{\widetilde{X}_i^\xi\}_{i\geq 1}$ and the hexagon measures of $\{{X}_i\}_{i\geq 1}$ are related by Radon-Nikodym derivatives uniformly bounded away from zero and infinity by constants independent of $j$ and $\xi$. Therefore $u_j^2(\xi)\asymp u_j^2$, where $u_j$ are the structure constants of $\{X_n\}_{n\geq 1}$, and  by Claim 2 on page \pageref{page-hexagon-claim}, $\sum_{j=k+3}^{k+n} u_j^2(\xi)\asymp n$ uniformly in $k$ and $\xi\in [-R,R]$. Necessarily, 
$$
\exists c_1,n_1\textrm{ s.t. }\forall k,n\geq n_1 \forall|\xi|\leq R,\  c_1^{-1} n\leq \mathrm{Var}(\widetilde{S}_{k+n}^\xi-\widetilde{S}_k^\xi)\leq c_1 n.
$$


Now we appeal to Lemma 7.17 in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book} and its proof. Fixing $k$, and applying Equation (7.21) in the proof of this lemma to the truncated chain $\{{X}_i\}_{i\geq k}$, we see that 
\begin{equation}\label{e.big-Ohs}
\mathsf{P}_{k+n}''(\xi)-\mathsf{P}_k''(\xi)=\mathrm{Var}(\widetilde{S}_{k+n}^\xi-\widetilde{S}_k^\xi)
+O(1)\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(\widetilde{S}_{k+n}^\xi-\widetilde{S}_k^\xi)}+O(1), 
\end{equation}
where the big-Ohs are uniform in $n$ and $\xi\in [-R,R]$. Combining this with the estimates for $\mathrm{Var}(\widetilde{S}_{k+n}^\xi-\widetilde{S}_k^\xi)$ above, we obtain that for all $k>n_1$, for some $n_2(k)$ and $\mathsf C(k)$, 
$$
\forall n\geq n_2(k) \forall \xi\in[-R,R],\  \mathsf C(k)^{-1} n\leq \mathsf{P}_{k+n}''(\xi)-\mathsf{P}_k''(\xi)\leq \mathsf C(k)n
$$

It remains to show that $\mathsf C(k)$ can be replaced by constants independent of $k$. It is sufficient to verify that the big-Ohs in \eqref{e.big-Ohs} are uniform in $k$. 
A close look at the proof of Lemma 7.17 in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book} shows that  the big Ohs depend only on the $L^\infty$ norms of   
$$
\varepsilon_{k,n}(x,y,\xi):=\frac{h_k(x,\xi)}{h_{k+n}(y,\xi)}\frac{d}{d\xi}\left(\frac{h_{k+n}(y,\xi)}{h_k(x,\xi)}\right)\textrm{ and }\frac{d}{d\xi}\varepsilon_{k,n}(x,y).
$$
By Lemmas 7.14 and 7.16 in \cite{Dolgopyat-Sarig-Book},  $h_j(x,\xi), 1/h_j(x,\xi), \partial_\xi h_j(x,\xi)$ and $\partial_\xi^2 h_j(x,\xi)$ are uniformly bounded by constants independent of $j$ and $\xi$, provided $|\xi|\leq R$. Thus $\varepsilon_{k,n}$ and $\partial_\xi\varepsilon_{k,n}$ are uniformly bounded, and $\mathsf C(k)$ can be taken independent of $k$.
<!-- end proof-86 -->
<!-- lem-59: body_md -->
\label{l.LLT-LD-Blocks}
There exists $c>0$ such that the following holds. Suppose  $0<|\xi|<1$ and $z_n=z_n(\xi):=\lfloor\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)\rfloor$. Then for all sufficiently large integers $L$,
$$
{\mathbb{P}}\left(S_{n+L}-S_n=z_{n+L}-z_{n}\, \big|\, X_n=x_n\right)>e^{-c\xi^2 L} \textrm{ for all $n\in\mathbb N$ and  $x_n\in\mathfrak P_n$}. 
$$
<!-- end lem-59 -->
<!-- proof-87: body_md -->
Assume by way of contradiction that the lemma is false. Then there are  $c_i\to\infty$, $0<|\xi_i|<1$,  $L_i\uparrow\infty$,  $n_i\in\mathbb N$,  and $x_{n_i}\in\mathfrak P_{n_i}$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{e.ass-by-cont}
{\mathbb{P}}\left(S_{n_i+L_i}-S_{n_i}=z_{n_i+L_i}(\xi_i)-z_{n_i}(\xi_i)\, \big|\, X_{n_i}=x_{n_i}\right)<e^{-c_i \xi_i^2 L_i}. 
\end{equation}

Let $\widehat{S}_i:=S_{n_i+L_i}-S_{n_i}$, $\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i(t)=\mathsf{P}_{n_i+L_i}(t)-\mathsf{P}_{n_i}(t)$, and $\widehat{z}_i:=z_{n_i+L_i}(\xi_i)-z_{n_i}(\xi_i)$. 
Let $\widetilde{X}_n^\xi$ denote the change of measure built in \S\ref{ss.change-of-measure}, and let 
$\displaystyle \widehat{S}_i^\xi:=\sum_{j=n_i+1}^{n_i+L_i}f_i(\widetilde{X}_i^\xi)$. 


\medskip
\noindent
{\em Step 1.\/} Uniform  estimates of the expectation and variance of $\widehat{S}_i^{\xi_i}$, given $\widetilde{X}_{n_i}^{\xi_i}=x_{n_i}$.

\medskip

By Lemma \ref{l.uniform-Doeblin}, $\widetilde{X}^\xi_n$ are uniformly elliptic with the same ellipticity constant for all $|\xi|<1$. An exponential mixing argument based on Corollary \ref{Cor-phi-mixing} shows that
\begin{align}
&\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}(\widehat{S}_i^{\xi_i}|\widetilde{X}_{n_i}^{\xi_i}=x_{n_i})=\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_i}(\widehat{S}_i^{\xi_i})+O(1)=
\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_i}(\widetilde{S}_{n_i+L}^{\xi_i})-\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi}(\widetilde{S}_{n_i}^{\xi_i})+O(1)\\
&=\mathsf{P}_{n_i+L_i}'(\xi_i)-\mathsf{P}_{n_i}'(\xi_i)+O(1),\textrm{ see \eqref{Pres1stDer}. Thus,  } \notag\\
&\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_i}(\widehat{S}_i^{\xi_i}|\widetilde{X}_{n_i}^{\xi_i}=x_{n_i})=\widehat{z}_i+O(1).\label{e.com-works}
\end{align}

Conditioning on the first state does not affect the ellipticity constant, therefore the  Markov chains $(\widetilde{X}_n^\eta)_{n\geq n_i}$ conditioned on $\widetilde{X}_{n_i}^{\eta}=x_{n_i}$ are also all uniformly elliptic with the same ellipticity constant ${\varepsilon}_0$ . By Theorem \ref{LmVarCycles},  there are constants $C_1, C_2$ such that for all $|\eta|\leq 1$ and $i\geq 1$, 
$$
 C_1^{-1}\sum_{j=n_i+3}^{n_i+L_i} u_n^2(\eta)-C_2\leq {\rm Var}(\widehat{S}^\eta_i|\widetilde{X}_{n_i}^{\eta}=x_{n_i})\leq C_1\sum_{j=n_i+3}^{n_i+L_i} u_n^2(\eta)+C_2,
$$
where $u_n(\eta)$ are the structure constants of $(\widetilde{X}_n^\eta)_{n\geq 1}$, see \eqref{e.u}. It is easy to see that the hexagon measures of  
$(\widetilde{X}_n^\eta)_{n\geq 1}$ differ from those of $({X}_n)_{n\geq 1}$ by densities which are uniformly bounded away from zero and infinity. 
Hence $u_n(\eta)\asymp u_n$, where $u_n=u_n(0)$ are the structure constants of $(X_n)_{n\geq 1}$. Looking at Theorem \ref{Theorem-D_N-Growth}, and specializing to $\eta=\xi_i$, we deduce that there is a constant $C_3$ such that for all  $i\geq 1$, 
\begin{equation}\label{e.var-xi-block-cond}
C_3^{-1} L_i\leq {\rm Var}(\widehat{S}_i^{\xi_i}|\widetilde{X}_{n_i}^{\xi_i}=x_{n_i})\leq C_3 L_i. 
\end{equation}


\medskip
\noindent
{\em Step 2.\/} Uniform estimates for $\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i'(0)$ and $\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i''(\eta)$, $|\eta|\leq 1$.

         
                                                                                                                                                                                           
   
                                                                                                                                       
   
                                                                                                                                                                     
 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
 
               
                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                   
                                
                                                                         
                                                               
             
                                                                                                                                                                  

$L_i\to\infty$, so by Lemma \ref{l.delta-pressure-is-uni-conv}, there exists  $C_5>0$ such that  for all $i$  large enough, 
$$
C_5^{-1} L_i\leq \widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i''(\cdot)\leq C_5 L_i\textrm{ on }[-1,1].
$$
Next by   \eqref{Pres1stDer},  $\mathsf{P}_i'(0)=\mathsf{P}_{n_i+L_i}'(0)-\mathsf{P}_{n_i}'(0)=\mathbb E(S_{n_i+L_i})-\mathbb E(S_{n_i})$, so by Proposition \ref{Prop-Drift}, 
\begin{equation}\label{e.P-i-O(1)}
\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i'(0)=O(1). 
\end{equation} 

 

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Step 3.\/} Uniform estimate of $\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i(\xi_i)-\xi_i\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i'(\xi_i)$. 

\medskip
Let $\varphi_i(\eta):=\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i(\eta)-\eta\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i'(\eta)$, then $\varphi_i'(\eta)=-\eta\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i''(\eta)$, and 
$\varphi_i(0)=0$, see \eqref{Pres0thDer}. Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
\varphi_i(\xi_i)&=\int_0^{\xi_i} \varphi_i'(\eta)d\eta\geq -C_5L_i\int_0^{\xi_i}\eta d\eta=-\frac{1}{2}C_5 L_i{\xi_i}^2. 
\end{align*}
It follows that for some {\em positive} constant $C_6$ (which depends on $\xi$), for all $i$ large enough, 
\begin{equation}\label{e.Legendre-Block-estimate}
\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i(\xi)-\xi\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i'(\xi)\geq -C_6 L_i\xi_i^2. 
\end{equation}

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Step 4.\/} Estimate of ${\mathbb{P}}[\widehat{S}_i=\widehat{z}_i|X_{n_i}=x_{n_i}]$.

\medskip
Recall that $C_4^{-1}\leq h_k(\cdot,\xi)\leq C_4$ for all $k$. Therefore, 
\begin{align}
&{\mathbb{P}}[\widehat{S}_i=\widehat{z}_i|X_{n_i}=x_{n_i}]\geq C_4^{-2}e^{\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i(\xi_i)-\xi_i\widehat{z}_i}\mathbb E\left(1_{[\widehat{S}_i=\widehat{z}_i]}\cdot e^{\xi_i\widehat{S}_i}\frac{h(X_{n_i+L_i},\xi_i)}{e^{\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i(\xi_i)} h_{n_i}(X_{n_i},\xi_i)}\, \bigg|\, X_{n_i}=x_{n_i}\right)\notag\\
&\equiv C_4^{-2} e^{\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i(\xi_i)-\xi(\lfloor{\mathsf{P}}_{n_i+L_i}'(\xi_i)\rfloor-\lfloor{\mathsf{P}}_{n_i}'(\xi_i)\rfloor)}\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_i}(1_{[\widehat{S}_i^{\xi_i}=\widehat{z}_i]}
|\widetilde{X}^{\xi_i}_{n_i}=x_{n_i})\ \ (\widetilde{X}^{\xi_i}_{n_i}=x_{n_i}\Leftrightarrow X_{n_i}=x_{n_i})\notag\\
&\geq C_4^{-2}e^{-2} e^{\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_i(\xi_i)-\xi_i\widehat{\mathsf{P}}_{i}'(\xi_i)}\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_i}(1_{[\widehat{S}_i^{\xi_i}=\widehat{z}_i]}
|\widetilde{X}^{\xi_i}_{n_i}=x_{n_i})\notag\\
&\geq C_7 e^{-C_6 L_i\xi_i^2}{\mathbb{P}}[\widehat{S}_i^\xi=\widehat{z}_i|\widetilde{X}^\xi_{n_i}=x_{n_i}],\textrm{ where $C_7:=C_4^{-2} e^{-2}$, see  \eqref{e.Legendre-Block-estimate}}\label{e.scottish}
\end{align}
Note that $C_7$ is independent of $i$.

To estimate ${\mathbb{P}}[\widehat{S}_i^{\xi_i}=\widehat{z}_i|\widetilde{X}^{\xi_i}_{n_i}=x_{n_i}]$, we consider the Markov array
$$
\begin{array}{cccclll}
  \widetilde{X}^{\xi_1}_{n_1+1} & \cdots &  \widetilde{X}^{\xi_1}_{n_1+L_1} &                     & &\textrm{conditioned on }\widetilde{X}^{\xi_1}_{n_1}=x_{n_1}&\\
  \widetilde{X}^{\xi_2}_{n_2+1} & \cdots &       \cdots          & \widetilde{X}^{\xi_2}_{n_2+L_2} & &\textrm{conditioned on }\widetilde{X}^{\xi_2}_{n_2}=x_{n_2}&\\
  \widetilde{X}^{\xi_3}_{n_3+1} & \cdots &       \cdots          & \cdots               &  \widetilde{X}^{\xi_3}_{n_2+L_3} & \textrm{conditioned on }\widetilde{X}^{\xi_3}_{n_3}=x_{n_3}  & \\
        \vdots       &        &                       &                      &                 & \ddots&\\                 
\end{array}
$$
together with additive functional generated by the jump functions $f_k(\widetilde{X}_k^{\xi_i})$. The rows have lengths $L_i\uparrow\infty$, and  the row sum are equal in distribution to $\widehat{S}_i^{\xi_i}$, conditioned on $\widehat{X}^{\xi_i}_{n_i}=x_{n_i}$. Moreover,

(1)  This array is uniformly elliptic, because $(\widetilde{X}^\eta_n)_{n\geq 1}$ is uniformly elliptic with the same ellipticity constant for all $|\eta|\leq 1$ (Lemma \ref{l.uniform-Doeblin}). 

(2) The variance of the row sums tends to infinity by  \eqref{e.var-xi-block-cond} and since  $L_i\to\infty$.

(3) Our additive functional is  hereditary\index{Hereditary property} in the sense of  Definition \ref{d.hereditary} in Appendix~\ref{AppMC}, by    Claim 2 on page \pageref{page-hexagon-claim} 
and Lemma \ref{Lemma-D_N-Growth}.

(4)  Irreducibility: The previous argument also shows that the co-range of our array is ${2\pi}\mathbb Z$. By Theorem \ref{t.co-range},  the essential range is $\mathbb Z$. Since the jump functions are integer-valued, this is also the algebraic range, and we obtain irreducibility. 

(5) Finally, and crucially,  
by  \eqref{e.com-works} and \eqref{e.var-xi-block-cond}, 
 $$
 \frac{\widetilde{\mathbb E}^{\xi_i}(\widehat{S}_i^{\xi_i}|\widetilde{X}^{\xi_i}_{n_i}=x_{n_i})-\widehat{z}_i}{{\sqrt{{\rm Var}(\widehat{S}_i^\xi|\widetilde{X}^{\xi_i}_{n_i}=x_{n_i})}}}
 =O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{L_i}}\right)\xrightarrow[i\to\infty]{}0.
 $$
By the local limit theorem for arrays, Theorem \ref{ThLLTArrays}, $${\mathbb{P}}[\widehat{S}_i^\xi=\widehat{z}_i|\widetilde{X}^\xi_{n_i}=x_{n_i}]\sim 1/\sqrt{2\pi{\rm Var}(\widehat{S}_i^\xi|\widetilde{X}_{n_i}^\xi=x_{n_i})}.$$ By  \eqref{e.var-xi-block-cond}, there is a constant $C_8$ such that for all $i$ large enough, 
$$
{\mathbb{P}}[\widehat{S}_i^\xi=\widehat{z}_i|\widetilde{X}^\xi_{n_i}=x_{n_i}]\geq \frac{C_8}{\sqrt{L_i}}. 
$$
Plugging this into \eqref{e.scottish}, we obtain that there is a positive constant $C_9$ such that  for all $i$ large enough, 
$$
{\mathbb{P}}[\widehat{S}_i=\widehat{z}_i|X_{n_i}=x_{n_i}]\geq \frac{C_7 C_8 e^{-C_6 L_i\xi_i^2}}{\sqrt{L_i}}>e^{-C_9 L_i \xi_i^2}.
$$
But this contradicts \eqref{e.ass-by-cont}, because $c_i\to\infty$.
<!-- end proof-87 -->
<!-- lem-60: body_md -->
\label{LmHDLower}
For some $c_2>0$, for all $|\xi|\leq 1$, for every $E^u_0$-segment $W$, 
$\displaystyle {\mathrm{HD}}(\mathsf{Gen}(\xi)\cap W)\geq 1-c_3 \xi^2. $
<!-- end lem-60 -->
<!-- proof-88: body_md -->
It is sufficient to consider $W$ such that $\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0\equiv 0$ on $W$, and so that $\pi(W)$ is a maximal $E^u_0$-segment in some cylinder $\<\dot{a}_0,\ldots,a_k\>$. For simplicity, we take $k=0$ (the modifications needed for the general case are routine). Let 
$$
\overline{S}_n(\widetilde{\omega}):=\sum_{j=1}^n f_j\big(X^{(0)}_k(\pi(\widetilde{\omega}))\bigr)=\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_n\bigl((\widetilde{\psi}_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ\widetilde{\psi}_0)(\widetilde{\omega})\bigr)-\widetilde{{\mathfrak{z}}}_0(\widetilde{\omega}).
$$
By  Lemma \ref{Lemma-Modified-Approx-Canonical}, 
$z_{nN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})=\overline{S}_n(\widetilde{\omega})+O(1)\textrm{ on }W.$



Fix $|\xi|\leq 1$, let $z_n=\lfloor\mathsf{P}_n'(\xi)\rfloor$, and let  $L\!\!=\!\!L(\xi)$ be a constant,  to be specified later.
Let
$$
K_n(\xi):=\{\widetilde{\omega}\in W: \overline{S}_{nL}(\widetilde{\omega})=z_{nL}\}, \ K(\xi):=\bigcap_{n} K_n(\xi).
$$ 
If  ${\widetilde{\omega}}\in K(\xi)$, then $z_{nLN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})=\overline{S}_{nL}({\widetilde{\omega}})+O(1)=\mathsf{P}_{nL}'(\xi)+O(1)$.  By Lemma \ref{l.solution-xi}, $\exists \xi_n'\to\xi$ such that $\mathsf{P}_{nL}'(\xi_n')=z_{nLN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})$. Also, $\mathcal P_{nLN_0}'(\xi_{nLN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}}))=z_{LN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})$, by definition. Looking at  Proposition \ref{p.Pressure-and-Geometric-Pressure}, we deduce that  $\xi_{nLN_0}({\widetilde{\omega}})\to\xi$, and by  Theorem \ref{t.historical-crit}, $\mu_\xi$ is a historic measure for ${\widetilde{\omega}}$. This shows that
$$
S_{{\overline \xi}}\cap W\supset K(\xi)\textrm{ for all }\xi\geq {\overline \xi}.
$$

By Frostman's lemma,\index{Frostman's lemma} \index{Hausdorff dimension} to prove that ${\mathrm{HD}}(K(\xi))>1-s$, it is sufficient to construct  a probability measure $\nu$ on $K(\xi)$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{e.mass-dist}
\exists\delta_0,c_0>0\textrm{ s.t. for all intervals $I$, }|I|<\delta_0\Rightarrow \nu(I)\leq c_0|I|^{1-s}.
\end{equation}
$K_n(\xi)$ is a union of non overlapping linear segments $I_{n,j}$ so that for each $j$, $\pi(I_{n,j})$ is a  maximal $E^u_{0}$-segment in some cylinder $\<\dot{x}_0^{n,j},\ldots,x_{nL}^{n,j}\>$, $x_0^{n,j}=a_0$. It follows that  for all $j,j'$, either $I_{n,j}$ contains the interior of $I_{n+1,j'}$,  or the interiors of $I_{n,j}$ and $I_{n+1,j'}$ are disjoint.  Thus the interiors of $I_{n,j}$ form a semi-algebra $\mathcal S$ of subsets of $W\setminus\{\textrm{endpoints of $I_{n,j}$}\}$.

We define a set function $\nu:\mathcal S\to [0,1]$ as follows. If $n=0$, there is just one interval $I_{0,1}=W$ and we define $\nu(I_{0,1})=1$. Suppose by induction we defined $\nu(I_{n,j})$ for all $j$. Let 
$\{I_{n,j, \ell}\}$ be the enumeration of the $I_{n+1,\ell}$ with interiors inside $I_{n,j}$, then we set 
$$ 
\nu(I_{n,j,\ell}):=\nu(I_{n,j})\times\frac{|I_{n, j, \ell}|}{\sum_t |I_{n, j, t}|}. 
$$
A standard argument shows that  $\nu$ is $\sigma$-additive on $\mathcal S$. By Carath\'eodory's extension theorem, $\nu$   extends to a Borel probability measure on $W$. 

The key to the structure of $\nu$ is the following estimate:

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Step 1.\/}  There is a constant $c>0$ such that for every $\xi$, 
if $L=L(\xi)$ is large enough,  then for some  $n_0>0$ and every $n\geq n_0$, 
$                  
\displaystyle \sum_\ell |I_{n, j, \ell}|\geq |I_{n, j}| e^{-c \xi^2 L} .
$          


\medskip
\noindent
{\em Proof of Step 1.\/} 
Set $\Delta S_{n,L}:=S_{nL}-S_{(n-1)L}, $ $\Delta V_{n,L}:= \mathrm{Var}(\Delta S_{n,L}),$
$\Delta z_{n,L}=z_{nL}-z_{(n-1)L}$,  $\Delta \mathsf{P}_{n,L}=\mathsf{P}_{nL}(\xi)-\mathsf{P}_{(n-1)L} (\xi)$,  $\Delta\mathcal F_{n_i,L_i}(t):=(1/\Delta V_{n_i,L_i})\log\mathbb E(e^{t\Delta S_{n_i,L_i}})$. 

Suppose $\pi(I_{n,j})$ is a maximal $E^u_0$-segment in $\<\dot{x}_0,\ldots,x_{nL}\>$, then 
$\displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^{nL}f_j(x_j)=z_{nL}$, and  each 
 $\pi(I_{n,j,\ell})$ is a maximal $E^u_{0}$-segment in 
some   cylinder  $\<\dot{x}_0,\ldots,x_{(n+1)L}\>$ such that 
$\displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^{(n+1)L}f_j(x_j)=z_{(n+1)L}$. By the Markov property, 
$$
\frac{1}{|I_{n, j}|}\sum_\ell |I_{n, j, \ell}|={\mathbb{P}}[\Delta S_{n,L}=\Delta z_{n,L}|X_{nL}=x_{nL}].
$$
By Lemma \ref{l.LLT-LD-Blocks}, for some $c>0$, and $L=L(\xi)$ large,   for all $n$ sufficiently large, 
\begin{equation}\label{e.snl}
{\mathbb{P}}[\Delta S_{n,L}=\Delta z_{n,L}|X_{nL}=x_{nL}]>\exp[-cL\xi^2].
\end{equation} 
Step 1 follows.
Henceforth we fix $L=L(\xi)$ as in Step 1.

\medskip
There is a cylinder $\<\dot{x}_0,\ldots,x_{(n+1)L}\>$ such that  $|I_{n,j,\ell}|=\ell^u(\<\dot{x}_0,\ldots,x_{(n+1)L}\>)$ and $|I_{n,j}|=
\ell^u(\<\dot{x}_0,\ldots,x_{nL}\>)$. Looking at Lemma \ref{Lemma-Cylinder-Area}, we see that if $L$ is sufficiently large, then  there are constants $\rho =\rho_L$ and ${\varepsilon}>0$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{e.rho-eps}
\displaystyle \rho\leq \frac{|I_{n,j,\ell}|}{|I_{n,j}|}\leq e^{-{\varepsilon} L}.
\end{equation}



\medskip
\noindent
{\em Step 2.\/} For some constant $C_0>0$, for every $n\geq n_0$,  $I_{n,j}\in\mathcal S$, and $s>c\xi^2/{\varepsilon}$, 
$$
\nu(I_{n,j})\leq C_0 |I_{n,j}|^{1-s}.
$$

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Proof of Step 2.\/}  Fix $n_0$ as in Step 1.
Since there are only finitely many intervals $I_{n_0,j}$, there is a constant $C_0$ such that $\nu(I_{n_0,j})\leq C_0 |I_{n_0,j}|^{1-s}$ for all $j$ and $s>c\xi^2/{\varepsilon}$. 
We claim that $\nu(I_{n,j})\leq C_0 |I_{n,j}|^{1-s}$ for all $n\geq n_0$, $j$ and $s>c\xi^2/{\varepsilon}$. 

For $n=n_0$ this follows from the definition of $C_0$. Assume by induction that  the statement holds for $n$. Every $I_{n+1,i}$ equals $I_{n,j,\ell}$ for some $j,\ell$. 
By Step 1 and the definition of $\nu$,
$\displaystyle
\frac{\nu(I_{n,j,\ell})}{\nu(I_{n,j})}\leq \frac{|I_{n,j,\ell}|}{|I_{n,j}|} e^{c\xi^2 L}.
$
If $s\geq c\xi^2/{\varepsilon}$,  then $\displaystyle e^{c\xi^2 L}\leq e^{s{\varepsilon} L}\leq \biggl(\frac{|I_{n,j,\ell}|}{|I_{n,j}|}\biggr)^{-s}$, whence 
$\displaystyle
\frac{\nu(I_{n,j,\ell})}{\nu(I_{n,j})}\leq \frac{|I_{n,j,\ell}|^{1-s}}{|I_{n,j}|^{1-s}}
$, and therefore 
$$
\nu(I_{n+1,i})=\nu(I_{n,j,\ell})\leq \frac{\nu(I_{n,j})}{|I_{n,j}|^{1-s}}\times |I_{n,j,\ell}|^{1-s}\leq C_0|I_{n,j,\ell}|^{1-s}=C_0|I_{n+1,i}|^{1-s}.
$$ 


\medskip
\noindent
{\em Step 3.\/} For some $\delta_0>0$, for every linear segment $I\subset W$, if $|I|<\delta_0$ and $s>c\xi^2/{\varepsilon}$, then $\nu(I)\leq C_0 |I|^{1-s}$.

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Proof of Step 3.\/} First note that $\nu$ is non-atomic, because by Step 2, the measure of a set with diameter $r$ tends to zero as $r\to 0$.  



Let $\delta_0:=\min\limits_{j} |I_{n_0,j}|$, and suppose $|I|<\delta_0$. It is convenient to think of $I$ and $W$ as of intervals. 
Let $J$ be a closed sub-interval of $\overline{I}$ such that both endpoints of $J$ are inside $\overline{K({\varepsilon})}$, and $\overline{I}\cap \overline{K({\varepsilon})}=\overline{J}\cap \overline{K({\varepsilon})}$. 

Let $I_{n_0,j_1},I_{n_0,j_2}$ be the one or two intervals which contain the endpoints of $J$ in their closure.  The gap between $I_{n_0,j_1}$ and $I_{n_0,j_2}$ is less than $|J|$, whence less than $\delta_0$. Necessarily,  the interior of the gap  does not intersect any other $I_{n_0,i}$, and is  disjoint from $K_{n_0}(\xi)$. Thus 
$\overline{J}\cap \overline{K(\xi)}\subset \overline{I_{n_0,j_1}}\cup \overline{I_{n_0,j_2}}$. 

\medskip
\noindent
{\em Case 1:\/} Neither of $\overline{I_{n_0,j_1}}$, $\overline{I_{n_0,j_2}}$ covers $J$. 
In this case, each of $\overline{I_{n_0,j_1}}$, $\overline{I_{n_0,j_2}}$ has an endpoint inside the interior of $J$. 

Let $N\geq n_0$ be the maximal integer for which there exist intervals $I_{N,j_1},I_{N,j_2}$ such that $\overline{J}\cap \overline{I_{N,j_i}}=\overline{J}\cap \overline{I_{n_0,j_i}}$ ($i=1,2$). Clearly,  $I_{N,j_1},I_{N,j_2}$ both contain some endpoint of $J$ in their closures, and at least one of their endpoints is inside the interior of $J$. Also  
$
\overline{J}\cap \overline{K(\xi)}\subset  \overline{I_{N,j_1}}\cup \overline{I_{N,j_2}}.
$
Without loss of generality, $\nu(\overline{J}\cap \overline{I_{N,j_1}})\geq \nu(\overline{J}\cap\overline{I_{N,j_2}})$. Then, 
$
\nu(I)=\nu(\overline{J}\cap \overline{K(\xi)})\leq 2\nu(\overline{J}\cap \overline{I_{N,j_1}}). 
$

Let $N'$ be the maximal integer $N'\geq N$ for which there exists  $I_{N',j}$ such that $\overline{I_{N',j}}$ contains an endpoint of $J$, has an endpoint in the interior of $J$, and 
$
\nu(\overline{J})\leq 2\nu(\overline{J}\cap \overline{I_{N',j}}).
$
